components.name: accordion
components.title: Accordion
components.description: Stacked disclosure sections: each item has a header button that shows or hides its panel.
components.whenToUse:
Use for FAQs, settings groups and long detail pages where readers scan headings first. Prefer `Tabs` when exactly one view is shown at a time and all are peers, and `Collapsible` for a single show/hide region. Built on Base UI: full keyboard support (Enter/Space toggle, focus moves with Tab), `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` wired for you.

Key props (on `Accordion`): `value` / `defaultValue` (array of open item values), `onValueChange`, `multiple` (allow several open at once), `disabled`.
examples:
<Accordion defaultValue={["billing"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="billing">
    <AccordionTrigger>How does billing work?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>Invoices go out on the 1st of each month.</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

components.name: account-setup-progress
components.title: AccountSetupProgress
components.description: An onboarding checklist summary: a labelled progress bar with "2/4" steps and the next step.
components.whenToUse: Use at the top of a dashboard or settings page while setup is incomplete. Prefer `Stepper` when the user moves through the steps in place, and `Progress` alone for non-setup progress.

props.name: stepsDone
props.doc: Steps finished. Clamped to 0…stepsTotal.

props.name: stepsTotal
props.doc: Total steps in the setup.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading above the bar.

props.name: next
props.doc: What to do next, shown under the bar. Pass `null` to hide.

examples: <AccountSetupProgress stepsDone={3} stepsTotal={5} next="Invite your team" />

components.name: activity-feed
components.title: ActivityFeed
components.description: A compact feed of who did what, with avatars and timestamps, for dashboards and detail panes.
components.whenToUse: Use for a short "recent activity" card. Prefer `AuditTrail` for compliance logs with exact timestamps, and `Timeline` for a dated sequence of milestones. Renders as a list for screen readers.

props.name: items
props.doc: Rows, newest first. Omit for sample data.

examples: <ActivityFeed items={[{ id: "1", user: "Maya Chen", action: "paid invoice INV-2041", time: "2m ago" }]} />

components.name: add-card-form
components.title: AddCardForm
components.description: A payment card form: card number, expiry and CVC with the right autofill hints, and a save button.
components.whenToUse:
Use in billing settings or checkout when you collect card details yourself. If you use a hosted payment element (Stripe Elements and similar), render that instead and keep only the layout. Field ids are generated, so several forms can share a page.

Fields are submitted as `cc-number`, `cc-exp` and `cc-csc` in the FormData.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called on submit with the form's FormData. The page does not reload.

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: Text on the submit button.

examples: <AddCardForm onSubmit={(data) => saveCard(Object.fromEntries(data))} />

components.name: admin-stat-strip
components.title: AdminStatStrip
components.description: A row of admin KPIs with label, value and a percentage delta, four up on desktop.
components.whenToUse: Use at the top of an admin or analytics page. Prefer `StatCard` for a single, larger KPI with a sparkline. Marked up as a description list (label → value) so screen readers pair them.

props.name: stats
props.doc: KPIs to show, in order. Omit for sample data.

examples: <AdminStatStrip stats={[{ label: "MRR", value: "$48,200", delta: 8 }, { label: "Churn", value: "2.1%", delta: -3 }]} />

components.name: admin-user-row
components.title: AdminUserRow
components.description: One member row for an admin user list: avatar with presence, name, email, permission level and an actions menu.
components.whenToUse: Stack rows inside a bordered container for a members table. Prefer `DataTable` when you need sorting, selection or many columns. Put a `DropdownMenu` in `actions` for real row actions.

props.name: name
props.doc: Full name; initials are derived for the avatar.

props.name: role
props.doc: Permission level shown as a chip.

props.name: online
props.doc: Presence dot: true for online, false for offline, omit to hide.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Replaces the default "more" button, e.g. with a `DropdownMenu`.

props.name: onActionsClick
props.doc: Called when the default "more" button is pressed. Ignored when `actions` is set.

examples:
<AdminUserRow name="Theo Okafor" email="theo@northwind.com" role="write" online
  actions={<DropdownMenu>…</DropdownMenu>} />

components.name: agent-trace
components.title: AgentTrace
components.description: An AI agent run as a timeline of tool calls and steps.
components.whenToUse: A hairline rail connects the steps; the running step spins, finished steps report their time, and steps with `detail` fold out (arguments, output, errors). Use it to show what an agent did. Prefer `ToolCallCard` for a single call, and `BuildPipeline` for CI stages in a row. Each step announces its status to screen readers; details are disclosure buttons.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Steps in run order.

props.name: title
props.doc: Header label.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Right-aligned summary, e.g. "4 tools · 3.1s · $0.012". Defaults to "done/total steps".

examples:
<AgentTrace
  meta="3 tools · 2.4s"
  steps={[
    { id: "1", name: "search_invoices", status: "done", duration: "0.8s", detail: '{ "customer": "Northwind" }' },
    { id: "2", name: "draft_email", status: "running" },
    { id: "3", name: "send_email", status: "pending" },
  ]}
/>

components.name: ai-composer
components.title: AiComposer
components.description: A chat input for AI apps: multiline prompt, suggestion chips, model picker, attach, and a send button that becomes stop while streaming.
components.whenToUse: Use as the input of a chat or assistant panel. Prefer `PromptInput` for a single-line prompt without the model picker, and `Textarea` for plain forms. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and Enter during IME composition is left alone. Works controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`; it clears itself after `onSubmit`).

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled prompt text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called on every edit and when a suggestion chip is picked.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called on Enter or the send button with the trimmed prompt. Not called when empty or streaming.

props.name: onStop
props.doc: Called by the stop button while `streaming`.

props.name: streaming
props.doc: While true the send button becomes a stop button.

props.name: suggestions
props.doc: Prompt starters shown above the input; picking one fills the input.

props.name: models
props.doc: Models offered in the picker.

props.name: model
props.doc: Controlled model id.

props.name: onAttach
props.doc: Called by the paperclip button. Wire it to a file input or picker.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the text area.

components.name: alert-dialog
components.title: AlertDialog
components.description: A modal confirmation for destructive or irreversible actions; renders a demo trigger and content when given no children.
components.whenToUse:
Use when the user must confirm before something cannot be undone (delete, revoke, cancel plan). Unlike `Dialog`, it cannot be dismissed by clicking outside, and screen readers announce it as an alert dialog. Focus is trapped inside and returns to the trigger on close; Escape cancels. Always give it an `AlertDialogTitle` and `AlertDialogDescription`.

Key props (on `AlertDialog`): `open` / `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange(open)`.
examples:
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete invoice</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Delete invoice INV-2041?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>This cannot be undone.</AlertDialogDescription>
    <AlertDialogActions>
      <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</AlertDialogClose>
      <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="destructive" />} onClick={remove}>Delete</AlertDialogClose>
    </AlertDialogActions>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

components.name: announcement-bar
components.title: AnnouncementBar
components.description: A full-width strip above the site header for one short announcement (launch, sale, maintenance).
components.whenToUse: Use for site-wide news on marketing pages. Prefer `Banner` for in-app notices with tones and an action, and `Callout` for notes inside content. Exposed as a labelled region; the dismiss button only renders when `onDismiss` is given (persist the dismissal yourself).

props.name: children
props.doc: The message; may include a link. Keep it to one line.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Shows a dismiss button and is called when it is pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the region.

examples: setHidden(true)}> Lumen 2.4 is out. See what's new

components.name: api-key-list
components.title: ApiKeyList
components.description: A card listing API keys by name with a masked preview, creation date, and create and rotate actions.
components.whenToUse: Use on a developer settings page. Never pass full secrets: show a masked `preview` and reveal a new key once, in a dialog, after `onCreate`. Prefer `CreateApiKey` or `SecretReveal` for the one-time reveal and `DataTable` for large key inventories with scopes and last-used columns.

props.name: keys
props.doc: Keys to list. Omit for sample data.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the card.

props.name: onCreate
props.doc: Called by "Create key".

props.name: onRotate
props.doc: Called by a row's "Rotate" button with that key.

examples:
<ApiKeyList
  keys={[{ id: "k1", name: "Production", preview: "md_live_••••8f2a", created: "Aug 12" }]}
  onCreate={openCreateDialog}
  onRotate={(key) => rotate(key.id)}
/>

components.name: app-shell
components.title: AppShell
components.description: A product layout frame: optional sidebar on the left (from md up), optional top bar, and a scrolling content area.
components.whenToUse: Use as the outer frame of an app page or an app preview. Prefer `Sidebar` for the navigation itself (pass it as `sidebar`) and `Topbar` for the header. Below md the sidebar is hidden, so also render a mobile menu (for example a `Sheet`) inside `topbar`.

props.name: sidebar
props.doc: Left column content, usually navigation. Hidden below the md breakpoint.

props.name: sidebarLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the sidebar landmark.

props.name: topbar
props.doc: Rendered above the content, full width of the main column.

props.name: children
props.doc: Page content; this area scrolls.

examples:
<AppShell sidebar={<Sidebar />} topbar={<Topbar />} sidebarLabel="Workspace">
  <PageHeader title="Invoices" />
</AppShell>

components.name: approval-card
components.title: ApprovalCard
components.description: A request card with the requester, a summary and approve or reject actions.
components.whenToUse: Use for human-in-the-loop steps: refunds, access requests, an agent asking permission before a tool call. Prefer `AlertDialog` when the decision must block the page. The card is an `article` named by its title, so a stack of requests reads as separate items.

props.name: title
props.doc: What is being requested. Also the card's accessible name.

props.name: requester
props.doc: Who asked; initials are derived for the avatar.

props.name: summary
props.doc: Optional context under the requester line.

props.name: approveLabel
props.doc: Text on the approve button.

props.name: rejectLabel
props.doc: Text on the reject button.

examples:
<ApprovalCard title="Refund $1,240 on INV-2041" requester="Theo Okafor"
  summary="Customer was double charged in October." onApprove={approve} onReject={reject} />

components.name: area-chart
components.title: AreaChart
components.description: A smooth area chart with a hairline grid and gradient wash; strokes stay 1.5px at any size and a highlight can pin one value.
components.whenToUse: Use for a single trend over time in a card or KPI tile (no axes, no tooltip). Prefer `InteractiveAreaChart` for hover tooltips and axes, `LineChart` for several series, and `BarChart` for discrete periods. Screen readers get `label` plus a summary (count, first, last, peak). It fills its container: size it with `className` (default `h-32 w-full`).

props.name: data
props.doc: Series values, left to right. Omit for sample data.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name; a short data summary is appended for screen readers.

props.name: grid
props.doc: Three dashed hairlines at 25/50/75%.

props.name: smooth
props.doc: Monotone curve (never overshoots the data) instead of straight segments.

props.name: highlight
props.doc: Index of a point to mark with a dot and a hairline crosshair.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Stroke and wash colour, from the status tokens.

examples: <AreaChart data={[18, 22, 27, 31, 36, 45, 52]} label="Weekly revenue, $k" tone="success" highlight={6} />

components.name: artifact-preview
components.title: ArtifactPreview
components.description: A framed preview of something an AI produced (a snippet, a chart, a draft) with a title bar, copy and expand actions.
components.whenToUse: Use inside a chat thread to show a generated artifact inline. Prefer `CodeBlock` for code that needs syntax highlighting and line numbers, and `ToolResultPanel` for raw tool output. The copy button only appears with `copyValue`, the expand button only with `onExpand`.

props.name: title
props.doc: File or artifact name in the title bar; also names the region.

props.name: children
props.doc: The rendered preview.

props.name: copyValue
props.doc: Text copied by the copy button (usually the source). Omit to hide the button.

props.name: onExpand
props.doc: Called by the expand button, e.g. to open a full-screen dialog. Omit to hide the button.

examples:
<ArtifactPreview title="pricing-table.tsx" copyValue={source} onExpand={() => setOpen(true)}>
  <PricingTable />
</ArtifactPreview>

components.name: aspect-ratio
components.title: AspectRatio
components.description: A box that keeps a fixed width-to-height ratio, for images, video and embeds.
components.whenToUse: Children should fill it absolutely (`absolute inset-0 size-full object-cover`). Uses the native CSS `aspect-ratio`, so it works in server components and needs no JavaScript.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: Width divided by height: 16 / 9, 4 / 3, 1 for a square.

components.name: assign-picker
components.title: AssignPicker
components.description: A list of teammates to assign something to, with the current assignee highlighted.
components.whenToUse: Use inline in a popover or side panel to pick one owner for a task, ticket or invoice. Prefer `Combobox` when the team is long enough to need search. Follows the WAI-ARIA listbox pattern: one Tab stop, Arrow Up/Down and Home/End move, Enter or Space (or click) selects.

props.name: people
props.doc: People to choose from. Omit for sample data.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selection. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled picker.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial selection for the uncontrolled picker.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen person's id.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the list.

components.name: attachment-chip
components.title: AttachmentChip
components.description: A small chip for one attached file, with an optional remove button.
components.whenToUse: Use in a composer or form to list files the user has attached. Prefer `FileDropzone` for picking and uploading files, and `PromptInputAttachments` for the AI prompt input. The remove button only renders with `onRemove` and is named "Remove <file name>".

props.name: name
props.doc: File name; truncated to fit.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Optional detail after the name, e.g. the file size.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Shows a remove button and is called when it is pressed.

examples: <AttachmentChip name="INV-2041.pdf" meta="240 KB" onRemove={() => remove(file)} />

components.name: audio-player
components.title: AudioPlayer
components.description: A compact, controlled audio row: play/pause button, title, subtitle and a progress bar.
components.whenToUse: It renders no `<audio>` element: you own playback and pass `playing` and `progress`. Use it for podcast lists, voice notes and call recordings. Prefer `AudioRecorder` to capture audio, and `VideoPlayerChrome` for video.

props.name: title
props.doc: Track name. Also used in the button's label ("Play Northwind kickoff").

props.name: playing
props.doc: Whether audio is playing; switches the icon and label.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called by the play/pause button.

props.name: progress
props.doc: Playback position in percent, 0 to 100. Clamped.

components.name: audio-recorder
components.title: AudioRecorder
components.description: A microphone recorder with start, pause and stop, an elapsed timer, live waveform bars, playback with a progress bar and a download button.
components.whenToUse: Use to capture a voice note or memo in the browser (MediaRecorder + Web Audio, no dependencies). Prefer `AudioPlayer` to play existing audio. The finished waveform is a keyboard slider (Arrow keys seek 1s, Shift 5s, Space plays). Without a microphone or permission it stays idle with a plain-language hint. You own upload: take the Blob from `onRecorded`.

props.name: maxDuration
props.doc: Longest recording in seconds. Recording stops by itself when it is reached.

props.name: onRecorded
props.type: (blob: Blob, meta: { duration: number; url: string; mimeType: string }) => void
props.doc: Called with the finished recording and its object URL.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the card.

props.name: description
props.doc: Shown under the title.

props.name: fileName
props.doc: Base name of the downloaded file. The extension follows the recording format.

props.name: bars
props.doc: Number of waveform bars.

examples:
<AudioRecorder maxDuration={60} title="Voice note" description="Attach to INV-2041"
  onRecorded={(blob, { duration }) => upload(blob, duration)} />

components.name: audit-filter-bar
components.title: AuditFilterBar
components.description: A filter toolbar for an audit log: free-text search, an actor chip filter and a date range.
components.whenToUse: Put it above `AuditTrail` or an audit `DataTable`. Prefer `TableToolbar` for generic tables and `FacetFilter` when several filters can be on at once. Every control works uncontrolled; read the values through the `on*Change` callbacks, or control the actor with `actor` + `onActorChange`.

props.name: onSearchChange
props.doc: Called with the search text on every keystroke.

props.name: actorOptions
props.doc: Actor chips. The first is the "everyone" option by convention.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Controlled actor value.

props.name: defaultActor
props.doc: Initial actor when uncontrolled.

props.name: onActorChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen actor's value.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.doc: Called with ISO day strings when either end of the range changes.

examples:
<AuditFilterBar
  onSearchChange={setQuery}
  onActorChange={setActor}
  onRangeChange={(r) => setRange(r)}
/>

components.name: audit-log-entry
components.title: AuditLogEntry
components.description: One line of an audit log: who did what to which record, with a relative timestamp.
components.whenToUse: Use for a single event; stack several in `AuditTrail`. Prefer `ActivityFeed` for casual "recent activity" without exact times. The timestamp is a `<time datetime>` for machines.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Who did it; initials are derived for the avatar.

props.name: action
props.doc: What they did, written to follow the name ("archived invoice").

props.name: target
props.doc: The record acted on, shown emphasised after the action.

props.name: date
props.doc: When it happened. Defaults to about two hours ago.

examples: <AuditLogEntry actor="Maya Chen" action="approved refund on" target="INV-2041" date="2026-11-14T09:12:00Z" />

components.name: audit-trail
components.title: AuditTrail
components.description: A bordered list of audit log entries, newest first, each with a relative timestamp.
components.whenToUse: Use on security and admin pages to show who changed what. Pair it with `AuditFilterBar` above. Prefer `ActivityFeed` for casual activity, and `DataTable` when the log needs paging and sorting.

props.name: entries
props.doc: Entries to show. Omit for a sample trail with times relative to now.

examples: <AuditTrail entries={[{ id: "1", actor: "Maya Chen", action: "approved refund on", target: "INV-2041", time: "2026-11-14T09:12:00Z" }]} />

components.name: auth-card
components.title: AuthCard
components.description: A centred card frame for sign in, sign up and password reset forms: title, description, body and footer.
components.whenToUse: It is layout only; put your `FormField`s and `Button`s inside. Use `footer` for the switch link ("No account? Sign up"). Prefer `Card` for anything that is not an auth screen. The card is a section named by its title.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading (an `h2`) and the section's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Below a divider, centred: usually the sign in / sign up switch.

props.name: children
props.doc: The form fields and buttons.

examples: Create an account}>

components.name: autocomplete
components.title: Autocomplete
components.description: A text field that suggests matching options as you type, with the first eight matches in a listbox.
components.whenToUse: Free text is allowed: the value is whatever is typed, and picking a suggestion fills it in. Use for "type or pick" fields (customer, city, tag). Prefer `Combobox` when the value must be one of the options, and `Select` for a short fixed list. Follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: Arrow Down/Up move through suggestions, Enter picks, Escape closes, focus stays in the input.

props.name: options
props.doc: Suggestions, matched case-insensitively anywhere in the string. Omit for sample data.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the text on every keystroke and when a suggestion is picked.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the wrapper (sets the width; default `w-64`).

props.name: id
props.doc: Input id, for an external `<label htmlFor>`.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label. Falls back to the placeholder.

components.name: avatar-group
components.title: AvatarGroup
components.description: Overlapping avatars for a team, with name tooltips, a "+N" overflow popover and a "Maya, Theo and 7 others" summary.
components.whenToUse: Each avatar is ringed in the surface colour so the stack reads cleanly on cards; hovering or focusing one lifts it above its neighbours without moving the layout. Initials on token-tinted backgrounds stand in for missing photos. Data-driven: pass `people`. Prefer the `AvatarGroup` exported from `avatar` (a plain flex wrapper) when you compose `Avatar` children by hand.

props.name: people
props.doc: Everyone in the group, in display order. Omit for sample data.

props.name: max
props.doc: Avatars shown before the "+N" chip. If only one person would overflow, they are shown instead of "+1".

props.name: size
props.doc: Avatar diameter: sm 24px, md 32px, lg 40px.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the group, also the overflow popover title.

props.name: summary
props.doc: Show a "Maya, Theo and 7 others" line after the stack.

examples:
<AvatarGroup label="Northwind team" max={4} size="sm"
  people={[{ name: "Maya Chen", role: "Head of Finance", src: "/maya.jpg" }, { name: "Theo Okafor" }]} />

components.name: avatar-upload
components.title: AvatarUpload
components.description: A profile photo picker: the current avatar with an Upload button that opens the file chooser and previews the pick.
components.whenToUse: Use in profile and team settings. It previews locally and hands you the `File`; uploading is yours. Prefer `ImageUpload` for larger images with drag and drop, and `FileDropzone` for any file.

props.name: name
props.doc: Person's name, for the image alt text and the initials fallback.

props.name: src
props.doc: Current photo URL, shown until a new file is picked.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the picked image file.

props.name: buttonLabel
props.doc: Text on the button.

examples: <AvatarUpload name="Maya Chen" src={user.avatarUrl} onChange={(file) => uploadAvatar(file)} />

components.name: avatar
components.title: Avatar
components.description: A round user picture with an initials fallback while the image loads or if it fails.
components.whenToUse: Compose `Avatar` > `AvatarImage` + `AvatarFallback`. Add `AvatarBadge` for a status dot, and wrap several in this file's `AvatarGroup` for a simple overlapping stack. Prefer the data-driven `AvatarGroup` from `avatar-group` for tooltips and a "+N" overflow. Give `AvatarImage` an `alt` with the person's name, or `alt=""` when the name is printed next to it.

props.name: size
props.doc: Diameter: sm 24px, default 32px, lg 40px. Override with a `size-*` class for others.

examples:
<Avatar size="lg">
  <AvatarImage src="/maya.jpg" alt="Maya Chen" />
  <AvatarFallback>MC</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>

components.name: back-link
components.title: BackLink
components.description: A quiet "← Back" link to the parent page, placed above a page title.
components.whenToUse: Use on detail pages ("← Invoices"). Prefer `Breadcrumb` when the hierarchy is deeper than one level. It is a real link (`<a href>`), so it works without JavaScript and opens in a new tab; for Next.js client navigation pass `onClick` with `router.push`, or wrap your own `Link`. The arrow nudges left on hover.

props.name: href
props.doc: Parent page URL.

props.name: children
props.doc: Link text; name the destination ("Invoices"), not just "Back".

examples: <BackLink href="/invoices">Invoices</BackLink>

components.name: back-to-top
components.title: BackToTop
components.description: A floating back to top button that appears after the reader scrolls, with a ring that fills as they progress.
components.whenToUse: Use on long docs, articles and changelogs. Fixed bottom-right; move it with `className`. Scrolls smoothly unless reduced motion is on, then moves focus to `<main>` (or the first `<h1>`) so keyboard users land at the top too. While hidden it is out of the tab order.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: Show after this many pixels of scroll.

props.name: target
props.doc: Element to scroll; defaults to the window.

examples:
<BackToTop threshold={600} />
// inside a scrolling panel:
<BackToTop target={panelRef} className="absolute" />

components.name: badge
components.title: Badge
components.description: A small pill label for status, counts and categories ("Paid", "Beta", "3 new").
components.whenToUse:
Use next to text or in table cells. Prefer `StatusBadge` for a status with a dot, `TagsInput` for editable tags, and `Kbd` for keyboard keys. `render={<a href="…" />}` makes it a link (hover styles turn on automatically). Add an icon with `data-icon="inline-start"` on the svg.

Variants: default (ink), accent, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link.
examples:
<Badge variant="accent">Beta</Badge>
<Badge variant="destructive">Overdue</Badge>
<Badge render={<a href="/changelog" />} variant="outline">v2.4</Badge>

components.name: banner
components.title: Banner
components.description: A full-width, tinted notice bar for in-app messages, with an optional action and dismiss button.
components.whenToUse: Use at the top of an app or a page section for state the user should know about (trial ending, degraded service, unpaid invoice). Prefer `AnnouncementBar` for marketing news, `InlineAlert` or `Callout` inside content, and `Toast` for transient feedback. It is a polite live region, so a banner that appears later is announced. `danger` uses `role="alert"` and interrupts.

props.name: children
props.doc: The message. Keep it to one sentence.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Colour and urgency. `danger` is announced assertively.

props.name: action
props.doc: A button or link shown before the dismiss button.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Shows a dismiss button and is called when it is pressed.

examples:
<Banner tone="warning" action={<Button size="sm" variant="outline">Update card</Button>} onDismiss={hide}>
  Your card ending 4242 expires this month.
</Banner>

components.name: bar-chart
components.title: BarChart
components.description: Rounded-top bars on a hairline baseline; hovering one bar dims its siblings and surfaces the value, and the peak is marked by default.
components.whenToUse: Use for one value per period or category (monthly revenue, signups per day). Prefer `StackedBarChart` for parts of a whole, `HorizontalBarChart` for long category names, and `AreaChart` for a continuous trend. Screen readers get `label` followed by every label and value. Size it with `className` (default `h-40 w-full`).

props.name: data
props.doc: One bar per item, left to right. `label` is printed under the bar. Omit for sample data.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name; every label and formatted value is appended for screen readers.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats values in the hover bubble and the accessible summary.

examples:
<BarChart label="Revenue by month" format={(n) => `$${(n / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`}
  data={[{ label: "Sep", value: 56100 }, { label: "Oct", value: 61400 }]} />

components.name: bento-grid
components.title: BentoGrid
components.description: A responsive bento grid: feature tiles of different spans on a six column grid that collapse to one column on phones.
components.whenToUse: Use on landing pages to show four to seven product features. Each tile has an icon, title, copy and an optional `visual`; tiles with `href` become links. Prefer `FeatureGrid` for equal tiles. Server component friendly, no motion, no client JavaScript.

props.name: items
props.doc: Tiles in reading order. Omit for sample data.

examples:
<BentoGrid items={[
  { title: "Real time analytics", description: "Charts update as events arrive.", icon: BarChart3Icon, span: 4, rows: 2 },
  { title: "Instant alerts", description: "Get pinged when a metric crosses a line.", icon: BellIcon, span: 2 },
]} />

components.name: billing-address
components.title: BillingAddress
components.description: Billing address fields (street, city, state, postal code) with browser autofill hints, for checkout and billing settings.
components.whenToUse: Drop it inside your own `<form>`; it renders fields only, no submit button. Field names are `address`, `city`, `state` and `postal-code`, so `new FormData(form)` reads them directly. Ids are generated, so it can appear twice on a page (billing and shipping) with different `section`s.

props.name: section
props.doc: Autofill section, e.g. "billing" or "shipping". Becomes the autocomplete token prefix.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks every field required.

examples:
<form onSubmit={save}>
  <BillingAddress section="billing" />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>

components.name: blog-card
components.title: BlogCard
components.description: A linked article card: cover image, tag, relative date, title and a two-line excerpt.
components.whenToUse: Use in blog indexes, changelogs and "related posts". The whole card is one link, so do not nest other links or buttons inside. Prefer `Card` for non-link content. Without `image` the 16:9 slot shows a sunken placeholder, so grids stay aligned.

props.name: title
props.doc: Post title (an `h3`); also the link's name.

props.name: excerpt
props.doc: Summary, clamped to two lines.

props.name: href
props.doc: Post URL.

props.name: image
props.doc: Cover image URL, cropped to 16:9. Decorative: the title names the link.

props.name: date
props.doc: Publish date, shown as "3d ago" with the exact time for machines.

props.name: tag
props.doc: Category shown above the title.

examples:
<BlogCard href="/blog/close-books-faster" title="Close the books in two days"
  excerpt="How Northwind cut month-end from a week to two days." image="/covers/close.jpg"
  tag="Finance" date="2026-11-02" />

components.name: breadcrumb-ellipsis
components.title: BreadcrumbEllipsis
components.description: A "…" marker for collapsed middle levels in a breadcrumb trail.
components.whenToUse: Decorative by default (hidden from screen readers). To let people open the hidden levels, wrap it in a `DropdownMenuTrigger` and give that trigger `aria-label="Show more pages"`.
examples: <BreadcrumbEllipsis />

components.name: breadcrumb
components.title: Breadcrumb
components.description: A navigation trail of links with chevron separators; the last item is the current page.
components.whenToUse: Use at the top of nested pages (Customers › Northwind › INV-2041). Prefer `BackLink` when there is only one level to go back. Follows the WAI-ARIA breadcrumb pattern: a labelled `nav` with an ordered list, separators hidden from screen readers, and `aria-current="page"` on the last item. Long trails wrap; pass `BreadcrumbEllipsis` yourself if you collapse the middle.

props.name: items
props.doc: Steps from the root to the current page. Omit for sample data.

examples: <Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "Customers", href: "/customers" }, { label: "Northwind", href: "/customers/northwind" }, { label: "INV-2041" }]} />

components.name: build-pipeline
components.title: BuildPipeline
components.description: CI/CD stages in a row (Install → Typecheck → Test → Deploy), each with a status icon.
components.whenToUse: Use on deploy and PR pages for a glanceable pipeline. Prefer `AgentTrace` for a vertical log with details, and `Stepper` for a user-driven multi-step flow. Wraps on narrow screens; each stage announces its status, and the running stage is marked `aria-current="step"`.

props.name: stages
props.doc: Stages in order. Omit for sample data.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the list.

examples:
<BuildPipeline stages={[
  { name: "Install", status: "success" },
  { name: "Test", status: "running" },
  { name: "Deploy", status: "pending" },
]} />

components.name: bulk-actions-bar
components.title: BulkActionsBar
components.description: A floating bar that appears when table rows are selected: "3 selected", your action buttons and Clear.
components.whenToUse: Render it under a selectable `DataTable` or list and pass the selection size as `count`; it renders nothing at 0. Sticky to the bottom of its scroll container. The count is a live region, so changes are announced; the bar itself is a labelled region.

props.name: count
props.doc: Number of selected items. The bar is hidden at 0.

props.name: children
props.doc: Action buttons, usually `Button size="sm"`.

props.name: onClear
props.doc: Shows a Clear button and is called when it is pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the bar.

examples:
<BulkActionsBar count={selected.length} onClear={() => setSelected([])}>
  <Button size="sm" variant="outline">Export</Button>
  <Button size="sm" variant="destructive">Delete</Button>
</BulkActionsBar>

components.name: bulk-user-import
components.title: BulkUserImport
components.description: A CSV import panel for inviting many users: format note, CSV dropzone and an Import button.
components.whenToUse: Use in admin "Members" pages. Parsing and inviting are yours: `onImport` gets the dropped files when the user presses Import. Prefer `FileDropzone` alone for generic uploads.

props.name: onImport
props.doc: Called with the chosen CSV file(s) when Import is pressed.

examples: <BulkUserImport onImport={async (files) => invite(await parseCsv(files[0]))} />

components.name: button-group
components.title: ButtonGroup
components.description: Joins adjacent `Button`s into one segmented control with shared borders (Day | Week | Month, Copy | ▾).
components.whenToUse: Use for a few related actions that belong together. Prefer `SegmentedControl` or `ToggleGroup` when exactly one option is selected. Works best with `variant="outline"` buttons. Give the group an `aria-label` so screen readers announce what the buttons are for.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Lay the buttons out in a row (default) or a column.

examples:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Invoice actions">
  <Button variant="outline">Send</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Download</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Void</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.description: The Hairline keycap: the kit's one button, in eight variants and nine sizes.
components.whenToUse:
Use `default` (ink) for the primary action, `outline` for secondary, `ghost` in toolbars, `destructive` for irreversible actions, `accent` at most once per screen, `link` for inline text actions. For an icon-only button use `IconButton` (it requires `aria-label`). To render a link that looks like a button, pass `render={<a href="/pricing" />}` (or a Next.js `<Link />`); `nativeButton` is set for you. Disable with `disabled`; Base UI keeps it focusable when you also pass `focusableWhenDisabled`.

Solid variants carry an inner top highlight and bottom edge (shadow-ink), outline a 1px key edge (shadow-key). Hover changes one property, press sinks 0.5px, nothing shifts layout.

Sizes: xs 28px, sm 32px, default 36px, lg 44px, xl 48px; icon, icon-xs, icon-sm, icon-lg are square.
examples:
<Button>Save invoice</Button>
<Button variant="outline" size="sm"><DownloadIcon /> Export</Button>
<Button render={<a href="/pricing" />} variant="accent" size="lg">See pricing</Button>

components.name: calendar-agenda
components.title: CalendarAgenda
components.description: A day's events as a simple time and title list, with optional meta under each entry.
components.whenToUse: Use in a sidebar or dashboard card for "Today". Prefer `EventCalendar` for a week or month view with event blocks, and `CalendarMonth` to pick a date. Marked up as a list; times are `<time>`.

props.name: items
props.doc: Events in time order. Omit for sample data.

examples: <CalendarAgenda items={[{ id: "1", time: "09:00", title: "Finance standup", meta: "15 min" }]} />

components.name: calendar-month
components.title: CalendarMonth
components.description: A single month grid for picking a day, with real weekday alignment and full keyboard support.
components.whenToUse: Use inline or inside a `Popover` to pick a date. Prefer `DatePicker` for a form field with a native picker, `DateRangePicker` for from/to, and `EventCalendar` to show events. Selection is controlled: pass `selected` and `onSelect`. Keyboard: one Tab stop; Arrow keys move by day or week, Home/End jump to the first/last day, Enter or Space selects. Each day is announced with its full date, and the selected day is `aria-pressed`.

props.name: month
props.doc: Any date inside the month to show. Defaults to September 2026.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Selected day of the month, 1 to 31.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the day of the month that was picked.

examples:
const [day, setDay] = React.useState<number>()
<CalendarMonth month={new Date(2026, 10, 1)} selected={day} onSelect={setDay} />

components.name: callout
components.title: Callout
components.description: A tinted note inside content: optional title and body, in info, success, warning or danger.
components.whenToUse: Use in docs, forms and settings to point out something the reader should know. Prefer `Banner` for page-level notices, `InlineAlert` for form errors and status with an icon, and `Toast` for transient feedback. It is a static `role="note"`, not a live region.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Tint of the border and background.

props.name: title
props.doc: Bold first line.

examples: <Callout tone="warning" title="Invoices are final">Sent invoices cannot be edited, only voided.</Callout>

components.name: cancel-flow
components.title: CancelFlow
components.description: A two-step subscription cancel flow: ask why (one reason), then confirm.
components.whenToUse: Use in billing settings behind a "Cancel plan" button, or inside a `Dialog`. Prefer `AlertDialog` for a one-step confirmation. Reasons are a labelled radio group, Continue is disabled until one is chosen, and focus moves to each new step's heading.

props.name: planName
props.doc: Plan being cancelled, used in the heading.

props.name: reasons
props.doc: Reasons to choose from.

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Called with the chosen reason when the user confirms.

examples: <CancelFlow planName="Scale" onConfirm={(reason) => cancelSubscription({ reason })} />

components.name: card
components.title: Card
components.description: The basic raised surface: a bordered, rounded panel with optional header, content and footer slots.
components.whenToUse: Compose `Card` > `CardHeader` (`CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction`) + `CardContent` + `CardFooter`. Spacing comes from one `--card-spacing` variable, so `size="sm"` tightens every slot at once. A first child `` bleeds to the edges. Use it for any grouped content; prefer `StatCard` for a single KPI and `BlogCard` for a linked article. Server component friendly.

props.name: size
props.doc: Spacing scale for every slot: default 20px, sm 14px.

examples:
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Northwind</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Customer since 2023</CardDescription>
    <CardAction><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Edit</Button></CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Open balance: $12,400</CardContent>
  <CardFooter><Button size="sm">Send invoice</Button></CardFooter>
</Card>

components.name: carousel
components.title: Carousel
components.description: A horizontal, scroll-snapping row of slides with previous/next buttons.
components.whenToUse: Use for testimonials, product shots or cards that do not fit in one row. Shows about 1.2 slides on phones, 2 on tablets and 3 on desktop; touch users swipe natively. Prefer `Marquee` for an auto-scrolling logo strip. Follows the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern: a labelled region, each slide a group named "2 of 6", Arrow Left/Right scroll when the track is focused, buttons disable at the ends, and scrolling is instant under reduced motion.

props.name: children
props.doc: One child per slide.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the carousel region.

examples:
<Carousel label="Customer stories">
  {stories.map((s) => <StoryCard key={s.id} {...s} />)}
</Carousel>

components.name: cart-line-item
components.title: CartLineItem
components.description: One product row in a cart or order summary: title, price, a quantity stepper and remove.
components.whenToUse: Stack rows inside a cart drawer or checkout. Quantity is controlled: pass `quantity` and update it in `onQuantityChange`. The stepper is a group named "Quantity for <title>" so its +/- buttons make sense to screen readers; the remove button only renders with `onRemove`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Product name.

props.name: price
props.doc: Pre-formatted price, e.g. "$480.00".

props.name: quantity
props.doc: Current quantity (controlled).

props.name: onQuantityChange
props.doc: Called with the new quantity, already clamped to `min`…`max`.

props.name: min
props.doc: Lowest quantity the stepper allows.

props.name: max
props.doc: Highest quantity the stepper allows.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Shows a remove button and is called when it is pressed.

props.name: media
props.doc: Optional thumbnail, e.g. a 40px image.

examples:
<CartLineItem title="Lumen Pro, annual" price="$480.00" quantity={qty}
  onQuantityChange={setQty} onRemove={() => remove(id)} />

components.name: case-study-card
components.title: CaseStudyCard
components.description: A customer-story card: company eyebrow, headline, one big result figure and an optional delta chip.
components.whenToUse: Use on marketing and customers pages, one outcome per card. For a live dashboard number use StatCard; for a quote use Testimonial. Only show results the customer has approved; never invent figures.

props.name: company
props.doc: Customer name, shown as a small uppercase eyebrow.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline describing the outcome. Rendered as an h3.

props.name: result
props.doc: The headline figure, pre-formatted (e.g. "2 days", "$1.2M").

props.name: delta
props.doc: Optional percent change shown beside the result; negative values render as a decrease.

props.name: href
props.doc: Wraps the card in a link when set, so the whole card opens the full story.

examples: <CaseStudyCard company="Northwind" title="Month-end close in two days" result="2 days" delta={-60} />

components.name: center
components.title: Center
components.description: A layout primitive that centres its children horizontally and vertically in a narrow, text-centred column.
components.whenToUse: Use for empty states, auth screens and single-message pages. For a page-width wrapper use Container; for a row of items use Cluster; for a vertical list use Stack.

props.name: size
props.doc: Max width of the column. Defaults to "lg" (32rem).

examples: <Center className="min-h-80"><EmptyState title="No invoices yet" /></Center>

components.name: character-count
components.title: CharacterCount
components.description: A "42/280" counter for a text field that turns red past the limit and tells screen readers only when the limit is near.
components.whenToUse: Place it under a Textarea or Input and point the field's `aria-describedby` at its `id`. It does not block typing; pair it with the field's `maxLength` if you need a hard cap.

props.name: value
props.doc: Current length, usually `value.length`.

props.name: max
props.doc: The limit. Past it the count turns red.

props.name: warnAt
props.doc: Remaining characters at which screen readers start hearing the count. Defaults to 10% of `max`.

props.name: id
props.doc: Id for the field's `aria-describedby`.

components.name: chart-card
components.title: ChartCard
components.description: A raised card that frames a chart with a title, an optional description and an optional header action.
components.whenToUse: Wrap AreaChart, BarChart, LineChart and friends in it so every chart on a dashboard shares one header style. The title labels the region for screen readers. For a single KPI with a sparkline use StatSparkline.

props.name: title
props.doc: Card heading, rendered as an h3 that names the region.

props.name: description
props.doc: Secondary line under the title, such as the time range.

props.name: action
props.doc: Rendered at the header's end: a range picker, a menu or a link.

props.name: children
props.doc: The chart, plus any ChartLegend.

examples:
<ChartCard title="Revenue" description="Last 12 weeks" action={<Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Export</Button>}>
  <AreaChart data={weekly} />
</ChartCard>

components.name: chart-legend
components.title: ChartLegend
components.description: A row of colour swatches and series names to sit under a chart.
components.whenToUse: Pass the same colours your chart uses so the key matches. Swatches are decorative; the label carries the meaning. Use inside ChartCard below the chart.

props.name: items
props.doc: Series to list. Colors fall back to accent, success, warning and danger in turn.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the list. Defaults to "Legend".

examples: <ChartLegend items={[{ label: "Revenue", color: "var(--accent)" }, { label: "Refunds", color: "var(--danger)" }]} />

components.name: chart-tooltip-card
components.title: ChartTooltipCard
components.description: A small raised card for chart hover details: a title and label-value rows with tabular numbers.
components.whenToUse: Render it inside your chart's hover layer, positioned at the pointer. It is a polite live region, so screen readers hear the values as the hovered point changes. For a tooltip on a button or icon use Tooltip instead.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading, usually the hovered x value (a date or category).

props.name: rows
props.doc: Label-value pairs, values pre-formatted. Labels double as keys, so keep them unique.

examples: <ChartTooltipCard title="Week 12" rows={[{ label: "Revenue", value: "$49,000" }, { label: "Refunds", value: "$1,200" }]} />

components.name: chat-thread
components.title: ChatThread
components.description: A scrolling chat transcript of MessageBubbles that sticks to the newest message unless the reader has scrolled up.
components.whenToUse: Use for AI chat and support threads. Give it a fixed height (e.g. `className="h-96"`) so it scrolls. It is a `role="log"` region, so screen readers hear new messages politely. Pair with PromptInput or AiComposer below it.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Messages oldest first. `id` must be stable; `streaming` shows the live cursor on that bubble.

props.name: empty
props.doc: Shown when `messages` is empty. Defaults to a muted "No messages yet".

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the log region. Defaults to "Conversation".

examples:
<ChatThread
  className="h-96"
  messages={[
    { id: "1", role: "user", content: "Summarise INV-2041" },
    { id: "2", role: "assistant", content: "Northwind owes $12,400, due Friday.", streaming: true },
  ]}
/>

components.name: check-run-list
components.title: CheckRunList
components.description: A compact list of CI checks (build, lint, e2e) with a status icon and word for each.
components.whenToUse: Use on pull request, deploy and release screens. For a multi-stage pipeline with arrows use BuildPipeline. Status is always spelled out in text, never colour alone.

props.name: runs
props.doc: Checks in display order. `name` is the React key, so keep names unique.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the list. Defaults to "Checks".

examples: <CheckRunList runs={[{ name: "build", status: "success" }, { name: "e2e", status: "running" }]} />

components.name: checkbox-group
components.title: CheckboxGroup
components.description: A labelled group that stacks related Checkboxes, so screen readers announce the group name before each option.
components.whenToUse: Use for "pick any" choices (notification channels, permissions). For "pick one" use RadioGroup; for filters as chips use ChipFilter. Give it a `label` (visible) or an `aria-label`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible group heading; also names the group for screen readers.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Stack vertically (default) or wrap in a row.

examples:
<CheckboxGroup label="Email me about">
  <Label className="flex items-center gap-2"><Checkbox name="notify" value="invoices" defaultChecked /> Paid invoices</Label>
  <Label className="flex items-center gap-2"><Checkbox name="notify" value="reports" /> Weekly reports</Label>
</CheckboxGroup>

components.name: checkbox
components.title: Checkbox
components.description: An accessible checkbox built on Base UI: 16px box, 44px touch target, accent fill when checked, a dash when indeterminate.
components.whenToUse: Use for independent on/off choices and multi-select lists; wrap several in CheckboxGroup. For a setting that applies immediately use Switch. Controlled with `checked` + `onCheckedChange(checked: boolean)`, or uncontrolled with `defaultChecked`. Pass `name` and `value` to submit with a form. Label it with a wrapping `<Label>` or `aria-label`; set `aria-invalid` to show the error state.
examples:
<Label className="flex items-center gap-2"><Checkbox name="terms" required /> I accept the terms</Label>
<Checkbox checked={all} indeterminate={some} onCheckedChange={toggleAll} aria-label="Select all rows" />

components.name: checkout-summary
components.title: CheckoutSummary
components.description: A compact checkout panel: line items, a total and one pay button.
components.whenToUse: Use beside a payment form (CreditCardInput) at the last step of checkout. For a full order breakdown with tax and discounts use OrderSummary. Prices are pre-formatted strings, so format money with Intl.NumberFormat before passing it in.

props.name: items
props.doc: Line items. `name` is the React key, so keep names unique.

props.name: total
props.doc: Pre-formatted total, e.g. "$61".

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading. Defaults to "Order summary".

props.name: payLabel
props.doc: Pay button text. Defaults to "Pay now".

props.name: onPay
props.doc: Called when the pay button is pressed. Set `payType="submit"` instead to submit the surrounding form.

props.name: payType
props.doc: Button type. Use "submit" inside a `<form>`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the pay button, e.g. while card details are invalid or a payment is in flight.

examples:
<CheckoutSummary
  items={[{ name: "Pro · monthly", price: "$49" }]}
  total="$49"
  onPay={submit}
  payLabel="Pay $49"
/>

components.name: chip-filter
components.title: ChipFilter
components.description: A row of pill-shaped radio chips for picking one filter, uncontrolled unless a value is passed.
components.whenToUse: Use above a list or table to switch between a few status filters ("All", "Paid", "Overdue"). For many options use Select; for toggling several filters at once use FacetFilter; for switching views use SegmentedControl or Tabs. Keyboard: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move and select, Home/End jump to the ends.

props.name: options
props.doc: Chips in order. `value` must be unique.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selection. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled filter.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial selection for the uncontrolled filter.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the chip's `value` whenever the selection changes.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the radio group. Defaults to "Filter".

examples:
const [status, setStatus] = React.useState("all")
<ChipFilter label="Invoice status" options={[{ value: "all", label: "All" }, { value: "paid", label: "Paid" }]} value={status} onChange={setStatus} />

components.name: choice-card
components.title: ChoiceCard
components.description: A large selectable card button with an optional icon, a title and a description.
components.whenToUse: Use for onboarding and plan or workspace-type choices where each option needs a sentence of explanation. Pass `selected` to make it a toggle button (`aria-pressed`); wrap a set in a `role="group"` with an `aria-label`. For compact single choice use RadioGroup or SegmentedControl; for pricing use PlanCard.

props.name: title
props.doc: Bold first line.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting sentence under the title.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Selected state. When defined the card is a toggle button and announces pressed or not pressed.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Leading icon, sized to 20px.

examples: setType("solo")} /> setType("team")} />

components.name: citation-chip
components.title: CitationChip
components.description: A small inline chip that cites a source in an AI answer: an optional numbered index plus the source name.
components.whenToUse: Place it inline after the sentence it supports. It renders a button (open a SourceCard or side panel in `onClick`), or a link when `href` is set. For a full source preview use SourceCard; for attached files in a prompt use ContextPill.

props.name: index
props.doc: Footnote number shown in accent before the label.

props.name: href
props.doc: Renders an external link (opens in a new tab) instead of a button.

examples: Refunds settle in 5-10 days Stripe docs

components.name: cluster
components.title: Cluster
components.description: A layout primitive that lays children out in a wrapping row with an even gap, like tags, buttons or badges.
components.whenToUse: Use for horizontal groups that should wrap on narrow screens. For a vertical list use Stack; for centring use Center; for page width use Container. `gap` is in 4px steps, so `gap={2}` is 8px.

props.name: gap
props.doc: Space between items in 4px steps (2 = 8px). Defaults to 2.

props.name: align
props.doc: Cross-axis alignment. Defaults to "center".

props.name: justify
props.doc: Main-axis distribution. Defaults to "start".

examples: <Cluster gap={2} justify="end"><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button><Button>Save</Button></Cluster>

components.name: code-block
components.title: CodeBlock
components.description: An ink-well code block in both themes, with lightweight token colouring (strings, keywords, JSX tags, comments) and a copy button.
components.whenToUse: Use for static snippets in docs, onboarding and API-key screens. It highlights with a tiny built-in tokenizer (no Shiki/Prism), so it suits short JS/TS/JSX/shell snippets. For a live editable area use CodeEditorFrame; for a shell session use TerminalWindow; for a single command with a copy button use CopyButton beside an inline `<code>`.

props.name: code
props.doc: The source to show and copy. A trailing newline is ignored.

props.name: language
props.doc: Label shown in the header badge, e.g. "tsx", "bash", "json". Does not change highlighting.

props.name: filename
props.doc: File name shown in the header.

props.name: showLineNumbers
props.doc: Prefix each line with its number (not copied).

examples: <CodeBlock filename="install.sh" language="bash" code={"npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.minidev.pro/r/button.json"} />

components.name: code-editor-frame
components.title: CodeEditorFrame
components.description: A neutral editor chrome: a file-name tab bar over a monospace body that hosts your own editor or code.
components.whenToUse: Wrap a `<textarea>`, CodeMirror or Monaco in it so the editor matches the kit. For read-only highlighted snippets with a copy button use CodeBlock; for a whole window with traffic lights use WindowChrome.

props.name: filename
props.doc: File name shown in the tab bar; also names the region for screen readers.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Controls at the tab bar's end, such as Run or Format buttons.

props.name: children
props.doc: The editor itself.

examples:
<CodeEditorFrame filename="schema.sql" actions={<Button size="xs" variant="ghost">Run</Button>}>
  <textarea aria-label="SQL" className="w-full resize-none bg-transparent outline-none" rows={8} />
</CodeEditorFrame>

components.name: collapsible-sidebar
components.title: CollapsibleSidebar
components.description: A Sidebar with a built-in collapse toggle on its edge that shrinks it to an icon rail.
components.whenToUse: Use as the left rail of an app shell. Uncontrolled by default; pass `collapsed` + `onCollapsedChange` to persist the state. Put SidebarNavItem children inside; their labels truncate when collapsed. For a full layout use AppShell; on mobile use MobileNavDrawer.

props.name: children
props.doc: Sidebar content, usually SidebarNavItems.

props.name: collapsed
props.doc: Controlled collapsed state. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled sidebar.

props.name: defaultCollapsed
props.doc: Initial state for the uncontrolled sidebar.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.doc: Called with the next state when the toggle is pressed.

examples:
<CollapsibleSidebar>
  <SidebarNavItem icon={<HomeIcon />} active>Home</SidebarNavItem>
  <SidebarNavItem icon={<ReceiptIcon />}>Invoices</SidebarNavItem>
</CollapsibleSidebar>

components.name: collapsible
components.title: Collapsible
components.description: A single show-and-hide section built on Base UI: a full-width trigger button and a panel it opens.
components.whenToUse:
Use for one optional block (advanced settings, an address, "show more"). For a stack of sections use Accordion; for a table row that expands use ExpandableRow. The trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` automatically.

Key props (on `Collapsible`): `open` / `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange(open)`, `disabled`. Style the open state with `data-panel-open` on the trigger (e.g. rotate a chevron with `group-data-[panel-open]:rotate-180`).
examples:
<Collapsible defaultOpen>
  <CollapsibleTrigger className="group">Advanced <ChevronDownIcon className="size-4 transition-transform group-data-[panel-open]:rotate-180" /></CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsiblePanel>Webhook retries, idempotency keys and rate limits.</CollapsiblePanel>
</Collapsible>

components.name: color-picker
components.title: ColorPicker
components.description: A row of colour swatches that works as a radio group: pick one colour, get its CSS colour string back.
components.whenToUse: Use for labels, tags, calendars and brand accents where a fixed palette beats a free picker. Uncontrolled unless `value` is passed. Each swatch has a spoken name ("Violet"), so pass `{ value, label }` objects for custom palettes. Keyboard: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move and select, Home/End jump to the ends. For a theme switcher use ThemePicker.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selection (a CSS colour string from `colors`). Leave undefined for an uncontrolled picker.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial selection for the uncontrolled picker. Defaults to the first colour.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen swatch's CSS colour string.

props.name: colors
props.doc: The palette. Plain strings are named by their value, so prefer `{ value, label }` for readable names.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the group. Defaults to "Color".

examples:
const [color, setColor] = React.useState("oklch(0.52 0.12 150)")
<ColorPicker label="Label colour" value={color} onChange={setColor} />

components.name: column-visibility-menu
components.title: ColumnVisibilityMenu
components.description: A "Columns" button that opens a checklist of table columns to show or hide; uncontrolled unless `visible` is passed.
components.whenToUse: Put it in a TableToolbar above a DataTable, then filter your DataTable `columns` by the visible ids. Ids always come back in column order. For a full saved-view system use SavedViews.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Every toggleable column, in table order.

props.name: visible
props.doc: Controlled list of visible column ids. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled menu.

props.name: defaultVisible
props.doc: Initial visible ids for the uncontrolled menu. Defaults to every column.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the visible ids, in column order, after each toggle.

props.name: label
props.doc: Trigger button text. Defaults to "Columns".

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the trigger button.

components.name: combobox
components.title: Combobox
components.description: A select-style button that opens a searchable list: type to filter, arrow keys to move, Enter to pick. Built on Base UI Combobox.
components.whenToUse: Use when a single choice has more than about 7 options (customers, assignees, countries). For a short fixed list use Select; for several choices use MultiSelect; for free text with suggestions use Autocomplete. Uncontrolled unless `value` is passed. Label it with FormField (pass the same `id` to both) or `aria-label`.

props.name: items
props.doc: Options. `value` must be unique; `label` is shown and searched.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selection (an item's `value`). Leave undefined for an uncontrolled combobox.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial selection for the uncontrolled combobox.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the picked item's `value`.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Trigger text while nothing is selected.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: Placeholder of the search field inside the popup. Defaults to "Filter…".

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the trigger button (width defaults to w-64).

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: Shown when the filter matches nothing.

props.name: id
props.doc: Id for the trigger, so a `<label htmlFor>` or FormField can name it.

props.name: name
props.doc: Submits the selected `value` under this name inside a `<form>`.

props.name: required
props.doc: Requires a selection before the form submits.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

examples:
const [customer, setCustomer] = React.useState("northwind")
<FormField id="customer" label="Customer">
  <Combobox id="customer" items={[{ value: "northwind", label: "Northwind Traders" }]} value={customer} onChange={setCustomer} />
</FormField>

components.name: command-dialog
components.title: CommandDialog
components.description: A command palette in a dialog; uncontrolled with its own "Search commands" trigger unless `open` is passed.
components.whenToUse: A thin wrapper over CommandPalette with a plain outline trigger and no ⌘K listener. Prefer CommandPalette directly when you want the ⌘K shortcut or a custom trigger. Commands take `id`, `label`, optional `keywords`, `shortcut` and `onSelect`.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Leave undefined to get a built-in trigger button and internal state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called with the next open state.

props.name: commands
props.doc: Commands to search; same shape as CommandPalette's.

examples:
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)
<CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} commands={[{ id: "new", label: "New invoice", onSelect: createInvoice }]} />

components.name: command-item
components.title: CommandItem
components.description: One row of a command list: an optional icon, a label and an optional keyboard shortcut hint.
components.whenToUse: Use to build your own command or action list. For a ready-made searchable palette use CommandPalette (or CommandDialog for a trigger + dialog); for "/" commands in an editor use SlashCommandMenu. `active` marks the keyboard-highlighted row.

props.name: children
props.doc: The command label.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: Shortcut hint shown at the row's end, e.g. "⌘N". Display only; bind the key yourself.

props.name: active
props.doc: Highlighted state, for the row the keyboard is on.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Leading icon, sized to 16px.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Runs when the row is clicked or activated with Enter/Space.

examples: <CommandItem icon={<FilePlusIcon />} shortcut="⌘N" onSelect={createInvoice}>New invoice</CommandItem>

components.name: command-palette
components.title: CommandPalette
components.description: A searchable command dialog: type to filter, arrow keys to move, Enter to run, opened from a trigger button or ⌘K / Ctrl+K.
components.whenToUse: Use as the app-wide "do anything" launcher. Uncontrolled it renders its own trigger and listens for ⌘K; pass `open` + `onOpenChange` to launch it from your own button or shortcut. For a ready trigger-plus-dialog pair use CommandDialog; for one row use CommandItem; for "/" commands inside an editor use SlashCommandMenu. Follows the APG combobox-with-listbox pattern.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Omit it and the palette manages itself: it renders a trigger and listens for ⌘K / Ctrl+K.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called with the next open state (Escape, outside click, after running a command).

props.name: commands
props.doc: Commands to search. Defaults to a set of Lumen actions.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: Rendered when the palette is uncontrolled. Defaults to a search button with a ⌘K hint.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Search field placeholder. Defaults to "Type a command…".

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: Shown when nothing matches. Defaults to "No commands".

examples:
<CommandPalette
  commands={[
    { id: "new-invoice", label: "Create invoice", shortcut: "⌘N", onSelect: () => router.push("/invoices/new") },
    { id: "theme", label: "Toggle dark mode", keywords: ["theme", "light"], onSelect: toggleTheme },
  ]}
/>

components.name: comment-composer
components.title: CommentComposer
components.description: A comment box: a textarea and a submit button that stays disabled until there is text. ⌘/Ctrl+Enter submits.
components.whenToUse: Use under a CommentThread or on an issue, invoice or review page. For an AI chat input use PromptInput or AiComposer; for @mentions use MentionInput. It clears itself after `onSubmit` and hands you the trimmed text.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the trimmed text when the user submits. The box then clears.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the textarea. Defaults to "Comment".

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: Submit button text. Defaults to "Comment".

examples: <CommentComposer onSubmit={(text) => addComment({ body: text })} submitLabel="Reply" />

components.name: comment-thread
components.title: CommentThread
components.description: A vertical thread of comments, each with an avatar, author, time and body.
components.whenToUse: Use on issues, invoices, reviews and docs. Pair with CommentComposer underneath to add replies. For chat between a person and an AI use ChatThread; for a system event log use ActivityFeed or AuditTrail.

props.name: comments
props.doc: Comments in display order. Defaults to a short Lumen thread.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the list. Defaults to "Comments".

examples: <CommentThread comments={[{ id: "c1", author: "Maya Chen", body: "Sent the reminder.", time: "2h ago" }]} />

components.name: commit-row
components.title: CommitRow
components.description: One git commit as a list row: author avatar, message, author and relative time, the short SHA and a copy button.
components.whenToUse: Stack several inside a bordered container for a commit history on deploy, release or PR screens. For CI status per commit add a CheckRunList; for a code change view use DiffView.

props.name: sha
props.doc: Short SHA, shown and copied as is.

props.name: message
props.doc: Commit subject line; truncates to one line.

props.name: author
props.doc: Author display name. Initials are derived for the avatar.

props.name: date
props.doc: Commit time (ISO string or Date). Pass a fixed value from your data so server and client render the same.

examples: <CommitRow sha="f90e1ab" message="Fix invoice rounding" author="Maya Chen" date="2026-11-12T09:30:00Z" />

components.name: comparison-table
components.title: ComparisonTable
components.description: A feature-by-plan matrix: one row per feature, a check, a dash or a value per plan.
components.whenToUse: Use under pricing cards to compare plans in detail. For the plan cards themselves use PricingTable or PlanCard; for comparing AI models use ModelCompare. Checks and dashes carry screen-reader text ("Included" / "Not included").

props.name: features
props.doc: Row labels, in order. Each plan's `values` line up with them by index.

props.name: plans
props.doc: Columns. A boolean renders a check or a dash, a string renders as text.

props.name: featureLabel
props.doc: Visible heading of the first column. Defaults to "Feature".

props.name: caption
props.doc: Table caption for screen readers, e.g. "Plan comparison".

examples:
<ComparisonTable
  features={["Seats", "Audit log"]}
  plans={[{ name: "Starter", values: ["2", false] }, { name: "Scale", values: ["Unlimited", true] }]}
/>

components.name: confirm-destructive
components.title: ConfirmDestructive
components.description: A ready-made "are you sure?" flow: a red trigger button that opens an alert dialog with Cancel and a destructive Confirm.
components.whenToUse: Drop it in wherever one destructive action needs a confirmation step. Both buttons close the dialog; `onConfirm` runs on Confirm. Focus starts inside, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the trigger. For custom layouts compose AlertDialog yourself; for type-the-name confirmation use DeleteAccountConfirm; for a settings section use DangerZone.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.doc: Text of the red trigger button. Defaults to "Delete".

props.name: title
props.doc: Dialog title, phrased as the question.

props.name: description
props.doc: The consequence, read when the dialog opens.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.doc: Confirm button text. Defaults to "Confirm"; prefer the verb, e.g. "Delete invoice".

props.name: cancelLabel
props.doc: Cancel button text. Defaults to "Cancel".

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Runs when Confirm is pressed, before the dialog closes.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called with the next open state.

examples: <ConfirmDestructive triggerLabel="Delete invoice" title="Delete INV-2041?" description="This cannot be undone." confirmLabel="Delete" onConfirm={remove} />

components.name: connected-account
components.title: ConnectedAccount
components.description: A settings row for a linked third-party account: provider, account handle and a Disconnect button.
components.whenToUse: Stack one per provider under an "Connected accounts" heading in settings. For an integration with a Connect state and description use IntegrationCard; for SSO setup use SsoProviderCard. Bring your own provider logo through `icon`.

props.name: provider
props.doc: Provider name, e.g. "GitHub".

props.name: account
props.doc: The linked account, e.g. an email or handle.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Leading logo or icon, sized to 20px.

props.name: onDisconnect
props.doc: Runs when Disconnect is pressed. Confirm first if unlinking loses data.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Button text. Defaults to "Disconnect".

examples: <ConnectedAccount provider="GitHub" account="@maya-chen" icon={<GithubIcon />} onDisconnect={() => unlink("github")} />

components.name: console-output
components.title: ConsoleOutput
components.description: A monospace log pane for console or build output, with warn and error lines tagged in text and colour.
components.whenToUse: Use for build logs, function logs and dev-tool panels. It is a keyboard-scrollable `role="log"` region. For an interactive shell look use TerminalWindow; for a thrown error with frames use StackTrace.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Lines oldest first. `level` defaults to "log".

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the log region. Defaults to "Console".

examples: <ConsoleOutput lines={[{ text: "ready on :3000" }, { level: "warn", text: "deprecated API" }, { level: "error", text: "fetch failed" }]} />

components.name: container
components.title: Container
components.description: A layout primitive that centres page content at a readable max width with responsive side padding (16px, 24px from sm).
components.whenToUse: Wrap each page section's content in it. For a narrow centred column use Center; for spacing children use Stack or Cluster.

props.name: size
props.doc: Max width: sm 672px (prose), default 1024px, lg 1280px (dashboards), full none.

examples: <Container size="lg"><PageHeader title="Invoices" /></Container>

components.name: context-chip
components.title: ContextChip
components.description: A small toggle chip for adding context to an AI prompt (a file, a page, a selection), shown pressed when active.
components.whenToUse: Use in a row above PromptInput to let people switch context sources on and off. It is a toggle button (`aria-pressed`). For an attached item with a remove button use ContextPill; for suggested prompts use SuggestionChips; for filters use ChipFilter.

props.name: active
props.doc: Pressed state. When defined the chip announces as a toggle button.

examples: <ContextChip active={useFile} onClick={() => setUseFile((v) => !v)}>invoice.pdf</ContextChip>

components.name: context-menu
components.title: ContextMenu
components.description: A right-click (or long-press) menu for any surface, built on Base UI: opens at the pointer, arrow keys move, Enter runs, Escape closes.
components.whenToUse: Wrap a row, card or canvas item and pass `items`; each runs its `onSelect` and closes the menu. Mark irreversible actions `destructive`. Always offer the same actions somewhere visible (a DropdownMenu or row actions) since right-click is hidden from many users. For a menu opened by a button use DropdownMenu.

props.name: children
props.doc: The surface that opens the menu on right-click or long-press.

props.name: items
props.doc: Menu entries in order. `id` must be unique.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the wrapping trigger element.

examples:
<ContextMenu items={[{ id: "rename", label: "Rename", shortcut: "F2" }, { id: "delete", label: "Delete", destructive: true, onSelect: remove }]}>
  <FileRow name="Q3-report.pdf" />
</ContextMenu>

components.name: context-pill
components.title: ContextPill
components.description: A rounded pill naming one item attached to an AI prompt (a file, a URL, a selection), with an optional remove button.
components.whenToUse: Show a row of them above or inside PromptInput for the context the model will see. Pass `onRemove` to make it dismissible. For on/off context toggles use ContextChip; for uploaded files with size and progress use AttachmentChip; for a removable tag use TagsInput.

props.name: children
props.doc: The item's name; truncates when long.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Leading icon, sized to 12px.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Shows a remove button that calls this.

props.name: removeLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the remove button. Defaults to "Remove <children>" when children is text.

examples: <ContextPill icon={<FileTextIcon />} onRemove={() => detach("invoice.pdf")}>invoice.pdf</ContextPill>

components.name: conversation-sidebar
components.title: ConversationSidebar
components.description: A chat app's conversation list: a new-chat button on top, then titled threads with their last activity.
components.whenToUse: Use as the left rail of an AI chat screen next to ChatThread. Uncontrolled unless `activeId` is passed; the active thread gets `aria-current`. For general app navigation use Sidebar or CollapsibleSidebar.

props.name: items
props.doc: Conversations, newest first. Defaults to a few Lumen threads timed relative to now.

props.name: activeId
props.doc: Controlled active conversation.

props.name: defaultActiveId
props.doc: Active conversation when uncontrolled.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the picked conversation's id.

props.name: onNew
props.doc: Called by the "New chat" button.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Defaults to "Conversations".

examples: <ConversationSidebar items={threads} activeId={threadId} onSelect={setThreadId} onNew={startThread} />

components.name: cookie-banner
components.title: CookieBanner
components.description: A floating cookie-consent card fixed to the bottom-right, with Reject and Accept buttons of equal reach.
components.whenToUse: Render it only until the visitor chooses, and store the choice yourself (cookie or localStorage) in `onAccept` / `onReject`. It is a labelled, non-modal region, so the page stays usable. Pass `className="static"` to place it inline. For a site-wide notice bar use AnnouncementBar; for a blocking choice use AlertDialog.

props.name: onAccept
props.doc: Called when the visitor accepts non-essential cookies.

props.name: onReject
props.doc: Called when the visitor rejects non-essential cookies.

props.name: children
props.doc: The message. Defaults to a one-line analytics and preferences notice.
props.default: "We use cookies for analytics and pre...

props.name: policyHref
props.doc: Link to your cookie or privacy policy, shown after the message.

props.name: acceptLabel
