props.doc: Accept button text. Defaults to "Accept".

props.name: rejectLabel
props.doc: Reject button text. Defaults to "Reject".

examples: {!consent && <CookieBanner onAccept={() => save("all")} onReject={() => save("essential")} policyHref="/privacy" />}

components.name: copy-button
components.title: CopyButton
components.description: A Button that copies `value` to the clipboard and flips to a check and "Copied" for 1.5s, announced to screen readers.
components.whenToUse: Use beside API keys, links, install commands and ids. Takes every Button variant and size. For a monospace id that is itself the button use CopyId; for a whole snippet use CodeBlock (it has its own copy button).

props.name: value
props.doc: The text written to the clipboard.

props.name: label
props.doc: Button text at rest. Defaults to "Copy".

props.name: copiedLabel
props.doc: Button text after a successful copy. Defaults to "Copied".

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called after the text is on the clipboard.

examples: <CopyButton value="npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.minidev.pro/r/button.json" label="Copy command" />

components.name: copy-id
components.title: CopyId
components.description: A small monospace chip showing an id (user, invoice, request) that copies it on click.
components.whenToUse: Use in tables, detail headers and logs where an id should be visible and copyable. Long ids truncate visually but copy in full. For a labelled button beside some other text use CopyButton; for keys that should stay hidden use SecretReveal.

props.name: value
props.doc: The id shown and copied.

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called after the id is on the clipboard.

examples: <CopyId value="usr_8f2a91c4" />

components.name: coupon-input
components.title: CouponInput
components.description: A coupon or promo-code field with an Apply button and an inline, announced success or error message.
components.whenToUse: Use in a checkout or upgrade flow beside CheckoutSummary or OrderSummary. Validate on your server in `onApply`: return `true` for a valid code, `false` or an error string for an invalid one (a Promise works too). Enter applies; it never submits the surrounding form. Without `onApply` it runs a demo check that accepts "HAIRLINE".

props.name: onApply
props.doc: Validates the trimmed code. Return true when valid, false or an error message when not.

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: Shown after a valid code. Defaults to "Coupon applied".

props.name: errorMessage
props.doc: Shown after an invalid code when `onApply` returns false. Defaults to "Invalid code".

props.name: label
props.doc: Input placeholder and accessible name. Defaults to "Coupon code".

examples: <CouponInput onApply={async (code) => (await fetch(`/api/coupons/${code}`)).ok} successMessage="20% off applied" />

components.name: coverage-meter
components.title: CoverageMeter
components.description: A labelled bar for a percentage score such as test coverage, coloured green, amber or red by thresholds.
components.whenToUse: Use on CI, repo and quality dashboards. It is a `role="meter"`, so screen readers hear the label and percent. For usage against a limit use UsageMeter or QuotaBar; for task progress use Progress.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is measured. Defaults to "Line coverage".

props.name: value
props.doc: Percent, 0-100. Values outside are clamped.

props.name: good
props.doc: At or above this the bar is green. Defaults to 80.

props.name: warn
props.doc: At or above this (and below `good`) the bar is amber; below it, red. Defaults to 60.

examples: <CoverageMeter label="Branch coverage" value={72} good={80} warn={60} />

components.name: create-api-key
components.title: CreateApiKey
components.description: An inline "name your key, then create it" row: a labelled input and a Create key button that stays disabled until there is a name.
components.whenToUse: Use at the top of an API keys settings page above ApiKeyList. Enter creates. Show the new secret once with SecretReveal after `onCreate`.

props.name: onCreate
props.doc: Called with the trimmed key name. The field clears afterwards.

props.name: label
props.doc: Field label. Defaults to "Key name".

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Input placeholder. Defaults to "Production".

examples: <CreateApiKey onCreate={async (name) => setSecret(await createKey(name))} />

components.name: credit-balance
components.title: CreditBalance
components.description: A compact inline readout of a prepaid balance: a small label and a large tabular number ("Credits 1,240").
components.whenToUse: Use in a topbar, billing page or usage screen for AI credits, wallet or prepaid balances. Format the number yourself. For usage against a limit use UsageMeter; for a KPI with a trend use StatCard; for animated changes wrap the number in NumberRoll.

props.name: balance
props.doc: Pre-formatted balance, e.g. "1,240" or "$18.40".

props.name: label
props.doc: Label before the number. Defaults to "Credits".

examples: <CreditBalance label="AI credits" balance={new Intl.NumberFormat().format(1240)} />

components.name: credit-card-input
components.title: CreditCardInput
components.description: Card details fields with brand-aware formatting, a Luhn check, auto-advance and inline errors; UI only, never sends card data anywhere.
components.whenToUse:
The number groups by brand (Visa, Mastercard and Discover 4-4-4-4, Amex 4-6-5), the brand shows as a text badge, expiry formats to MM / YY and advances on its own, and the CVC expects 4 digits for Amex. Fields carry cc-* autocomplete hints and aria-invalid, and errors appear once a field is left. It formats and checks input in the browser and does not process, tokenize or transmit payments: for real payments prefer your provider's hosted fields (Stripe Elements and the like) for PCI scope, and use this for demos, prototypes or providers that accept raw values. For a saved card use PaymentMethodCard; for a full add-card flow use AddCardForm.

`onChange` receives `{ number, expiry, cvc, brand, name, postalCode, valid }`; `luhn(digits)` is exported for your own checks.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called on every edit with the parsed values.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial field values; `number` and `expiry` may include spaces or a slash.

props.name: showName
props.doc: Show the name on card field.

props.name: showPostalCode
props.doc: Show the postal code field.

props.name: showBrands
props.doc: Show the accepted brands, the detected one highlighted.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label of the card fields group. Defaults to "Card details".

props.name: hint
props.doc: Helper line shown while there is no error.

examples: <CreditCardInput onChange={(card) => setCanPay(card.valid)} showPostalCode={false} />

components.name: cta-banner
components.title: CtaBanner
components.description: A full-width call-to-action band: a heading, an optional line of copy and one primary action, stacked on mobile.
components.whenToUse: Use at the end of a marketing page or section. Pass `action.href` for navigation (renders a link) or `action.onClick` for an in-page action. For a hero use Hero; for a dismissible notice use Banner or AnnouncementBar; for an in-app upsell use UpgradePrompt.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading, rendered as an h3.

props.name: description
props.doc: One supporting line.

props.name: action
props.type: { label: string; onClick?: () => void; href?: string }
props.doc: The single primary action. `href` renders a link; otherwise a button calling `onClick`.

examples: <CtaBanner title="Ship your UI today" description="Install any component with one command." action={{ label: "Get started", href: "/docs" }} />

components.name: currency-input
components.title: CurrencyInput
components.description: A money amount field with the currency code inside on the left, a decimal keypad on mobile and tabular digits.
components.whenToUse: Use for prices, invoice amounts and payouts. The value is the typed string (digits, ".", "," and "-"); parse it yourself, e.g. `Number(v.replace(/,/g, ""))`, and store minor units on the server. For a stepper with +/- use NumberInput; for quantities use QuantityStepper. Label it with FormField (same `id`) or `aria-label`; without either it is named "Amount in USD".

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled value. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial value for the uncontrolled field.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the sanitised string on every edit.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code shown inside the field, e.g. "USD", "EUR". Defaults to "USD".

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Defaults to "0.00".

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name for FormData.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the wrapper (width defaults to w-40).

props.name: id
props.doc: Id for a `<label htmlFor>` or FormField.

examples:
const [amount, setAmount] = React.useState("")
<FormField id="amount" label="Amount"><CurrencyInput id="amount" currency="EUR" value={amount} onChange={setAmount} /></FormField>

components.name: danger-zone
components.title: DangerZone
components.description: A red-outlined settings section for one irreversible action, whose button asks for confirmation before `onConfirm` runs.
components.whenToUse: Put it last on a settings page (delete workspace, delete project, transfer ownership). Pass `children` to replace the built-in confirm button with your own actions, such as DeleteAccountConfirm for type-the-name confirmation.

props.name: title
props.doc: Section heading. Defaults to "Danger zone".

props.name: description
props.doc: What the action destroys.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Button and confirm text. Defaults to "Delete workspace".

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Runs after the person confirms in the dialog.

props.name: children
props.doc: Replaces the built-in confirm button.

examples:
<DangerZone
  description="Delete Northwind and all of its invoices. This cannot be undone."
  actionLabel="Delete workspace"
  onConfirm={deleteWorkspace}
/>

components.name: data-table
components.title: DataTable
components.description: A product data table: sortable headers, row selection with a bulk bar, hover row actions, sticky header, density and skeleton loading.
components.whenToUse: Use for lists of records people scan, sort and act on (invoices, users, deploys). Define `columns` once with a `cell` renderer and an optional `sortValue`; pass `data` and a stable `getRowId`. For a plain static table use Table; for 10k+ rows use VirtualizedList; for SQL output use SqlResultTable. Pair with TableToolbar, ColumnVisibilityMenu and TablePagination around it.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Column definitions. Defaults, with `data`, to a Lumen invoice table.

props.name: data
props.doc: Rows. Defaults, with `columns`, to eight sample invoices.

props.name: getRowId
props.doc: Stable id per row; selection and React keys use it. Defaults to the row index, which breaks selection when data reorders, so pass one.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: Adds a checkbox column.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Controlled selected row ids. Leave undefined for internal selection.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.doc: Called with the selected row ids after every change.

props.name: bulkActions
props.doc: Rendered in the floating bar while rows are selected.

props.name: rowActions
props.doc: Rendered at the row's end, revealed on hover/focus.

props.name: onRowClick
props.doc: Makes rows clickable and focusable; Enter on a focused row also fires it.

props.name: defaultSort
props.doc: Initial sort for uncontrolled sorting, e.g. { id: "amount", dir: "desc" }.

props.name: sort
props.doc: Controlled sort. Pass with `onSortChange`; null means unsorted.

props.name: onSortChange
props.doc: Called when a header is clicked: asc, then desc, then null.

props.name: density
props.doc: Row height: compact 36px, default 44px, comfortable 56px.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows five skeleton rows instead of data and sets aria-busy.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Fixes the height and makes the header sticky.

props.name: empty
props.doc: Shown when `data` is empty. Defaults to "No results".

props.name: caption
props.doc: Screen-reader caption that names the table. Strongly recommended.

examples:
const columns: Column<Invoice>[] = [
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", cell: (r) => r.customer, sortValue: (r) => r.customer },
  { id: "amount", header: "Amount", align: "right", cell: (r) => money(r.amount), sortValue: (r) => r.amount },
]
<DataTable columns={columns} data={invoices} getRowId={(r) => r.id} selectable caption="Invoices"
  bulkActions={(ids) => <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onClick={() => archive(ids)}>Archive</Button>} />

components.name: date-picker
components.title: DatePicker
components.description: A date field on the browser's native date input: a localised format, a built-in calendar popup and full keyboard and screen-reader support for free.
components.whenToUse: The value is an ISO date string ("2026-11-14"), so store, compare (`a < b`) and send it as is. Uncontrolled unless `value` is passed; set the value to "" to clear. Use `min` / `max` to bound it. For a start-end pair use DateRangePicker; for times use TimePicker; for an always-visible month grid use CalendarMonth. Label it with FormField (same `id`) or `aria-label`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled ISO date ("YYYY-MM-DD"), or "" for empty. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial ISO date for the uncontrolled field.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the ISO date string, or "" when cleared.

props.name: min
props.doc: Earliest selectable ISO date.

props.name: max
props.doc: Latest selectable ISO date.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name for FormData.

props.name: id
props.doc: Id for a `<label htmlFor>` or FormField.

examples:
const [due, setDue] = React.useState("2026-11-14")
<FormField id="due" label="Due date"><DatePicker id="due" value={due} onChange={setDue} min="2026-11-01" /></FormField>

components.name: date-range-picker
components.title: DateRangePicker
components.description: A start and end date as two native date inputs in one labelled group.
components.whenToUse: Use for from/to filters, reporting periods and bookings. For a single date use `DatePicker`; for a visible month grid use `CalendarMonth`. Dates are ISO day strings ("2026-11-14"), the format `<input type="date">` uses.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled range. Leave out to let the picker hold its own state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial range when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the whole range whenever either end changes.

props.name: fromId
props.doc: Id for the start input, to point an external <label> at it.

props.name: toId
props.doc: Id for the end input.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the group.

examples:
const [range, setRange] = React.useState<DateRange>({ from: "2026-11-01", to: "2026-11-30" })
<DateRangePicker value={range} onChange={setRange} />

components.name: delete-account-confirm
components.title: DeleteAccountConfirm
components.description: A type-to-confirm block that keeps the delete button disabled until the phrase matches.
components.whenToUse: Use inline on a settings page for irreversible account deletion. For a modal confirmation use `AlertDialog` or `ConfirmDestructive`; for a group of risky settings use `DangerZone`.

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Called when the phrase matches and the button is pressed.

props.name: confirmText
props.doc: The exact text the user must type.

examples: <DeleteAccountConfirm onConfirm={() => deleteAccount()} />

components.name: density-toggle
components.title: DensityToggle
components.description: A two-option Compact / Comfortable switch for table and list row density.
components.whenToUse: Use in a table toolbar or view menu. For other short option sets use `SegmentedControl`; for on/off settings use `Switch`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled density.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial density when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the newly chosen density. Never called with an empty selection.

examples:
const [density, setDensity] = React.useState<Density>("comfortable")
<DensityToggle value={density} onChange={setDensity} />

components.name: description-list
components.title: DescriptionList
components.description: Label and value pairs in a two-column grid, for record details like a customer or an invoice.
components.whenToUse: Renders a semantic <dl>. Use for read-only record details. For editable settings use `FormField` rows; for tabular data with many records use `Table`.

props.name: items
props.doc: Pairs to show, in order. Defaults to a Lumen customer record.

examples: <DescriptionList items={[{ label: "Plan", value: "Growth" }, { label: "Seats", value: 12 }]} />

components.name: dialog
components.title: Dialog
components.description: A modal window on a scrim: focus is trapped inside, Escape and the close button dismiss it, focus returns to the trigger.
components.whenToUse:
Compose it from parts. Use for short forms and focused tasks that block the page. For "are you sure?" confirmations use `AlertDialog`; for side panels use `Sheet`; for a bottom sheet on mobile use `Drawer`; for non-modal content anchored to a button use `Popover`. Always render a `DialogTitle` (and ideally a `DialogDescription`) so the dialog has an accessible name.

Controlled: `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>`.
examples:
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit invoice</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Edit invoice</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Changes are saved to INV-2041.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    ...fields
    <DialogFooter showCloseButton>
      <Button>Save</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

components.name: diff-view
components.title: DiffView
components.description: A unified diff of one file: added lines tinted success, removed lines tinted danger, context muted.
components.whenToUse: Use to show a code or config change in a review, a deploy or an agent's proposed edit. For a single-line before/after use `InlineCodeDiff`; for plain code use `CodeBlock`. Screen readers hear "added" or "removed" before each changed line.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Lines in display order.

props.name: filename
props.doc: File path shown in the header bar and used in the region's accessible name.

examples:
<DiffView
  filename="lib/billing.ts"
  lines={[
    { type: "ctx", text: "export function total(items) {" },
    { type: "del", text: "  return sum(items)" },
    { type: "add", text: "  return sum(items) + tax(items)" },
    { type: "ctx", text: "}" },
  ]}
/>

components.name: donut-chart
components.title: DonutChart
components.description: A single value as a ring filled to a percentage of `max`, with the percentage in the centre.
components.whenToUse: Use for one ratio at a glance (storage used, goal reached). For several slices use `PieChart`; for concentric rings use `RadialChart`; for a half dial use `GaugeChart`; for a labelled linear bar use `Meter` or `Progress`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Current value, clamped to 0..max.

props.name: max
props.doc: Value that fills the ring.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the value measures. Used in the accessible name, e.g. "Seats used: 68%".

examples:
<DonutChart value={68} label="Seats used" />
<DonutChart value={3.4} max={5} label="Storage, GB" />

components.name: downgrade-warning
components.title: DowngradeWarning
components.description: An inline card that spells out what a plan downgrade removes, with keep and downgrade actions.
components.whenToUse: Use on a billing page before a plan change. For a multi-step cancellation use `CancelFlow`; for a modal confirmation use `AlertDialog`; to sell an upgrade instead use `UpgradePrompt`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the card.

props.name: description
props.doc: What the user loses by downgrading.

props.name: keepLabel
props.doc: Label of the safe (outline) action.

props.name: downgradeLabel
props.doc: Label of the destructive action.

props.name: onKeep
props.doc: Called by the safe action.

props.name: onDowngrade
props.doc: Called by the destructive action.

examples:
<DowngradeWarning
  title="Downgrade to Starter?"
  description="Audit logs and SSO turn off at the end of this billing period."
  onKeep={() => router.back()}
  onDowngrade={() => downgrade("starter")}
/>

components.name: drawer
components.title: Drawer
components.description: A bottom sheet for quick actions and mobile forms: a Sheet that slides up from the bottom edge.
components.whenToUse: Uncontrolled, it renders its own trigger button (pass `trigger` to replace it). Controlled, pass `open` and `onClose` and render your own trigger. For a side panel use `Sheet`; for a centred modal use `Dialog`; for an iOS style action list use `MobileActionSheet`.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Leave it out and the drawer renders its own "Open drawer" button.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called when the drawer asks to close (Escape, scrim click, close button).

props.name: side
props.doc: Edge the drawer slides from.

props.name: title
props.doc: Title in the drawer's header bar.

props.name: children
props.doc: Drawer content. Defaults to a Lumen invoice action list.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: Rendered when the drawer is uncontrolled. Defaults to an "Open drawer" button.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the panel.

examples:
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Invoice actions</Button>
<Drawer open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Invoice INV-2041">
  ...actions
</Drawer>

components.name: dropdown-menu
components.title: DropdownMenu
components.description: A menu that opens from a trigger: items with shortcuts, labels, separators, checkbox and radio items, and nested submenus.
components.whenToUse: Built on Base UI Menu: arrow keys move, typeahead jumps, Escape closes and focus returns to the trigger. Use for action menus on a button. For a right-click menu use `ContextMenu`; for an app menu bar use `Menubar`; to pick one value in a form use `Select`; for searchable commands use `CommandPalette`. With no children it renders a sample account menu.
examples:
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Options</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={edit}>Edit<DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘E</DropdownMenuShortcut></DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={remove}>Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>

components.name: due-date-chip
components.title: DueDateChip
components.description: A small calendar chip for a task or invoice due date, with a danger edge when overdue.
components.whenToUse: Use inside issue cards, table cells and list rows. For a relative time ("3 days ago") use `RelativeTime`; for a general status label use `StatusBadge`. The overdue state is announced to screen readers, not only shown in colour.

props.name: date
props.doc: Display text for the date, already formatted, e.g. "Nov 30".

props.name: overdue
props.doc: Mark the date as past due.

examples:
<DueDateChip date="Nov 30" />
<DueDateChip date="Oct 2" overdue />

components.name: editable-heading
components.title: EditableHeading
components.description: A page or document title that is itself a text input, styled as a heading.
components.whenToUse: Use for click-to-rename titles (documents, projects, dashboards). Enter commits and leaves the field, Escape restores the text from when editing began. For an editable table cell use `InlineCellEdit`; for a labelled form field use `Input` inside `FormField`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new text on every keystroke (and on Escape revert).

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown when empty.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Title".

examples:
const [title, setTitle] = React.useState("Q4 revenue review")
<EditableHeading value={title} onChange={setTitle} aria-label="Report title" />

components.name: email-button
components.title: EmailButton
components.description: The primary call-to-action link inside an email template, styled as an ink button.
components.whenToUse: It is an <a>, because email clients follow links, not buttons. Use one per email inside `EmailLayout`. For buttons in the app use `Button`.

props.name: children
props.doc: Button text.

props.name: href
props.doc: Absolute URL the email links to.

examples: <EmailButton href="https://app.example.com/invoices/2041">View invoice</EmailButton>

components.name: email-card
components.title: EmailCard
components.description: A bordered content block inside an email body, with an optional title.
components.whenToUse: Use inside `EmailLayout` to group a receipt summary, a code or a callout. For cards in the app use `Card`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the block.

props.name: children
props.doc: Body text or markup.

examples: <EmailCard title="Invoice INV-2041">$12,400.00 due Nov 30.</EmailCard>

components.name: email-footer
components.title: EmailFooter
components.description: The closing band of an email: sender address plus unsubscribe and preferences links.
components.whenToUse: Use as the last child of `EmailLayout`. Marketing email must carry a working unsubscribe link, so pass real URLs.

props.name: address
props.doc: Postal address or sender line.

props.name: unsubscribeHref
props.doc: URL of the one-click unsubscribe page.

props.name: preferencesHref
props.doc: URL of the email preferences page.

examples:
<EmailFooter
  address="Lumen Inc. · 548 Market St, San Francisco"
  unsubscribeHref="https://app.example.com/unsubscribe?t=abc"
  preferencesHref="https://app.example.com/settings/email"
/>

components.name: email-header
components.title: EmailHeader
components.description: The top band of an email template with the sender's brand name.
components.whenToUse: Use as the first child of `EmailLayout`. Pass `children` to replace the brand text with a logo.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Brand name shown when no children are passed.

props.name: children
props.doc: Custom content, such as a logo image. Replaces the brand text.

examples: <EmailHeader brand="Lumen" />

components.name: email-layout
components.title: EmailLayout
components.description: The 560px email shell that holds header, body, cards and footer.
components.whenToUse: Compose an email preview from `EmailHeader`, `EmailCard`, `EmailButton` and `EmailFooter` inside it, and wrap the whole thing in `EmailPreviewFrame` to show subject and sender. These parts render a preview in the app; inline the styles before sending real mail.

props.name: children
props.doc: Email sections, top to bottom.

examples:
$12,400.00 due Nov 30.
Pay invoice

components.name: email-preview-frame
components.title: EmailPreviewFrame
components.description: An inbox-style frame around an email preview showing the sender and subject line.
components.whenToUse: Use in template editors and notification settings to show what a message will look like. Put an `EmailLayout` inside it.

props.name: subject
props.doc: Subject line.

props.name: from
props.doc: Sender address.

props.name: children
props.doc: The email body, usually an `EmailLayout`.

examples:
<EmailPreviewFrame subject="Your invoice from Lumen" from="billing@lumen.dev">
  <EmailLayout>...</EmailLayout>
</EmailPreviewFrame>

components.name: emoji-picker
components.title: EmojiPicker
components.description: A compact grid of emoji buttons for reactions, with arrow-key navigation and one tab stop.
components.whenToUse: Use inside a `Popover` from a reaction button, or inline under a message. For a row of existing reaction counts use `ReactionBar`. Arrow keys move through the grid, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space picks.

props.name: emojis
props.doc: Emoji characters to offer, in order.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the chosen emoji character.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Number of grid columns; also the Up/Down arrow step.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the group.

examples:
<EmojiPicker onSelect={(emoji) => addReaction(messageId, emoji)} />
<EmojiPicker emojis={["✅", "👀", "🚀"]} columns={3} onSelect={react} />

components.name: empty-search
components.title: EmptySearch
components.description: The "no results" state for a search or filtered list, echoing the query back.
components.whenToUse: Use when a search or filter returns nothing. For a list that has no data yet use `EmptyState` or `EmptyTable`; for a failed request use `ErrorState`.

props.name: query
props.doc: The search text, quoted in the title.

props.name: description
props.doc: Hint under the title.
props.default: "Try a different query or clear filte...

props.name: onClear
props.doc: When set, shows a "Clear search" button that calls it.

examples: <EmptySearch query={query} onClear={() => setQuery("")} />

components.name: empty-state
components.title: EmptyState
components.description: A centred placeholder for a page or panel with nothing in it yet: icon, title, hint and one action.
components.whenToUse: Use for first-run screens ("No invoices yet"). For an empty table body use `EmptyTable`; for zero search results use `EmptySearch`; for a failure use `ErrorState`; for a missing page use `NotFoundState`.

props.name: title
props.doc: One short line saying what is empty.

props.name: description
props.doc: What to do next.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Label of the primary button. The button only renders when this is set.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Called by the primary button.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Decorative icon above the title. A quiet placeholder tile renders when omitted.

examples:
<EmptyState
  icon={<ReceiptIcon className="size-6" />}
  title="No invoices yet"
  description="Create your first invoice to start getting paid."
  actionLabel="New invoice"
  onAction={() => router.push("/invoices/new")}
/>

components.name: empty-table
components.title: EmptyTable
components.description: A sunken placeholder for a table or data grid with no rows yet, with an optional create action.
components.whenToUse: Use in place of the table body when the collection is empty. For a whole empty page use `EmptyState`; for zero filter matches use `EmptySearch`; while rows load use `LoadingTable`.

props.name: title
props.doc: One short line saying what is empty.

props.name: description
props.doc: What to do next.
props.default: "Create your first row to get started."

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Label of the create button. The button only renders when this is set.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Called by the create button.

examples: <EmptyTable title="No customers yet" actionLabel="Add customer" onAction={openCreate} />

components.name: env-badge
components.title: EnvBadge
components.description: A tiny uppercase label naming the deployment environment; production gets a danger edge.
components.whenToUse: Use beside API keys, deploy rows and headers so nobody mistakes prod for staging. To switch environments use `EnvSwitcher`; for general status use `StatusBadge`.

props.name: env
props.doc: Which environment to name.

examples: <EnvBadge env="production" />

components.name: env-switcher
components.title: EnvSwitcher
components.description: A Dev / Staging / Prod segmented control for scoping a console to one environment.
components.whenToUse: Use in a dashboard header or settings page to choose which environment's keys, logs or config are shown. To label a single environment use `EnvBadge`; for other option sets use `SegmentedControl` directly.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled environment: "dev", "staging" or "prod".

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial environment when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with "dev", "staging" or "prod".

examples:
const [env, setEnv] = React.useState("prod")
<EnvSwitcher value={env} onChange={setEnv} />

components.name: error-state
components.title: ErrorState
components.description: A centred failure message for a panel or page that could not load, with an optional retry.
components.whenToUse: It is a role="alert" region, so screen readers announce it when it appears. Use when a fetch fails. For a 5xx page use `ServerErrorState`; for a 404 use `NotFoundState`; for an inline form error use `InlineAlert`; for "no data yet" use `EmptyState`.

props.name: title
props.doc: One short line saying what failed.

props.name: description
props.doc: What happened and what to try.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: When set, shows a retry button that calls it.

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: Label of the retry button.

examples: <ErrorState description="We couldn't load invoices." onRetry={() => refetch()} />

components.name: event-calendar
components.title: EventCalendar
components.description: A week and day event scheduler with overlap layout, an all-day row, a current time line and click to create.
components.whenToUse: Use for meeting and shift schedules. Events are plain objects with Date `start` and `end`; `calendars` set their colours. Click an empty slot (or focus a day column and use Up/Down then Enter) to fire `onCreate`. For a month grid use `CalendarMonth`; for a list of upcoming events use `CalendarAgenda`; for project timelines use `GanttChart`.

props.name: events
props.doc: Events to place. Defaults to a sample Lumen work week around today.

props.name: calendars
props.doc: Calendars that colour events and fill the legend.

props.name: view
props.doc: Controlled view.

props.name: defaultView
props.doc: "auto" picks Day under 600px of width and Week above.

props.name: onViewChange
props.doc: Called when the Week/Day control or a day header changes the view.

props.name: defaultDate
props.doc: Any date inside the first week or day shown. Defaults to today.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.doc: 0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday.

props.name: scrollToHour
props.doc: Hour the grid scrolls to on mount.

props.name: hourHeight
props.doc: Pixel height of one hour row.

props.name: height
props.doc: Pixel height of the scrolling time grid.

props.name: slotMinutes
props.doc: Minutes a click on an empty slot snaps to.

props.name: onCreate
props.doc: Called when an empty slot is clicked or chosen with the keyboard.

props.name: onEventClick
props.doc: Called when an event block is clicked or activated with the keyboard.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for dates and times, e.g. "en-GB".

examples:
<EventCalendar
  events={[{ id: "1", title: "Sprint planning", start: new Date(2026, 10, 16, 11), end: new Date(2026, 10, 16, 12), calendar: "eng" }]}
  calendars={[{ id: "eng", label: "Engineering", tone: "info" }]}
  onCreate={({ start, end }) => openNewEvent(start, end)}
  onEventClick={(ev) => openEvent(ev.id)}
/>

components.name: expandable-row
components.title: ExpandableRow
components.description: A bordered row whose header toggles a details panel underneath (a disclosure).
components.whenToUse:
Use for one collapsible block of extra detail, like a log entry or an invoice line. For several mutually exclusive sections use `Accordion`; for an unstyled show/hide use `Collapsible`.

Controlled: `<ExpandableRow open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="…">`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Header text of the toggle button.

props.name: children
props.doc: Content of the details panel.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called with the next open state.

examples: content-type: application/json

components.name: export-data
components.title: ExportData
components.description: A settings row that explains a data export and offers one button to request it.
components.whenToUse: Use on account or workspace settings pages (GDPR exports, backups). For a destructive action use `DangerZone`; for a download list use `FileList`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the row.

props.name: description
props.doc: What the export contains and how long it takes.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Button label.

props.name: onExport
props.doc: Called when the button is pressed.

examples: <ExportData onExport={() => requestExport()} />

components.name: facet-filter
components.title: FacetFilter
components.description: A titled group of checkbox facets with result counts, for a filter sidebar.
components.whenToUse: Use for multi-select filters in a sidebar or popover. For filter chips in a toolbar use `ChipFilter`; for a single choice use `RadioGroup`; for many options with search use `MultiSelect`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Group heading.

props.name: options
props.doc: Facets to list. Defaults to invoice statuses with counts.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selection.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Selection when uncontrolled. With the sample options, "Open" and "Overdue" start checked.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the full new selection, in toggle order.

components.name: faq-list
components.title: FaqList
components.description: Frequently asked questions as an accordion: one question per row, the answer unfolds beneath it.
components.whenToUse: Use on pricing and marketing pages. Each question is a button inside a heading, so screen reader users can jump between questions. For arbitrary collapsible sections use `Accordion`; for one disclosure use `ExpandableRow`.

props.name: items
props.doc: Question and answer pairs. Defaults to Lumen billing questions.

examples: <FaqList items={[{ q: "Can I cancel anytime?", a: "Yes, from Billing. You keep access until the period ends." }]} />

components.name: feature-flag-toggle
components.title: FeatureFlagToggle
components.description: A bordered row with a flag name, a description and a switch that turns the flag on or off.
components.whenToUse: Use in admin and settings screens for named flags or experiments. The switch is labelled by the name and described by the description. For a plain labelled switch use `Switch` with `label`; for a grid of notification channels use `NotificationPreferences`.

props.name: name
props.doc: Flag name; also the switch's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.doc: What the flag changes.

props.name: checked
props.doc: Controlled on/off state.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.doc: Initial state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: Called with the new state.

examples:
<FeatureFlagToggle
  name="new-invoice-editor"
  description="Roll out the v2 editor to this workspace."
  checked={enabled}
  onCheckedChange={setEnabled}
/>

components.name: feature-grid
components.title: FeatureGrid
components.description: A responsive grid of feature cards, each with an optional icon, a title and a short description.
components.whenToUse: Use on marketing pages to list product capabilities: one column on phones, two on tablets, three on desktop. For an asymmetric showcase use `BentoGrid`; for a plan-by-plan matrix use `PlanComparison`.

props.name: features
props.doc: Cards to show. Defaults to six Lumen features with icons.

examples:
<FeatureGrid
  features={[
    { title: "Invoices in seconds", description: "Draft, send and track from one screen.", icon: <ReceiptIcon className="size-5" /> },
    { title: "Automatic reminders", description: "Nudges stop the moment a payment lands." },
  ]}
/>

components.name: feedback-thumbs
components.title: FeedbackThumbs
components.description: A pair of thumbs up / thumbs down toggle buttons for rating an answer or article.
components.whenToUse: Use under AI responses and help articles. Pressing the active thumb again clears the vote (value becomes null). For message actions like copy and retry use `MessageActions`; for star ratings use `Rating`; for up/down vote counts use `VoteControl`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled vote. null means no vote.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial vote when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new vote, or null when cleared.

examples: <FeedbackThumbs onChange={(v) => track("answer_feedback", { vote: v })} />

components.name: file-dropzone
components.title: FileDropzone
components.description: A drag-and-drop upload zone with accept/reject drag states, type and size validation, and a file list with progress, retry and remove.
components.whenToUse:
Click, Enter or Space opens the file picker; dropping works too. Pass `upload` to stream progress per file; without it files are listed as done at once and handed to `onFiles`. For a single avatar use `AvatarUpload`; for an image with preview and crop use `ImageUpload` or `ImageCropper`; for listing existing files use `FileList`.

GOLD STANDARD COMPONENT. Four designed states (rest, hover, drag-accept, drag-reject); the hairline dashed border is SVG so the dashes stay crisp and march while dragging.

props.name: onFiles
props.doc: Called with accepted files every time files are added.

props.name: upload
props.doc: Optional uploader. Call onProgress(0..1) as bytes go out; throw to fail. Without it, files are listed as done immediately.

props.name: accept
props.doc: Same syntax as <input accept>: MIME types, wildcards and extensions, e.g. "image/*,.pdf".

props.name: multiple
props.doc: Allow several files at once. When false, a new file replaces the previous one.

props.name: maxSize
props.doc: Largest accepted file, in bytes. Larger files are listed with an error.

props.name: maxFiles
props.doc: Most files the list will hold. Extra files are ignored.

props.name: showList
props.doc: Show the file list under the zone.

props.name: label
props.doc: Main line inside the zone.

props.name: hint
props.doc: Secondary line. Defaults to the accepted types and max size.

examples:
<FileDropzone
  accept="image/*,.pdf"
  maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024}
  upload={(file, onProgress) => uploadToS3(file, onProgress)}
  onFiles={(files) => console.log(files)}
/>

components.name: file-list
components.title: FileList
components.description: A stack of file rows with name, metadata and an optional download action.
components.whenToUse: Use for attachments, exports and documents on a record. For one row use `FileRow`; for uploading use `FileDropzone`; for a folder hierarchy use `FileTree`.

props.name: files
props.doc: Files to list. Defaults to a few Lumen documents.

props.name: onDownload
props.doc: Called with the file id. When present, each row shows a download button (the sample files show one regardless).

examples:
<FileList
  files={[{ id: "f1", name: "INV-2041.pdf", meta: "PDF · 184 KB" }]}
  onDownload={(id) => download(id)}
/>

components.name: file-reference
components.title: FileReference
components.description: A compact chip-like card citing a source file: name, path and a line range.
components.whenToUse: Use in agent and code-review UIs to show which file and lines an answer or change refers to. For a web citation use `CitationChip` or `SourceCard`; for a downloadable file use `FileRow`.

props.name: name
props.doc: File name, shown bold.

props.name: path
props.doc: Full path, shown in mono under the name.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Line range, e.g. "1–92" or "L42".

examples: <FileReference name="billing.ts" path="src/lib/billing.ts" lines="42–68" />

components.name: file-row
components.title: FileRow
components.description: One file as a bordered row: icon, name, metadata line and an optional download button.
components.whenToUse: Use alone for a single attachment, or let `FileList` render a stack. For an attachment pill in a composer use `AttachmentChip`; for upload progress use `FileDropzone`.

props.name: name
props.doc: File name, truncated when long.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Secondary line, e.g. "PDF · 184 KB".

props.name: onDownload
props.doc: When set, shows a download icon button labelled "Download {name}".

examples: <FileRow name="Q3-revenue-report.xlsx" meta="Spreadsheet · 1.2 MB" onDownload={() => download("q3")} />

components.name: file-tree
components.title: FileTree
components.description: A code editor style file explorer with file icons, git status, a filter field and full tree keyboard support.
components.whenToUse: Use for repos, artifacts and agent workspaces. Folders are nodes with a `children` array (even empty); files have none. Paths passed to `onSelect` are names joined by "/". Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern. For a generic nested list without file semantics use `TreeView`; for a single file citation use `FileReference`.

props.name: data
props.doc: Nested files and folders. Paths are built from names joined by "/".

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.doc: Folder paths open on first render.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Controlled selected path.

props.name: activePath
props.doc: The file open in the editor. Defaults to the last selected file.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the path of a file or folder when it is selected.

props.name: searchable
props.doc: Show the filter field above the tree.

props.name: showStatus
props.doc: Show git status letters and folder change dots.

props.name: sort
props.doc: Sort folders first, then names alphabetically.

props.name: title
props.doc: Header title, usually the project name. Pass an empty string to hide the header.

examples:
<FileTree
  title="lumen-web"
  data={[{ name: "app", children: [{ name: "page.tsx", status: "M" }] }, { name: "package.json" }]}
  defaultExpanded={["app"]}
  onSelect={(path) => openFile(path)}
/>

components.name: filter-bar
components.title: FilterBar
components.description: A toolbar strip with a filter text field, slots for filter controls and an optional Clear button.
components.whenToUse: Use above a list or table. Put `Select`, `ChipFilter` or `MultiSelect` controls in `children`. For a full table toolbar with bulk actions use `TableToolbar`; for audit logs use `AuditFilterBar`.

props.name: children
props.doc: Filter controls rendered after the text field.

props.name: query
props.doc: Controlled filter text. Leave out for an uncontrolled field.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.doc: Called with the filter text on every keystroke and when cleared.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Placeholder of the text field.

props.name: onClear
props.doc: When set, shows a "Clear" button at the end that calls it.

examples:
const [q, setQ] = React.useState("")
<FilterBar query={q} onQueryChange={setQ} onClear={() => setQ("")}>
  <Select ... />
</FilterBar>

components.name: floating-action-button
components.title: FloatingActionButton
components.description: A round, fixed-position primary button in the bottom-right corner of the viewport.
components.whenToUse: Use for the one primary action of a mobile or canvas screen ("New invoice"). Takes every `Button` prop. An icon-only FAB must have an `aria-label`. For an inline primary action use `Button`; for a sticky bottom action bar use `StickyBar`.
examples:
<FloatingActionButton aria-label="New invoice" onClick={create}>
  <PlusIcon />
</FloatingActionButton>

components.name: floating-label-input
components.title: FloatingLabelInput
components.description: A text field whose label rests inside the input and floats onto the top border on focus or once filled.
components.whenToUse: Pass `label` for one field (input, or textarea with `multiline`). Without `label` it renders a small sign-up form built from `fields`. The label is a real <label>; `error` sets aria-invalid and is announced. For a classic label-above field use `Input` inside `FormField`; for passwords use `PasswordInput`; for formatted values use `MaskedInput`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The field label. When omitted, the `fields` form is rendered instead.

props.name: multiline
props.doc: Render a textarea instead of an input.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Textarea rows when `multiline`.

props.name: type
props.doc: Input type, e.g. "email", "tel", "url". Ignored when `multiline`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new text on every keystroke.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Icon shown at the start of the field (inputs only).

props.name: hint
props.doc: Helper text under the field, linked with aria-describedby.

props.name: error
props.doc: Error message. Marks the field invalid and replaces the hint.

props.name: fields
props.doc: Fields of the sample form rendered when no `label` is passed.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the form values when the sample form is submitted and valid.

components.name: footer-mega
components.title: FooterMega
components.description: A multi-column site footer: brand and tagline on the left, titled link columns across the rest.
components.whenToUse: Use at the bottom of marketing sites with many links. Each column is a labelled nav landmark. For a single row of links use `FooterNav`.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Link columns after the brand block. Defaults to three Lumen columns.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Brand name shown in the first column.

props.name: tagline
props.doc: Short line under the brand name.

examples:
<FooterMega
  brand="Lumen"
  tagline="Invoicing for teams that close their books every day."
  columns={[{ title: "Product", links: [{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing" }] }]}
/>

components.name: footer-nav
components.title: FooterNav
components.description: A one-line site footer: brand on the left, a row of quiet links on the right.
components.whenToUse: Use for app and docs footers with a handful of links. For a marketing footer with titled link columns use `FooterMega`.

props.name: links
props.doc: Links in the footer nav. Defaults to a typical set for Lumen.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Brand name on the left.

examples: <FooterNav brand="Lumen" links={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Status", href: "https://status.example.com" }]} />

components.name: forgot-password-form
components.title: ForgotPasswordForm
components.description: An auth card asking for an email address to send a password reset link to.
components.whenToUse: A real <form>: Enter submits, the browser checks the email format, and `onSubmit` receives the trimmed address. For setting the new password use `ResetPasswordForm`; for passwordless sign-in use `MagicLinkForm`.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the email address on submit. Return a promise to show a pending state until it settles.

props.name: title
props.doc: Card heading.

props.name: description
props.doc: Line under the heading.
props.default: "We'll email you a link to reset it."

examples: <ForgotPasswordForm onSubmit={async (email) => await sendResetLink(email)} />

components.name: form-field
components.title: FormField
components.description: A label, a control, and a description or error message stacked with the right spacing and wiring.
components.whenToUse: Pass the control's `id` as `id`. When the child is a single element, FormField links it to the description or error with `aria-describedby` and sets `aria-invalid` while there is an error, so screen readers read the message. Use around `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select` and friends. For a label that floats inside the input use `FloatingLabelInput`.

props.name: id
props.doc: The control's id; the label points at it.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label.

props.name: description
props.doc: Help text under the control. Hidden while there is an error.

props.name: error
props.doc: Error message. Replaces the description and marks the control invalid.

props.name: required
props.doc: Adds a visual asterisk. Also set `required` on the control itself.

props.name: children
props.doc: The control, usually one element with the same `id`.

examples:
<FormField id="email" label="Work email" description="We send invoices here." error={errors.email} required>
  <Input id="email" type="email" required />
</FormField>

components.name: funnel-chart
components.title: FunnelChart
components.description: A funnel chart with stage bars laid out horizontally or vertically, conversion rates and drop-off between stages, an optional comparison series and bars that spring to new values when the data changes.
components.whenToUse: Use for signup and checkout funnels. Pass `stages` for one series, or `datasets` to add a segmented switch between them. Screen readers get a full data table. For a compact list of bars use `FunnelSteps`; for flows that branch use `SankeyChart`.

props.name: stages
props.doc: Stages from the top of the funnel down.

props.name: datasets
props.doc: Datasets to switch between with a segmented control. Ignored when `stages` is set.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: "auto" is horizontal when the container is at least 480px wide, vertical below that.

props.name: title
props.doc: Chart title; also the figure's accessible name.

props.name: compareLabel
props.doc: Legend text for the comparison series.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats values in the bars and the table.

props.name: showCompare
props.doc: Draw the comparison outline when stages carry `compare`.

examples:
<FunnelChart
  title="Visitors to paid"
  stages={[
    { label: "Visitors", value: 48200, compare: 44100 },
    { label: "Signed up", value: 12840, compare: 11200 },
    { label: "Paid", value: 1464, compare: 1210 },
  ]}
/>

components.name: funnel-steps
components.title: FunnelSteps
components.description: A compact conversion funnel as stacked bars, each sized against the largest step.
components.whenToUse: Use in a card or sidebar for a quick funnel readout. For a full chart with step conversion rates, drop-off, a comparison period and dataset switching use `FunnelChart`; for arbitrary categories use `HorizontalBarChart`.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Funnel stages, top to bottom. Defaults to a Lumen signup funnel.

examples: <FunnelSteps steps={[{ label: "Visited", value: 12840 }, { label: "Signed up", value: 3210 }, { label: "Paid", value: 464 }]} />

components.name: gantt-chart
components.title: GanttChart
components.description: A project timeline with day and week scales, a today line, progress fills, dependency arrows, a sticky task column and focusable bars.
components.whenToUse: Use for launch plans and delivery schedules. Tasks take Date objects or ISO day strings; `end` is inclusive. Tasks with the same `group` share a heading and colour; `dependsOn` draws arrows. For a single plain bar row use `GanttRow`; for calendar events by the hour use `EventCalendar`; for request spans use `TraceWaterfall`.

props.name: tasks
props.doc: Tasks to plot. Defaults to a six week Lumen launch plan built around today.

props.name: scale
props.doc: Controlled zoom level.

props.name: defaultScale
props.doc: Initial zoom level when uncontrolled.

props.name: onScaleChange
props.doc: Called when the Day/Week control changes the scale.

props.name: today
props.doc: The date the today line marks. Defaults to the current date.

props.name: padDays
props.doc: Empty days drawn before the first and after the last task.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading above the chart. Empty hides the header row.

props.name: nameWidth
props.doc: Width of the sticky task column in px.

props.name: onTaskClick
props.doc: Called when a bar is clicked or activated with the keyboard.

examples:
<GanttChart
  title="Launch plan"
  tasks={[
    { id: "design", name: "Landing page design", start: "2026-11-02", end: "2026-11-09", progress: 60, group: "Design" },
    { id: "build", name: "Checkout flow", start: "2026-11-10", end: "2026-11-20", group: "Engineering", dependsOn: ["design"] },
  ]}
  onTaskClick={(task) => openTask(task.id)}
/>

components.name: gantt-row
components.title: GanttRow
components.description: One labelled timeline row with a bar placed from `start` to `end` on a 0..max scale.
components.whenToUse: Use for a lightweight schedule built from a few rows (sprints, rollouts) where positions are plain numbers such as day indexes or percentages. For real dates, dependencies, scales and a today line use `GanttChart`; for nested spans of a trace use `TraceWaterfall`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Task name in the left column.

props.name: start
props.doc: Bar start on the 0..max scale.

props.name: end
props.doc: Bar end on the 0..max scale.

props.name: max
props.doc: Length of the whole scale.

examples:
<GanttRow label="Billing API" start={10} end={45} />
<GanttRow label="QA" start={20} end={26} max={30} />

components.name: gauge-chart
components.title: GaugeChart
components.description: A half-circle dial filled to a percentage of `max`, with the percentage inside and a caption below.
components.whenToUse: Use for one bounded score (health, quota, NPS-style index). For a full ring use `DonutChart`; for a goal ring with a target use `GoalRing`; for a linear labelled bar use `Meter`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Current value, clamped to 0..max.

props.name: max
props.doc: Value that fills the dial.

props.name: label
props.doc: Caption under the dial; also used in the accessible name.

examples:
<GaugeChart value={72} label="Uptime score" />
<GaugeChart value={41} max={50} label="Seats" />

components.name: goal-ring
components.title: GoalRing
components.description: A circular progress ring for one goal, with the percentage in the centre and a caption below.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a single target read at a glance (weekly goal, quota met). For a linear bar use Progress, for a bounded measurement use Meter, and for several values in one ring use RadialChart.

props.name: value
props.doc: Progress from 0 to 100. Values outside the range are clamped.

props.name: label
props.doc: Caption under the ring; also the accessible name.

examples: <GoalRing value={72} label="Weekly goal" />

components.name: heading
components.title: Heading
components.description: A semantic h1 to h6 with the kit's size, weight and tracking for each level.
components.whenToUse: Use it for in-app section and page headings. For a page title with actions use PageHeader, for a section intro with eyebrow and description use SectionHeader, and for marketing headlines use Hero.

props.name: as
props.doc: Which heading element to render; the level also sets the size. Pick by document outline, restyle with className.

examples: <Heading as="h3">Billing</Heading>

components.name: health-indicator
components.title: HealthIndicator
components.description: A coloured dot and a word for a service's health: operational, degraded or down.
components.whenToUse: Use it inline in tables and status lists. For a tinted pill use StatusBadge, for a bare dot use StatusDot, and for a history strip use UptimeBar.

props.name: status
props.doc: Health state; sets the dot colour (success, warning, danger).

props.name: label
props.doc: Text beside the dot. Defaults to the status word, capitalised.

examples: <HealthIndicator status="degraded" label="API" />

components.name: heatmap-cell
components.title: HeatmapCell
components.description: One square of a heatmap, tinted from sunken to accent by intensity.
components.whenToUse: Use it to build custom grids (activity by hour, usage by day). For a ready year of daily cells use StreakCalendar.

props.name: intensity
props.doc: Strength from 0 to 1; clamped. 0 is the sunken surface, 1 is full accent.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name and tooltip, for example the date and count. Defaults to the intensity as a percentage.

examples: <HeatmapCell intensity={0.6} label="Tue 14:00, 42 runs" />

components.name: hero
components.title: Hero
components.description: A centred marketing headline with an optional eyebrow, description and up to two calls to action.
components.whenToUse: Use it at the top of a landing or product page. For an in-app page title use PageHeader, for a mid-page section intro use SectionHeader, and for a closing call to action use CtaBanner.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Short line above the title, for example a release or category.

props.name: title
props.doc: The headline, rendered as the page's h1.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences under the headline.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: Solid ink button.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: Outline button beside the primary one.

examples:
<Hero
  eyebrow="New in 2.4"
  title="Invoices that chase themselves"
  description="Reminders, retries and receipts on autopilot."
  primaryAction={{ label: "Start free", href: "/signup" }}
  secondaryAction={{ label: "Book a demo", onClick: openDemo }}
/>

components.name: horizontal-bar-chart
components.title: HorizontalBarChart
components.description: Labelled horizontal bars scaled to the largest value, for ranking categories at a glance.
components.whenToUse: Use it for top-N lists with long labels (customers, pages, endpoints). For values over time use BarChart or AreaChart, and for parts of a whole use StackedBarChart or DonutChart.

props.name: data
props.doc: One bar per entry, in display order. Defaults to invoices per customer.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats the value shown at the end of each bar. Defaults to the plain number.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the chart.

examples: <HorizontalBarChart label="Invoices by customer" data={[{ label: "Northwind", value: 124 }, { label: "Globex", value: 52 }]} />

components.name: hover-card
components.title: HoverCard
components.description: A rich preview that opens when the pointer rests on, or focus lands in, its trigger.
components.whenToUse: Built on Base UI Preview Card: it waits before opening, stays open while the pointer moves onto the card, flips to stay on screen and closes on Escape. Use it for supplementary detail (a person, a record, a link). Anything the user must act on belongs in a Popover; a short text hint belongs in a Tooltip. The trigger should be a link or button so keyboard users can reach it.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The element that opens the card, ideally a link or button.

props.name: children
props.doc: Card content.

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side of the trigger the card opens on. It flips if there is no room.

props.name: align
props.doc: Alignment along that side.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Milliseconds to wait before opening.

props.name: closeDelay
props.doc: Milliseconds to wait before closing once the pointer leaves.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the card opens or closes.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the card panel.

examples:
Maya Chen}>

Maya Chen

Finance lead

components.name: icon-button
components.title: IconButton
components.description: A square Button that holds only an icon and requires an aria-label.
components.whenToUse: Use it for toolbar and row actions (close, more, delete). When the action needs a visible word, use Button with an icon and text instead; pair an IconButton with a Tooltip when the icon alone is not obvious.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Required: the icon has no text, so this is the button's only name.

props.name: size
props.doc: Square size: 28, 32, 36 (default) or 44px.

props.name: children
props.doc: The icon, for example a lucide-react icon. Sized to the button automatically.

examples: <IconButton aria-label="Delete invoice" variant="ghost" size="icon-sm"><TrashIcon /></IconButton>

components.name: image-cropper
components.title: ImageCropper
components.description: Crop an image inside a frame: drag to pan, zoom with the slider, wheel or pinch, pick an aspect, mask to a circle and rotate in 90° steps.
components.whenToUse: Use it before uploading a cover, avatar or product photo. onCrop reports the crop in source pixels; getCroppedBlob(src, rect, opts) renders it to a Blob for upload. For picking a file without framing use ImageUpload, and for a round avatar picker use AvatarUpload. Keyboard: arrows pan (Shift for bigger steps), + and - zoom, R rotates, 0 resets.

props.name: src
props.doc: Image URL or data URI. Remote images need CORS headers for getCroppedBlob.

props.name: aspects
props.doc: Aspect presets offered, as "w:h".

props.name: defaultCircle
props.doc: Start with the circular avatar mask on.

props.name: allowCircle
props.doc: Offer the circular mask toggle.

props.name: maxZoom
props.doc: Largest zoom, as a multiple of the size that just covers the frame.

props.name: showPreview
props.doc: Show the live preview and crop details beside the frame.

props.name: onCrop
props.type: (rect: CropRect, info: { aspect: Aspect; circle: boolean }) => void
props.doc: Called with the crop in source pixels once an interaction settles.

props.name: fileName
props.doc: File name used by the export button.

components.name: image-gallery
components.title: ImageGallery
components.description: A square-tile image grid, two columns on phones and three from the small breakpoint up.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a static set of photos or screenshots. For mixed heights use MasonryGrid, for one image at a time use Carousel, and to open a tile full screen wrap it in ImageLightbox.

props.name: images
props.doc: Images to tile, each with alt text. Defaults to six illustrated landscapes.

examples: <ImageGallery images={[{ src: "/a.jpg", alt: "Front of the store" }, { src: "/b.jpg", alt: "Checkout counter" }]} />

components.name: image-lightbox
components.title: ImageLightbox
components.description: A thumbnail that opens the full image in a modal viewer.
components.whenToUse: Built on Base UI Dialog: focus moves into the viewer and returns to the thumbnail on close, Escape and a click on the backdrop close it, and the page behind does not scroll. Use it to enlarge one image; for a grid of tiles use ImageGallery, and for paging through many images use Carousel.

props.name: src
props.doc: Image URL or data URI, used for both the thumbnail and the full view.

props.name: alt
props.doc: Describes the image; also names the viewer for screen readers.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the viewer opens or closes.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the thumbnail wrapper.

examples: <ImageLightbox src="/receipt.png" alt="Scanned receipt for INV-2041" />

components.name: image-upload
components.title: ImageUpload
components.description: A single-image picker: a drop zone that turns into a preview with a remove button.
components.whenToUse:
Use it for one cover, logo or photo. For a round profile picture use AvatarUpload, for several files of any type use FileDropzone, and to let the user frame the picture before saving use ImageCropper.

The preview uses an object URL that the component revokes when the image is replaced, removed or unmounted; upload the File from onChange, not the URL.

props.name: value
props.doc: Current image URL (controlled). Pass null to show the drop zone.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (url: string | null, file?: File | null) => void
props.doc: Called with a local preview URL and the File when an image is chosen, and with (null, null) when it is removed.

props.name: maxSize
props.doc: Largest accepted file in bytes. Defaults to 5 MB.

props.name: alt
props.doc: Alt text for the preview image.

examples: <ImageUpload value={coverUrl} onChange={(url, file) => { setCoverUrl(url); if (file) upload(file) }} />

components.name: impersonation-banner
components.title: ImpersonationBanner
components.description: A full-width strip that tells a support agent whose account they are viewing, with an Exit button.
components.whenToUse: Mount it at the very top of the app shell while impersonating. For system incidents use IncidentBanner, for trials use TrialBanner, and for general announcements use AnnouncementBar.

props.name: user
props.doc: Name or email of the account being viewed.

props.name: onExit
props.doc: Called when the Exit button is pressed; end the impersonation session here.

props.name: exitLabel
props.doc: Text of the exit button.

examples: <ImpersonationBanner user="maya@northwind.com" onExit={stopImpersonating} />

components.name: incident-banner
components.title: IncidentBanner
components.description: A full-width strip announcing an ongoing incident, its severity, and a link to the status page.
components.whenToUse: Use it at the top of an app or dashboard during an outage. For a dismissible product announcement use AnnouncementBar, for a message inside a page use InlineAlert or Callout, and for a service's current state use HealthIndicator.

props.name: title
props.doc: One line describing the incident.

props.name: severity
props.doc: Sets the dot colour: minor is accent, major is warning, critical is danger.

props.name: href
props.doc: Status page URL; the link is hidden when empty.

props.name: linkLabel
props.doc: Text of the status page link.

examples: <IncidentBanner severity="critical" title="Payments are failing in eu-west" href="https://status.example.com" />

components.name: infinite-scroll
components.title: InfiniteScroll
components.description: A scrolling list that loads the next page when a sentinel near the end comes into view.
components.whenToUse: It uses IntersectionObserver, never fires twice for the same page, shows a loading row and an end-of-list message, keeps a real "Load more" button as the accessible fallback, and offers Retry when a page fails. Use it for feeds of unknown length. For thousands of rows already in memory use VirtualList, and for numbered pages use Pagination.

props.name: loadMore
props.type: (page: number) => Promise<{ items: T[]; hasMore: boolean }>
props.doc: Fetch a page (0-based); return its items and whether more remain. Throw to show Retry.

props.name: renderItem
props.doc: Renders one item. Each is wrapped in an li.

props.name: rootMargin
props.doc: How far before the end to start loading, as a CSS margin.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the list.

examples:
<InfiniteScroll
  loadMore={async (page) => {
    const res = await fetch(`/api/orders?page=${page}`).then((r) => r.json())
    return { items: res.orders, hasMore: res.hasMore }
  }}
  renderItem={(order) => <OrderRow order={order} />}
/>

components.name: inline-alert
components.title: InlineAlert
components.description: A bordered message inside the page flow, with a tone icon, an optional title and body text.
components.whenToUse:
Use it next to the thing it is about (a form, a settings section). For a tinted aside in prose use Callout, for a page-wide strip use Banner or AnnouncementBar, and for a transient confirmation use Toast.

Danger and warning alerts use role="alert" so screen readers announce them when they appear; neutral and success use role="status", which is polite.

props.name: title
props.doc: Bold first line.

props.name: children
props.doc: Body text or inline content.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Sets the icon, the icon colour and the border colour.

examples: <InlineAlert tone="warning" title="Action needed">Add a payment method to keep access.</InlineAlert>

components.name: inline-cell-edit
components.title: InlineCellEdit
components.description: A table cell value that turns into a text field on click; Enter or blur saves, Escape cancels.
components.whenToUse: Use it for quick edits inside DataTable or Table rows. For a heading edited in place use EditableHeading, and for multi-field edits open a Dialog or Sheet with a form.

props.name: value
props.doc: The saved value shown when not editing.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new text when the edit is committed (Enter or blur), only if it changed.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the button and the field, for example the column name.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown when the value is empty.

examples: <InlineCellEdit value={row.name} label="Customer name" onChange={(name) => save(row.id, { name })} />

components.name: inline-code-diff
components.title: InlineCodeDiff
components.description: One removed line above one added line, for showing a small code or config change.
components.whenToUse: Use it in reviews, changelogs and agent tool results to show a single edit. For a whole file or several hunks use DiffView.

props.name: before
props.doc: The old line, shown with a minus.

props.name: after
props.doc: The new line, shown with a plus.

examples: <InlineCodeDiff before='timeout: 30' after='timeout: 60' />

components.name: input-affix
components.title: InputAffix
components.description: A text Input with icons or text fixed inside the field before or after the value.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a search icon, a currency sign, a unit, a domain suffix or a trailing button. For money with formatting use CurrencyInput, for a search field with clear and results use SearchInput, and for a plain field use Input. All Input props (value, onChange, size, aria-invalid…) pass to the inner input.

props.name: leading
props.doc: Content before the value: an icon or short text such as "$" or "https://".

props.name: trailing
props.doc: Content after the value: an icon, a unit, a suffix or a small button.

props.name: containerClassName
props.doc: Classes for the outer field box; className goes to the inner input.

examples:
<InputAffix leading={<SearchIcon />} placeholder="Search invoices" aria-label="Search invoices" />
<InputAffix trailing=".minidev.pro" defaultValue="acme" aria-label="Subdomain" />

components.name: input
components.title: Input
components.description: A single-line text field on Base UI Input, with hover, focus halo, invalid, disabled and read-only states.
components.whenToUse: Use it for any short text, email, number or password value; give it a Label (or wrap it in FormField) or an aria-label. For icons or units inside the field use InputAffix, for multi-line text use Textarea, and for specialised values use PasswordInput, SearchInput, NumberInput, CurrencyInput or OtpInput. Mark errors with aria-invalid so the border turns danger.
examples:
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" placeholder="you@company.com" aria-invalid={!!error} />

components.name: inset
components.title: Inset
components.description: A sunken, bordered well that sets content below the surrounding surface.
components.whenToUse: Use it inside a card or panel to hold secondary content (a code sample, an embedded preview, read-only details). For a raised container use Card, and for a padded note block with body text styles use Well.
examples: No payouts yet.

components.name: integration-card
components.title: IntegrationCard
components.description: A third-party integration with its name, a one-line description, a Connected or Available badge and a Connect or Manage button.
components.whenToUse: Use it in an integrations or app directory grid. For an account the user has already linked (with its identity and a disconnect action) use ConnectedAccount, and for single sign-on providers use SsoProviderCard.

props.name: name
props.doc: Integration name, also used to name the action button for screen readers.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line about what the integration does.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Logo or icon shown before the name.

props.name: connected
props.doc: Connected shows "Manage"; otherwise "Connect".

props.name: onConnect
props.doc: Called by the Connect button.

props.name: onManage
props.doc: Called by the Manage button.

examples: <IntegrationCard name="Slack" description="Post invoice events to a channel." icon={<SlackLogo />} connected onManage={openSettings} />

components.name: interactive-area-chart
components.title: InteractiveAreaChart
components.description: An area chart you scrub with the pointer or arrow keys; a crosshair pins the value and its change against a comparison line.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one headline series over time with an optional "last period" line (revenue, signups). For a static area use AreaChart, for several lines use LineChart, and for a tiny inline trend use StatSparkline. Keyboard: Left and Right step through points, Home and End jump to the ends.

props.name: data
props.doc: Points in order, left to right. Defaults to twelve months of revenue.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats values in the header and for screen readers.

props.name: label
props.doc: Series name, shown in the header and legend and used as the accessible name.

props.name: compareLabel
props.doc: Name of the comparison series.

examples:
<InteractiveAreaChart
  label="Revenue"
  compareLabel="Last year"
  format={(n) => `$${n}k`}
  data={[{ label: "Jan", value: 42, compare: 38 }, { label: "Feb", value: 47, compare: 40 }]}
/>

components.name: invite-members
components.title: InviteMembers
components.description: A card with an email field that sends workspace invites and lists the ones still pending.
components.whenToUse:
Use it in team settings or onboarding. For managing existing members and seats use SeatManager or TeamMemberRow, for CSV uploads use BulkUserImport, and for the invitee's side use JoinWorkspace.

Works uncontrolled out of the box; pass `pending` and handle `onInvite` to keep the list in your own state.

props.name: title
props.doc: Card title.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title.
props.default: "They get free UI access. Premium unl...

props.name: pending
props.doc: Pending invite emails (controlled).

props.name: defaultPending
props.doc: Initial pending emails when uncontrolled.

props.name: onInvite
props.doc: Called with a valid, new email when the form is submitted.

examples: <InviteMembers pending={invites} onInvite={(email) => api.invite(email)} />

components.name: invoice-detail
components.title: InvoiceDetail
components.description: One invoice as a card: number, dates and status on top, line items below, total at the foot.
components.whenToUse: Use it on an invoice page or in a side panel. For many invoices use InvoiceList, for a payment confirmation use Receipt, and for a cart before payment use OrderSummary or CheckoutSummary. Amounts are preformatted strings so you control currency and locale.

props.name: id
props.doc: Invoice number.

props.name: date
props.doc: Issue date, already formatted.

props.name: amount
props.doc: Invoice total, already formatted.

props.name: status
props.doc: paid is success, open is warning, void is neutral.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Line items. Defaults to a Northwind invoice from Lumen.

examples: <InvoiceDetail id="INV-2041" status="paid" amount="$1,246.00" lines={[{ label: "Growth plan", amount: "$1,246.00" }]} />

components.name: invoice-list
components.title: InvoiceList
components.description: A compact list of invoices: number and date on the left, amount and status badge on the right.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a billing history or a customer's recent invoices. For one invoice with line items use InvoiceDetail; for sorting, filtering and selection use DataTable.

props.name: items
props.doc: Invoices, newest first. Defaults to recent Lumen invoices.

examples: <InvoiceList items={[{ id: "INV-2041", date: "Sep 24, 2026", amount: "$12,400.00", status: "open" }]} />

components.name: ip-allowlist
components.title: IpAllowlist
