components.description: An editable list of IP addresses and CIDR ranges allowed to reach an account or API key.
components.whenToUse: Type an IPv4 or IPv6 address, optionally with a /prefix, and press Enter or Add; bad and duplicate entries are rejected with a message. Use it in security settings. For free-form tags use TagsInput; for API keys use ApiKeyList. Always validate again on the server.

props.name: value
props.doc: Allowed entries (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial entries when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the full list after an add or remove.

examples: <IpAllowlist value={ips} onChange={setIps} />

components.name: issue-card
components.title: IssueCard
components.description: A tracker issue as a card: key, status and priority badges, title and a meta line.
components.whenToUse: Use it in kanban columns, search results and linked-issue lists. For just the key use IssueKey, and for a full board use KanbanBoard.

props.name: id
props.doc: Issue key, for example "LUM-412".

props.name: status
props.doc: Workflow state, shown as a badge.

props.name: priority
props.doc: Priority, shown as a badge.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Line under the title: assignee, update time or labels.

examples: <IssueCard id="LUM-412" title="Add VAT reverse charge" status="In review" priority="Urgent" meta="Priya Raman · updated 2h ago" />

components.name: issue-key
components.title: IssueKey
components.description: A monospace tracker key such as LUM-412, as text or as a link to the issue.
components.whenToUse: Use it in commit rows, comments and tables wherever an issue is referenced. For the whole issue use IssueCard; for copyable IDs use CopyId.

props.name: value
props.doc: The key text.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the key a link.

examples: <IssueKey value="LUM-412" href="/issues/LUM-412" />

components.name: join-workspace
components.title: JoinWorkspace
components.description: A card where an invited user enters an invite code to join a team workspace.
components.whenToUse: Use it on an onboarding or "join your team" screen. For creating a new workspace use WorkspaceCreate, for the admin's side use InviteMembers, and for switching between workspaces use OrgSwitcher.

props.name: onJoin
props.doc: Called with the trimmed code on submit. Return a promise to show the pending state; throw an Error to show its message.

examples: <JoinWorkspace onJoin={async (code) => { await api.join(code) }} />

components.name: json-viewer
components.title: JsonViewer
components.description: A collapsible JSON tree with syntax colours, item counts, copy value and copy path, search highlighting and full keyboard navigation.
components.whenToUse: Use it for API responses, webhook payloads, tool-call results and debug panels. For JSON as plain highlighted text use CodeBlock, for tabular results use SqlResultTable, and for a file hierarchy use FileTree. Keyboard: arrows walk and fold the tree, Home and End jump, Enter toggles, C copies the focused value and P copies its path.

props.name: value
props.doc: Any JSON serialisable value. Defaults to a Lumen invoice API response.

props.name: title
props.doc: Label shown in the header, for example the request that produced the data. Pass an empty string to hide the header.

props.name: rootName
props.doc: Key shown on the root row. Empty hides it.

props.name: defaultExpandDepth
props.doc: Containers at or above this depth start open. The root is depth 0.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.doc: Extra container paths that start open, in `$.a.b[0]` form.

props.name: toolbar
props.doc: Show the search field and expand or collapse all buttons.

props.name: maxStringLength
props.doc: Longest string shown inline before it is cut with an ellipsis.

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called after a value or path is copied.

examples: <JsonViewer value={response} title="GET /v1/invoices/inv_8f3a2c" defaultExpandDepth={1} />

components.name: kanban-board
components.title: KanbanBoard
components.description: Columns of cards in a horizontally scrolling board, each column headed by its title and card count.
components.whenToUse: Use it to show work by stage from plain data. It is read-only; to compose your own columns with custom cards use KanbanColumn and IssueCard, and for reordering within one list use SortableList.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Columns left to right, each with its cards. Defaults to a Lumen engineering board.

examples: <KanbanBoard columns={[{ id: "todo", title: "To do", cards: [{ id: "1", title: "Export payouts", meta: "LUM-418" }] }]} />

components.name: kanban-column
components.title: KanbanColumn
components.description: One titled column of a board with an optional count badge; you supply the cards as children.
components.whenToUse: Use it to compose a custom board with your own cards (often IssueCard). For a board rendered from data in one call use KanbanBoard.

props.name: title
props.doc: Column heading, also the section's accessible name.

props.name: count
props.doc: Number shown in a badge beside the title.

props.name: children
props.doc: The cards.

examples:
<KanbanColumn title="In review" count={2}>
  <IssueCard id="LUM-397" title="Multi-currency totals" />
</KanbanColumn>

components.name: kbd
components.title: Kbd
components.description: A physical keycap for a key name or symbol: surface, hairline and a 1px key edge.
components.whenToUse: Use it inline in text, menus and tooltips to show a shortcut; group a combo with KbdGroup. For a searchable list of every shortcut use KeyboardShortcuts or ShortcutCheatSheet.
examples: <KbdGroup><Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd></KbdGroup>

components.name: keyboard-shortcuts
components.title: KeyboardShortcuts
components.description: A searchable shortcuts cheat sheet in a dialog, opened with the ? key or a trigger button, showing the right modifier glyphs for the viewer's platform.
components.whenToUse: Shortcuts are grouped, filtered as you type, and written once with portable names (mod, shift, alt, enter) that render as ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ↵ on a Mac and Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Enter elsewhere; screen readers hear the key names. The platform is read after mount, so server and client markup match. For a static, always-visible list use ShortcutCheatSheet; for one key inline use Kbd.

props.name: groups
props.doc: Shortcut groups, shown as titled columns. Defaults to a sample invoicing app.

props.name: title
props.doc: Dialog title.

props.name: hotkey
props.doc: Key that opens the sheet from anywhere on the page, outside text fields. Empty disables it.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Leave undefined for internal state.

props.name: showTrigger
props.doc: Render the built-in trigger button.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.doc: Text of the built-in trigger button.

examples:
<KeyboardShortcuts
  groups={[{ title: "Invoices", shortcuts: [{ keys: ["mod", "enter"], label: "Send invoice" }, { keys: ["N"], label: "New invoice" }] }]}
/>

components.name: kpi-row
components.title: KpiRow
components.description: A responsive row of headline numbers, each with a label, a value and an optional change.
components.whenToUse: Use it at the top of a dashboard for three to six metrics. For one metric with more detail use StatCard, for a metric with a trend line use StatSparkline, and for a slim inline band use StatsStrip.

props.name: items
props.doc: The metrics, in order. Defaults to four sample SaaS metrics.

examples:
<KpiRow items={[
  { label: "MRR", value: "$48k", delta: 8 },
  { label: "Churn", value: "1.1%", delta: -0.3, invert: true },
]} />

components.name: label
components.title: Label
components.description: The caption for a form control; point htmlFor at the control's id so clicking it focuses the field.
components.whenToUse: Use it beside Input, Textarea, Checkbox, Switch and friends. It dims when a sibling `peer` control is disabled or a `group` ancestor has data-disabled="true". For a label with description and error text wired up for you use FormField.
examples:
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" />

components.name: language-picker
components.title: LanguagePicker
components.description: A grid of language choices where exactly one is selected, each written in its own language.
components.whenToUse: Works as a radio group: Tab enters at the selected language, arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump to the ends. Use it in settings or onboarding for a handful of languages. For long lists use Select or Combobox; for regions use RegionPicker.

props.name: value
props.doc: Selected language id (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial language id when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen language id.

props.name: options
props.doc: Languages to offer. Defaults to English, Spanish, German and Japanese.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the group.

examples: <LanguagePicker value={lang} onChange={setLang} options={[{ id: "en", label: "English" }, { id: "fr", label: "Français" }]} />

components.name: latency-badge
components.title: LatencyBadge
components.description: A small monospace badge for a response time, coloured fast, slow or very slow.
components.whenToUse: Under `fast` ms is success, under `slow` ms is warning, anything above is danger. Use it in endpoint lists, traces and status tables. For a trend over time use StatSparkline, and for a waterfall of spans use TraceWaterfall.

props.name: ms
props.doc: Response time in milliseconds.

props.name: thresholds
props.doc: Upper bounds in ms for the success and warning colours. Defaults to 100 and 400.

examples:
<LatencyBadge ms={182} />
<LatencyBadge ms={950} thresholds={{ fast: 300, slow: 1000 }} />

components.name: light-provider
components.title: LightProvider
components.description: The page's single light source: it follows the pointer, drifts when idle, and every shadow and sheen in the kit falls away from it.
components.whenToUse: Optional: without it shadows fall from a fixed light. Render it once near the root (it renders nothing and only touches `document` in an effect, so it is SSR safe). Pick a material with MaterialSwitcher or by setting data-material on <html> or any subtree.

props.name: idle
props.doc: Drift when the pointer is idle or absent.

props.name: children
props.doc: Rendered as-is. Without children the root provider renders nothing visible.

components.name: line-chart
components.title: LineChart
components.description: Several smooth series on a hairline grid, each in a chart colour with a dot at its latest value.
components.whenToUse: Use it to compare a few series over the same periods (MRR, expansion, churn). For one series with scrubbing use InteractiveAreaChart, for a filled single series use AreaChart, and for a tiny trend use StatSparkline. Add a ChartLegend to name the series visually; `seriesLabels` names them for screen readers.

props.name: series
props.doc: One array of values per series; all series share the x axis.

props.name: seriesLabels
props.doc: Name of each series, in the same order; added to the accessible description with each series' latest value.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the chart.

props.name: grid
props.doc: Draw the dashed horizontal grid.

examples: <LineChart label="MRR by month" seriesLabels={["Total", "Expansion"]} series={[[12, 14, 17, 19], [4, 5, 6, 8]]} />

components.name: link-preview
components.title: LinkPreview
components.description: An unfurled link card: optional image, title, two-line description and the URL, opening in a new tab.
components.whenToUse: Use it for shared links in chat, comments and notes. For a preview that appears on hover over an inline link use HoverCard, and for a cited source in an AI answer use SourceCard or CitationChip.

props.name: url
props.doc: Destination, opened in a new tab.

props.name: title
props.doc: Page title.

props.name: description
props.doc: Page description, clamped to two lines.

props.name: image
props.doc: Preview image URL, shown at 2:1 above the text. Decorative.

examples: <LinkPreview url="https://lumen.app/changelog" title="Lumen changelog" description="Scheduled payouts and reminders." image="/og.png" />

components.name: link
components.title: Link
components.description: An inline text link in the accent text colour, underlined on hover, with a visible focus ring.
components.whenToUse: Use it for navigation in running text and help copy. For an action styled as a link use Button with variant="link"; for a link that looks like a button use Button with render={<a href="…" />}; for "back" navigation use BackLink. With target="_blank" it adds rel="noopener noreferrer" unless you pass rel. It renders a plain <a>; for client-side routing use your router's link with the same classes.
examples: <Link href="/docs/billing">Billing docs</Link>

components.name: list-item
components.title: ListItem
components.description: One row of a list: optional leading visual, a heading with an optional description, and optional trailing content.
components.whenToUse: Use it inside a bordered list or card for settings rows, people, files and search results. It renders a div; put it in an li when the parent is a ul. For a notification use NotificationItem, for a team member with a role use TeamMemberRow, and for a file use FileRow.

props.name: heading
props.doc: Main line, truncated to one line.

props.name: description
props.doc: Secondary line under the heading, truncated.

props.name: leading
props.doc: Visual before the text: an avatar, icon or checkbox.

props.name: trailing
props.doc: Content after the text: a badge, value, menu or button.

examples: <ListItem leading={<Avatar>…</Avatar>} heading="Maya Chen" description="Finance lead" trailing={<Badge>Owner</Badge>} />

components.name: live-cursors-bar
components.title: LiveCursorsBar
components.description: Overlapping initials of the people editing right now, each ringed in their cursor colour, with a count.
components.whenToUse: Use it in the header of a collaborative document or canvas. For a static stack of members use AvatarGroup, for one person's online state use PresenceDot, and for "typing…" use TypingIndicator.

props.name: people
props.doc: People currently in the document.

examples: <LiveCursorsBar people={[{ name: "Maya Chen", color: "var(--chart-1)" }, { name: "Theo Okafor", color: "var(--chart-2)" }]} />

components.name: loading-overlay
components.title: LoadingOverlay
components.description: A translucent layer with a spinner and label that covers its positioned parent while it refreshes.
components.whenToUse: Put it inside a relative container (a card, a table) while data reloads, so the stale content stays visible underneath. For a first load with no content yet use Skeleton or LoadingTable; for an inline wait use Spinner.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible text and the status message read by screen readers.

examples: {isFetching ? : null}

components.name: loading-table
components.title: LoadingTable
components.description: A skeleton table (header plus rows of shimmering cells) shown while table data loads for the first time.
components.whenToUse: Match rows and cols to the real table to avoid layout shift. For an empty result use EmptyTable, for refreshing a table that already has data use LoadingOverlay, and for any other shape use Skeleton.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Body rows to draw.

props.name: cols
props.doc: Columns to draw.

props.name: label
props.doc: Status message read by screen readers.

examples: {isLoading ? <LoadingTable rows={8} cols={5} /> : <DataTable … />}

components.name: logo-cloud
components.title: LogoCloud
components.description: A wrapping, centred row of customer names and marks for social proof.
components.whenToUse: Use it under a hero or above pricing. Only list real customers you have permission to name. For quotes use Testimonial or PressQuote, and for a scrolling strip wrap it in Marquee.

props.name: logos
props.doc: Customer names with an optional mark (an icon or an inline SVG).

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the list, for example "Customers".

examples: <LogoCloud label="Customers" logos={[{ name: "Northwind", mark: <NorthwindMark /> }, { name: "Globex" }]} />

components.name: magic-link-form
components.title: MagicLinkForm
components.description: A passwordless sign-in card: one email field that sends a sign-in link, then confirms where it went.
components.whenToUse: Use it as the whole sign-in step for passwordless apps. For email and password use SignUpForm or AuthCard with your own fields, for OAuth buttons use SocialAuthRow, and for entering a one-time code use OtpInput.

props.name: onSend
props.doc: Called with the trimmed email on submit. Return a promise to show the pending state; throw an Error to show its message.

props.name: title
props.doc: Card title.

examples: <MagicLinkForm onSend={async (email) => { await auth.sendMagicLink(email) }} />

components.name: markdown-editor
components.title: MarkdownEditor
components.description: A markdown textarea with a formatting toolbar, Cmd/Ctrl+B, I, E and K shortcuts, write, split and preview modes, a live preview rendered without innerHTML, and a word count.
components.whenToUse: Use it for release notes, comments, descriptions and docs fields. For rendering markdown only use MarkdownRenderer (or the exported MarkdownPreview), for rich text without markdown syntax use RichTextToolbar, and for chat input use PromptInput. Works controlled (value + onChange) or uncontrolled (defaultValue).

props.name: value
props.doc: Markdown text (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial markdown when uncontrolled. Defaults to sample release notes.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the full text on every edit and toolbar action.

props.name: mode
props.doc: View (controlled): write shows the textarea, preview the rendered result, split both.

props.name: defaultMode
props.doc: Initial view when uncontrolled.

props.name: onModeChange
props.doc: Called when the view changes.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the textarea.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown in the empty textarea.

props.name: minHeight
props.doc: Editor and preview height in px before the textarea is resized.

examples: <MarkdownEditor value={notes} onChange={setNotes} label="Release notes" defaultMode="write" />

components.name: markdown-renderer
components.title: MarkdownRenderer
components.description: Paragraphs and fenced code blocks from a markdown string, with no parser dependency.
components.whenToUse: Use it for short, trusted text such as AI replies, changelog notes or webhook docs where pulling in a full markdown parser is overkill. It never renders HTML, so the content is safe to show as is. For rich markdown (lists, links, tables) bring a real parser; for a single code sample use CodeBlock.

props.name: content
props.doc: Markdown source. Paragraphs and fenced code blocks are rendered; other syntax is shown as plain text.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the root wrapper.

examples:
<MarkdownRenderer content={"Install it:

```bash
npx shadcn add button
```"} />

components.name: marquee
components.title: Marquee
components.description: A strip that scrolls its children sideways in a seamless loop.
components.whenToUse: Use it for logo strips, release notes or "trusted by" rows. It pauses on hover and while anything inside has keyboard focus (WCAG 2.2.2), stops under prefers-reduced-motion, and the duplicate copy is hidden from screen readers. For a static row of logos use LogoCloud.

props.name: children
props.doc: Items to loop. They are rendered twice; the second copy is aria-hidden.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds for one full loop. Larger is slower.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the outer strip.

examples: Changelog 0.6 Base UI 1.8

components.name: masked-input
components.title: MaskedInput
components.description: A text field that formats as you type from a mask such as "(999) 999-9999".
components.whenToUse: Mask tokens: "9" digit, "A" letter, "*" letter or digit, "\\" escapes a token; anything else is a literal. The caret stays where you expect on insert, delete and paste, pasted text is refitted to the mask, and an optional guide shows the characters still to come. onChange returns the masked string, the raw characters and whether the mask is full. Use it for fixed-shape values (dates, plates, IBANs). For phone numbers with no fixed shape use PhoneInput; for one-time codes use OtpInput. Pass `mask` for a single field; without it the component renders `examples`.

props.name: mask
props.doc: The mask. When omitted, the `examples` list is rendered instead.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label above the field. Without one, pass `aria-label`.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible `label`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Raw value (slot characters only), for a controlled field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial raw value when uncontrolled. Extra or mismatched characters are dropped.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires on every edit with `{ masked, raw, complete }`.

props.name: guide
props.doc: Show the remaining mask while typing. `true` uses `guideChar`; a string is a template as long as the mask, e.g. "MM/DD/YYYY".

props.name: guideChar
props.doc: Character drawn for empty slots when `guide` is `true`.

props.name: uppercase
props.doc: Capitalise letters as they are typed.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown when empty and unfocused. Defaults to the guide template.

props.name: hint
props.doc: Help text under the field, linked with aria-describedby. Turns danger-coloured when `invalid`.

props.name: showComplete
props.doc: Show a check once every slot is filled.

props.name: showRaw
props.doc: Show the raw value (slot characters only) under the field.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the field invalid (aria-invalid) and colours the hint.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name. The submitted value is the masked string.

props.name: inputMode
props.doc: Virtual keyboard hint. Defaults to "numeric" for digit-only masks.

props.name: examples
props.doc: Fields rendered when no `mask` is passed.

examples:
<MaskedInput
  label="Phone"
  mask="(999) 999-9999"
  onChange={({ raw, complete }) => complete && save(raw)}
/>

components.name: masonry-grid
components.title: MasonryGrid
components.description: A masonry layout that keeps source order, for cards of uneven height.
components.whenToUse: A CSS grid with tiny rows where each item spans as many rows as its measured height. Items flow left to right, so keyboard and screen reader order match what you see, and the column count follows the container width. Use it for galleries, notes and testimonials; for equal-height cards use a plain grid. Each child is measured, so pass one element per item (no fragments).

props.name: children
props.doc: One element per tile. Keyed children keep their measured height when reordered.

props.name: minColumnWidth
props.doc: Minimum column width in pixels.

props.name: gap
props.doc: Gap between tiles in pixels, both directions. Keep it on the 4px grid.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the grid.

examples:
<MasonryGrid minColumnWidth={220} gap={16}>
  {posts.map((p) => <PostCard key={p.id} post={p} />)}
</MasonryGrid>

components.name: mention-input
components.title: MentionInput
components.description: A comment box that suggests people when you type "@" and inserts the handle you pick.
components.whenToUse: The suggestion list follows the caret, so mentions work mid-sentence, not only at the end. Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown move, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes; the textarea keeps focus and announces the active option through aria-activedescendant. Controlled or uncontrolled. Use TagsInput for a list of chips instead of free text.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the full text on every edit, including when a suggestion is inserted.

props.name: onMention
props.doc: Fires with the handle (without "@") when a suggestion is inserted.

props.name: suggestions
props.doc: Handles offered after "@", filtered by what follows it. At most six show at once.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the wrapper.

props.name: id
props.doc: Pair with a visible <label htmlFor>.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Comment" when there is no `id` to hang a label on.

components.name: menubar
components.title: Menubar
components.description: A desktop-style row of menus (File, Edit, View) built on Base UI Menubar.
components.whenToUse: Arrow keys move between menus and through items, typing jumps to an item, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Use it for app chrome in editors and dashboards; for a single menu behind a button use DropdownMenu, for site navigation use NavigationMenu.
examples:
<Menubar>
  <MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
    <MenubarContent>
      <MenubarItem onClick={newFile}>New file <MenubarShortcut>⌘N</MenubarShortcut></MenubarItem>
      <MenubarSeparator />
      <MenubarItem variant="destructive">Delete</MenubarItem>
    </MenubarContent>
  </MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>

components.name: merge-box
components.title: MergeBox
components.description: The merge panel at the foot of a pull request: check status plus the merge button.
components.whenToUse: When `canMerge` is false the callout turns to a warning and the button is disabled. Use it in code review and deploy UIs; for a generic status message use Callout.

props.name: canMerge
props.doc: All required checks passed. False shows the pending warning and disables the button.

props.name: onMerge
props.doc: Called when the merge button is pressed.

props.name: message
props.doc: Text under the "Ready to merge" or "Checks pending" title.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Button label.

examples: <MergeBox canMerge={checks.every((c) => c.ok)} onMerge={merge} />

components.name: message-actions
components.title: MessageActions
components.description: The copy, retry, thumbs up and thumbs down row under an AI reply.
components.whenToUse: Pass `feedback` to show which thumb is on; the buttons expose it as aria-pressed. Place it under a MessageBubble with role="assistant".

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Copy the reply.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Regenerate the reply.

props.name: onGood
props.doc: Thumbs up.

props.name: onBad
props.doc: Thumbs down.

props.name: feedback
props.doc: The vote already given, shown as a pressed thumb.

examples:
<MessageActions
  onCopy={() => navigator.clipboard.writeText(reply)}
  onRetry={regenerate}
  feedback={vote}
  onGood={() => setVote("good")}
  onBad={() => setVote("bad")}
/>

components.name: message-bubble
components.title: MessageBubble
components.description: One chat turn: user turns sit in a sunken capsule, assistant turns are plain prose, system turns are a quiet rule.
components.whenToUse: Use it for AI chat transcripts. Set `streaming` while tokens arrive to show a blinking cursor and mark the turn aria-busy. Put MessageActions under assistant turns; render markdown inside with MarkdownRenderer.

props.name: role
props.doc: Who is speaking. "user" aligns right in a capsule; "assistant" is left-aligned prose; "system" is a centred note.

props.name: streaming
props.doc: Tokens are still arriving: shows a cursor and sets aria-busy.

examples:
<MessageBubble role="user">Summarise invoice INV-2041</MessageBubble>
<MessageBubble role="assistant" streaming={isStreaming}>{reply}</MessageBubble>

components.name: meter
components.title: Meter
components.description: A labelled bar showing how much of a known range is used (storage, quota, seats).
components.whenToUse: Exposes role="meter" with the value and a percentage text. Use Meter for a level that can go up and down; use Progress for a task moving toward done.

props.name: value
props.doc: Current amount, in the same unit as `max`. Clamped to 0..max for display.

props.name: max
props.doc: Top of the range.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label above the bar; also its accessible name.

props.name: valueText
props.doc: What screen readers hear for the value, e.g. "42 of 50 GB". Defaults to the percentage.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Show `valueText` (or the percentage) beside the label.

examples: <Meter label="Storage" value={42} max={50} valueText="42 of 50 GB" showValue />

components.name: metric-delta
components.title: MetricDelta
components.description: A small arrow and percentage showing how a metric moved, green for good and red for bad.
components.whenToUse: Positive values point up, negative point down, zero is neutral with no arrow. Set `invert` for metrics where down is good (latency, churn, cost). Screen readers hear "Up 12%" or "Down 3%". Use it inside StatCard or a KPI row.

props.name: value
props.doc: Change in percent. 12 means +12%. The sign sets the arrow.

props.name: invert
props.doc: Down is good: negative values turn green and positive values red.

examples:
<MetricDelta value={12.4} />
<MetricDelta value={-8} invert />  // latency fell: shown green

components.name: mobile-action-sheet
components.title: MobileActionSheet
components.description: An iOS-style sheet of full-width actions with a separate Cancel row, for phone-sized screens.
components.whenToUse: Built on Base UI Dialog: focus moves into the sheet and is trapped there, the page is scroll-locked and inert, Escape or a tap on the scrim cancels, and focus returns to the trigger. Use it for a short list of verbs on one object; for forms or longer content use Drawer, for desktop menus use DropdownMenu.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Leave it out and the sheet manages itself behind a trigger button.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called on Cancel, Escape, a scrim tap or after an action runs. Set `open` to false here.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Rows in order. Put destructive actions last.

props.name: title
props.doc: Optional heading above the actions; also the dialog's accessible name.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.doc: Label of the Cancel row.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.doc: Label of the trigger button, shown only when the sheet is uncontrolled.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the action panel.

components.name: mobile-nav-drawer
components.title: MobileNavDrawer
components.description: A hamburger button that opens site navigation in a panel from the right edge.
components.whenToUse: Built on Sheet (Base UI Dialog), so focus is trapped, Escape and the scrim close it, the page is scroll-locked and focus returns to the hamburger. Links close the drawer when followed. Show it below your desktop breakpoint (e.g. className="md:hidden") next to NavMarketing or a NavigationMenu.

props.name: links
props.doc: Destinations in order. Rendered with next/link.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Title in the drawer header.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the wrapper around the hamburger button.

examples:
<MobileNavDrawer
  className="md:hidden"
  brand="Lumen"
  links={[{ href: "/pricing", label: "Pricing" }, { href: "/docs", label: "Docs" }]}
/>

components.name: model-compare
components.title: ModelCompare
components.description: A compact table of AI models by latency, cost and quality, with latency colour coded.
components.whenToUse: Exposes table semantics (role="table", rows, column headers) so screen readers can move by cell. Use it on model settings or pricing pages; to choose one model use ModelPicker.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Models to list, in display order.

examples: <ModelCompare rows={[{ name: "Mini", latencyMs: 84, cost: "$0.15 / 1M", quality: "Good" }]} />

components.name: model-picker
components.title: ModelPicker
components.description: A select for choosing an AI model, controlled or uncontrolled.
components.whenToUse: Built on the kit's Select (Base UI): full keyboard support, typeahead and a labelled trigger. Use it in chat composers and AI settings; to compare models side by side use ModelCompare.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled model id.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial model id when uncontrolled; pass null to start on the placeholder.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the chosen model id.

props.name: models
props.doc: Options in display order.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Trigger text when nothing is selected.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the trigger. Defaults to "Model".

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the trigger. Defaults to a 224px width.

examples:
const [model, setModel] = React.useState("lumen-pro")
<ModelPicker value={model} onChange={setModel} models={[{ id: "lumen-pro", label: "Lumen Pro" }]} />

components.name: morph-panel
components.title: MorphPanel
components.description: A button that stretches into the panel it opens on a spring, with a built-in feedback form.
components.whenToUse: One surface grows from a pill into a panel, its corners easing from 10 to 16px, while the label blurs out and the content blurs in. No popover, no jump. Escape and an outside click close it and focus returns to the trigger; with reduced motion it swaps instantly. Default content is a feedback form with a sent state; pass a render function as `children` for your own panel. For a plain anchored panel use Popover; for a modal use Dialog.

props.name: label
props.doc: Trigger text; also the panel's accessible name when it is a string.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Icon before the label.

props.name: width
props.doc: Panel width in px.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: Which corner of the trigger the panel grows from.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Fires when the panel opens or closes.

props.name: children
props.doc: Custom panel as a render function. Receives close(), which also returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the text by the default feedback form. Return a promise to show "Sending…"; reject to let the user retry.

examples:
<MorphPanel label="Feedback" onSubmit={(text) => api.feedback(text)} />
<MorphPanel label="New note" width={300}>{({ close }) => <NoteForm onDone={close} />}</MorphPanel>

components.name: multi-select
components.title: MultiSelect
components.description: A popover list with check marks and removable chips for the chosen items.
components.whenToUse: Each option is a toggle button (aria-pressed), so Tab and Space/Enter work without a custom keyboard model; chips under the trigger remove an item in one click and are labelled "Remove <name>". Use it for 2 to ~20 options; for long or searchable lists use Combobox, for free-form entry use TagsInput.

props.name: items
props.doc: Options in display order.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selection.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial selection when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the full new selection after every toggle or chip removal.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Trigger text when nothing is selected.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the trigger, e.g. "Reviewers". The current selection is read after it.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the trigger button.

components.name: nav-marketing
components.title: NavMarketing
components.description: A sticky top bar for marketing sites: brand, a few links and sign-in / get-started buttons.
components.whenToUse: The links hide below the md breakpoint; pair it with MobileNavDrawer there. Pass `actions` to replace the default buttons. For app navigation with dropdown panels use NavigationMenu; for an app sidebar use Sidebar.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Brand text at the left.

props.name: brandHref
props.doc: Where the brand links to.

props.name: links
props.doc: Primary destinations. Hidden below md.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Right-hand controls. Defaults to "Sign in" and "Get started" buttons.

examples:
<NavMarketing
  brand="Lumen"
  links={[{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing" }, { label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }]}
  actions={<Button size="sm" render={<a href="/signup" />}>Start free</Button>}
/>

components.name: navigation-menu
components.title: NavigationMenu
components.description: A site navigation bar whose items open rich dropdown panels, built on Base UI NavigationMenu.
components.whenToUse: Panels share one viewport that resizes between items; hover or click opens, arrow keys move between triggers, Escape closes and returns focus. Render NavigationMenuViewport once inside NavigationMenu. Use it for marketing and docs headers with grouped links; for app commands use Menubar, for a simple bar of links use NavMarketing.
examples:
<NavigationMenu>
  <NavigationMenuList>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuTrigger>Product</NavigationMenuTrigger>
      <NavigationMenuContent>
        <NavigationMenuLink href="/invoices">Invoices</NavigationMenuLink>
      </NavigationMenuContent>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuLink href="/pricing">Pricing</NavigationMenuLink>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
  </NavigationMenuList>
  <NavigationMenuViewport />
</NavigationMenu>

components.name: nested-nav
components.title: NestedNav
components.description: A collapsible tree of navigation groups that indents with depth, for settings and docs sidebars.
components.whenToUse: Groups are disclosure buttons (aria-expanded); leaves are links when they have an `href`, buttons otherwise. The node matching `activeId` gets aria-current="page". Use it for two or three levels of navigation; for a file-style tree with arrow-key navigation and selection use TreeView.

props.name: nodes
props.doc: Tree of nodes; any node with children becomes a collapsible group.

props.name: activeId
props.doc: Id of the current page's node; it is highlighted and marked aria-current="page".

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called when a leaf is activated (link or button).

examples:
<NestedNav
  activeId="invoices"
  nodes={[{ id: "billing", label: "Billing", children: [{ id: "invoices", label: "Invoices", href: "/billing/invoices" }] }]}
/>

components.name: newsletter-signup
components.title: NewsletterSignup
components.description: An email field and Subscribe button that stack on phones and sit in one row from sm up.
components.whenToUse: Uses native email validation. If `onSubmit` returns a promise the button shows "Subscribing…" until it settles, then a polite status line confirms success or reports the error; a rejected promise keeps the email so the user can retry. Use it in footers and blog sidebars; for a full sign-up flow use a form block.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Receives the email. Return a promise to show the pending and success states.

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: Status text after a successful submit.

props.name: buttonLabel
props.doc: Button label.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Placeholder in the field.

examples: <NewsletterSignup onSubmit={(email) => fetch("/api/subscribe", { method: "POST", body: email })} />

components.name: not-found-state
components.title: NotFoundState
components.description: A centred 404 panel with a code, heading, explanation and recovery buttons.
components.whenToUse: Use it in a Next.js not-found.tsx or when a record lookup returns nothing. Pass `actions` with real links (the defaults are inert placeholders). For an empty list use EmptyState; for a blocked page use PermissionDenied.

props.name: code
props.doc: Small code above the heading.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading text.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences on what happened and what to do next.
props.default: "That route is not in the registry. T...

props.name: actions
props.doc: Recovery buttons. Defaults to inert "Go home" and "Open gallery" buttons.

examples:
<NotFoundState
  description="That invoice was deleted or never existed."
  actions={<Button size="sm" render={<a href="/invoices" />}>Back to invoices</Button>}
/>

components.name: notebook-cell
components.title: NotebookCell
components.description: A Jupyter-style cell: a run button, the code in an editor frame, and its output below.
components.whenToUse: While `running` is true the run button is disabled and the cell is aria-busy; the output region is a labelled, keyboard-scrollable live region so results are announced. Use it for data and AI playgrounds; for static code use CodeBlock.

props.name: code
props.doc: Source shown in the editor frame.

props.name: output
props.doc: Result text. Omit (or pass null) to hide the output area.

props.name: onRun
props.doc: Called by the run button.

props.name: running
props.doc: The cell is executing: disables run and marks the cell busy.

props.name: filename
props.doc: File name in the editor frame's title bar.

examples: <NotebookCell code={source} output={result} running={busy} onRun={run} filename="query.sql" />

components.name: notification-inbox
components.title: NotificationInbox
components.description: A bell with an unread count that opens an inbox popover with All and Mentions tabs, unread dots and mark-all-read.
components.whenToUse: Built on Base UI Popover: focus moves in on open, Escape closes and returns focus to the bell, whose accessible name includes the unread count. Opening a row marks it read. Use it in app headers; for a single row use NotificationItem, for settings use NotificationPreferences.

props.name: notes
props.doc: Initial notifications, newest first. The inbox then tracks read state itself.

props.name: onOpenNote
props.doc: Called when a notification is opened (it is also marked read).

props.name: onMarkAllRead
props.doc: Called after "Mark all read".

props.name: viewAllHref
props.doc: Footer link to the full activity page. Omit to hide the footer.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the bell trigger.

examples:
<NotificationInbox
  notes={[{ id: "1", kind: "mention", who: "Mira Sato", text: "mentioned you in Q3 roadmap", time: "2m", unread: true }]}
  onOpenNote={(n) => router.push(`/inbox/${n.id}`)}
  viewAllHref="/activity"
/>

components.name: notification-item
components.title: NotificationItem
components.description: One row of a notification list: title, body, relative time and an unread dot.
components.whenToUse: The time renders with RelativeTime ("42 min ago") and is hydration-safe. Unread rows get a tinted background, an accent dot and "Unread" for screen readers. Stack rows in a list; for the bell-and-popover inbox use NotificationInbox.

props.name: title
props.doc: One-line headline; truncates.

props.name: body
props.doc: Supporting sentence under the title.

props.name: date
props.doc: When it happened. Defaults to 42 minutes ago.

props.name: unread
props.doc: Highlights the row and adds an unread dot.

examples: <NotificationItem title="Invoice INV-2041 paid" body="Northwind paid $12,400.00." date={paidAt} unread />

components.name: notification-preferences
components.title: NotificationPreferences
components.description: A list of labelled on/off switches for notification channels (email digests, product updates, security alerts).
components.whenToUse: Each row's label is wired to its switch, ids are unique per instance, and `onCheckedChange` reports which channel changed. Switches are uncontrolled from `defaultChecked`; persist changes in the callback. Use it on settings pages.

props.name: items
props.doc: Channels in display order.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: Fires with the channel id and its new state.

examples:
<NotificationPreferences
  items={[{ id: "email", label: "Email digests", defaultChecked: true }, { id: "sms", label: "SMS alerts" }]}
  onCheckedChange={(id, on) => savePreference(id, on)}
/>

components.name: number-input
components.title: NumberInput
components.description: A numeric field with minus and plus buttons, clamped to min and max.
components.whenToUse: Typing is free while the field has focus (you can clear it or type "15" past a min of 10); the value is clamped and committed on blur or Enter. ArrowUp/ArrowDown step natively, buttons disable at the bounds, and decimal steps avoid float drift (0.1 + 0.2 stays 0.3). Controlled or uncontrolled. Use Slider for a rough value on a range; use it for exact counts like seats or quantities.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with each committed, clamped value.

props.name: min
props.doc: Lowest allowed value.

props.name: max
props.doc: Highest allowed value.

props.name: step
props.doc: Amount the buttons and arrow keys add or remove.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the wrapper.

props.name: id
props.doc: Pair with a visible <label htmlFor>.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Number" when there is no `id` to hang a label on.

examples:
const [seats, setSeats] = React.useState(5)
<NumberInput value={seats} onChange={setSeats} min={1} max={50} aria-label="Seats" />

components.name: number-roll
components.title: NumberRoll
components.description: An odometer number whose digits roll on a spring when the value changes.
components.whenToUse: Each digit is a strip of 0-9 that springs to its place, so changing $1,284 to $1,391 rolls only the digits that changed. Digits keep their identity from the right, so 999 → 1,000 grows a column instead of reshuffling. Screen readers get the plain formatted value; with reduced motion the number swaps instantly. Use it for live totals, prices and KPI values; for a static number just render it with tabular-nums.

props.name: value
props.doc: The number to show. Change it to roll.

props.name: format
props.doc: Intl.NumberFormat options, e.g. { style: "currency", currency: "USD" }.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for formatting, e.g. "de-DE".

props.name: trend
props.doc: Briefly tint up/down changes with success/danger.

examples: <NumberRoll value={mrr} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} trend />

components.name: offline-banner
components.title: OfflineBanner
components.description: A full-width warning strip saying the app is offline, with an optional Retry button.
components.whenToUse: It is a polite live region (role="status"), so mounting it announces the message. Render it at the top of the page while `navigator.onLine` is false; for a whole empty panel use OfflineState.

props.name: message
props.doc: Message text.
props.default: "You are offline. Changes will sync w...

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Shows a Retry button that calls this.

examples: {!online ? <OfflineBanner onRetry={reconnect} /> : null}

components.name: offline-state
components.title: OfflineState
components.description: A card that says the app is offline, explains what still works, and offers a retry.
components.whenToUse: Use it in place of content that needs the network. For a thin page-wide strip use OfflineBanner; for a generic empty list use EmptyState.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading text.

props.name: description
props.doc: What still works and what is paused.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Called by the retry button.

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: Retry button label.

examples: <OfflineState onRetry={() => refetch()} description="Your drafts are saved on this device." />

components.name: onboarding-checklist
components.title: OnboardingChecklist
components.description: A "Get started" card of tickable setup tasks with a done count.
components.whenToUse: Each task is a checkbox (role="checkbox", aria-checked) toggled by click, Space or Enter; the header shows "2 of 4" progress. State is kept inside from `items`; persist it with `onToggle`. Use it on empty dashboards; for a strict linear flow use OnboardingWizard.

props.name: items
props.doc: Initial tasks in order.

props.name: title
props.doc: Card heading.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Fires with the task id and its new done state.

examples:
<OnboardingChecklist
  title="Set up Lumen"
  items={[{ id: "invite", label: "Invite your team" }, { id: "bank", label: "Connect a bank", done: true }]}
  onToggle={(id, done) => saveStep(id, done)}
/>

components.name: onboarding-wizard
components.title: OnboardingWizard
components.description: A three-step first-run flow: create a workspace, invite members, done.
components.whenToUse: A Stepper shows progress; when the step changes, focus moves to the new step so keyboard and screen reader users land on the fresh content. Use it as a starting point for a linear setup flow; for optional tasks in any order use OnboardingChecklist.

props.name: onComplete
props.doc: Called when the user reaches the final step.

examples: <OnboardingWizard onComplete={() => router.push("/dashboard")} />

components.name: order-summary
components.title: OrderSummary
components.description: Label and value lines above a separator and a bold total, for checkout and invoices.
components.whenToUse: Marked up as a description list (dt/dd) so each amount is read with its label. Values are preformatted strings: format money with Intl.NumberFormat before passing it in. Use it beside a checkout form; for a full price table use PricingTable.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Rows above the total, in order.

props.name: total
props.doc: Preformatted grand total.

props.name: totalLabel
props.doc: Label for the total row.

examples:
<OrderSummary
  lines={[{ label: "Subtotal", value: "$120.00" }, { label: "Tax", value: "$9.60" }]}
  total="$129.60"
/>

components.name: org-chart
components.title: OrgChart
components.description: A collapsible organisation chart with connector lines, initials avatars, team colours, per node counts and arrow key navigation.
components.whenToUse: Cards carry an initials avatar, name, role and a team coloured stripe; a pill under each manager shows how many people report up and folds the branch on a spring. Connectors are plain CSS borders and the tree scrolls sideways when wider than its container. Keyboard: one tab stop; ArrowLeft/Right walk siblings, ArrowDown opens or enters reports, ArrowUp goes to the manager, Home/End jump, Enter/Space selects and toggles. Use it for people directories and admin consoles; for a file-style hierarchy use TreeView, for a sidebar menu use NestedNav.

props.name: data
props.doc: The root person. Defaults to Northwind's leadership, four levels deep with the lower branches folded.

props.name: defaultExpandDepth
props.doc: Nodes at or above this depth start expanded. The root is depth 0.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.doc: Extra node ids that start expanded.

props.name: selectedId
props.doc: Controlled selected node id.

props.name: defaultSelectedId
props.doc: Initially selected node id when uncontrolled.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called when a node is clicked or activated.

props.name: teamTones
props.doc: Pin team names to colours. Unlisted teams are coloured in order.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the tree.

examples:
<OrgChart
  data={{ id: "ceo", name: "Maya Chen", role: "CEO", children: [{ id: "cto", name: "Theo Okafor", role: "CTO", team: "Engineering" }] }}
  defaultExpandDepth={1}
  onSelect={(node) => openProfile(node.id)}
/>

components.name: org-switcher
components.title: OrgSwitcher
components.description: A popover list of organizations with the current one checked and its plan beside it.
components.whenToUse: The trigger reads "<current org>, switch organization"; the current option carries aria-current. Picking one closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. Controlled (`value`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`). Use it at the top of a Sidebar; for a plain list of options use Select.

props.name: orgs
props.doc: Organizations in display order. The first is current until one is chosen.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled organization id. Omit it and the switcher keeps its own selection.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initially selected organization id when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the chosen organization id.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the trigger button.

examples:
<OrgSwitcher
  orgs={[{ id: "northwind", name: "Northwind", plan: "Business" }, { id: "halcyon", name: "Halcyon", plan: "Pro" }]}
  value={orgId}
  onChange={setOrgId}
/>

components.name: otp-input
components.title: OtpInput
components.description: A one-time code field drawn as separate slots, with SMS autofill, paste and a shake on error.
components.whenToUse: One real <input> sits invisibly over the slots, so paste, SMS autofill (autocomplete="one-time-code"), backspace, selection and screen readers all behave natively. The slots are pure paint: a fake caret, a glyph that settles in, a shake when `status` turns "invalid". Use it for 2FA and email verification codes; for other fixed-shape values use MaskedInput.

props.name: length
props.doc: Number of characters in the code.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled code.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial code when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the cleaned code on every edit.

props.name: onComplete
props.doc: Fires once when every slot is filled.

props.name: groups
props.doc: Split the slots into groups, e.g. [3, 3] renders "123 – 456". Must sum to `length`.

props.name: pattern
props.doc: Allowed characters. "alphanumeric" upper-cases letters.

props.name: status
props.doc: "invalid" shakes and turns the slots red (aria-invalid); "success" turns them green.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name for the hidden input.

props.name: size
props.doc: Slot size: "default" 40×44, "lg" 48×56.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "One-time code".

examples: <OtpInput length={6} groups={[3, 3]} onComplete={verify} status={error ? "invalid" : "idle"} />

components.name: page-header
components.title: PageHeader
components.description: The top of an app page: an h1 title, an optional description and right-aligned actions, over a hairline.
components.whenToUse: Renders the page's only h1, so use it once per page. Actions wrap under the title on narrow screens. For a marketing hero use a Hero block; for a section inside a page use a plain h2.

props.name: title
props.doc: Page title, rendered as the h1.

props.name: description
props.doc: One sentence under the title.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons on the right, e.g. a primary action and a secondary one.

examples:
<PageHeader
  title="Invoices"
  description="Everything billed to customers this year."
  actions={<Button size="sm">New invoice</Button>}
/>

components.name: pagination
components.title: Pagination
components.description: Previous / page numbers / Next controls for a paged list, with ellipses for long ranges.
components.whenToUse: Always shows the first and last page plus the current page's neighbours, and keeps a constant seven slots so the bar never changes width as you page. The current page has aria-current="page"; every button has a spoken label ("Page 4"). The component is controlled: keep `page` in state (1-based) and update it in onPageChange. For infinite feeds use a "Load more" button instead.

props.name: page
props.doc: Current page, 1-based.

props.name: pageCount
props.doc: Total number of pages. Zero or one hides nothing but disables both arrows.

props.name: onPageChange
props.doc: Fires with the requested 1-based page.

examples:
const [page, setPage] = React.useState(1)
<Pagination page={page} pageCount={Math.ceil(total / pageSize)} onPageChange={setPage} />

components.name: password-input
components.title: PasswordInput
components.description: A password field with an eye button that shows or hides what was typed.
components.whenToUse: Accepts every native input prop (name, autoComplete, required, value, onChange…). The toggle is a real button labelled "Show password" / "Hide password" that controls the field via aria-controls. Use autoComplete="current-password" on sign-in and "new-password" on sign-up; for a strength meter use PasswordStrength.

props.name: size
props.doc: Field height: "sm" 32px, "default" 36px, "lg" 44px.

examples:
<label htmlFor="pw">Password</label>
<PasswordInput id="pw" name="password" autoComplete="current-password" required />

components.name: password-strength
components.title: PasswordStrength
components.description: A new-password field with a four segment strength meter and a live checklist of rules.
components.whenToUse: The score is announced politely as it changes, rules are plain text for screen readers ("(met)" / "(not met)"), and nothing blocks typing. Swap in your own scorer (for example zxcvbn) with the `score` prop and your own policy with `rules`. Use it on sign-up and change-password forms; on sign-in use PasswordInput alone.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled password.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial password when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the password on every edit.

props.name: rules
props.doc: Rules shown in the checklist.

props.name: score
props.doc: Override the built in 0 to 4 score.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label above the field.

props.name: id
props.doc: Input id; also prefixes the meter and checklist ids.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name.

examples:
<PasswordStrength
  label="New password"
  onChange={setPassword}
  rules={[{ label: "At least 12 characters", test: (v) => v.length >= 12 }]}
/>

components.name: payment-method-card
components.title: PaymentMethodCard
components.description: A saved card on file: brand, masked last four digits, expiry and an Edit button.
components.whenToUse: Screen readers hear "Visa ending in 4242, expires 09/28" instead of the dots. Never pass a full card number; only the last four. Use it on billing settings pages; to collect a new card use your payment provider's hosted fields.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Card network, e.g. "Visa".

props.name: last4
props.doc: Last four digits only.

props.name: exp
props.doc: Expiry as MM/YY.

props.name: onEdit
props.doc: Called by the Edit button.

examples: <PaymentMethodCard brand="Mastercard" last4="4444" exp="11/27" onEdit={openBillingPortal} />

components.name: peek-panel
components.title: PeekPanel
components.description: A non-modal side panel for previewing a record beside a list, with a title bar and close button.
components.whenToUse: It is a labelled landmark (aside) that leaves the rest of the page usable; Escape inside it calls `onClose`, and the close button only renders when `onClose` is given. Place it in a flex row next to the list. For a modal overlay that traps focus use Sheet; for a resizable split use a resizable panel layout.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading in the title bar; also the landmark's accessible name.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called by the close button and by Escape inside the panel.

examples: {issue ? setIssue(null)}>{issue.body} : null}

components.name: permission-chip
components.title: PermissionChip
components.description: A small uppercase chip showing an access level: admin, write or read.
components.whenToUse: Admin is accent-tinted, write is filled, read is quiet, so levels scan at a glance in member tables. Screen readers hear "admin access". For arbitrary labels use Badge; for live status use StatusBadge.

props.name: level
props.doc: Access level shown on the chip.

examples: <PermissionChip level="write" />

components.name: permission-denied
components.title: PermissionDenied
components.description: A centred panel explaining that the user lacks access, with buttons to request it or go elsewhere.
components.whenToUse: Say which role is needed in `description`. Pass `actions` with real handlers (the defaults are inert placeholders). For a missing page use NotFoundState; for a single locked control use PermissionChip or a disabled button with a Tooltip.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading text.

props.name: description
props.doc: Which permission is missing and who can grant it.
props.default: "You need admin on this workspace to ...

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons. Defaults to inert "Request access" and "Switch workspace" buttons.

examples:
<PermissionDenied
  description="You need the Billing admin role to view invoices."
  actions={<Button size="sm" onClick={requestAccess}>Request access</Button>}
/>

components.name: phone-input
components.title: PhoneInput
components.description: A telephone field with the phone keypad on mobile and tel autofill, free-form so any country's format works.
components.whenToUse: Accepts every native input prop (name, required, aria-invalid…); onChange gives the string. Validate and normalise (e.g. to E.164) on submit, not while typing. For a fixed national format with live formatting use MaskedInput with "(999) 999-9999".

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled value. Leave it out for an uncontrolled field (use defaultValue).

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the raw text on every edit.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Phone number" when there is no `id` to hang a label on.

examples:
<label htmlFor="phone">Phone</label>
<PhoneInput id="phone" name="phone" value={phone} onChange={setPhone} />

components.name: pie-chart
components.title: PieChart
components.description: An SVG pie chart with leader line labels, a legend and slices that pull out on hover or focus.
components.whenToUse: Hover or focus a slice and it pulls out on a spring while the readout shows its value and share. Slices are one tab stop; arrow keys, Home and End move between them, and a visually hidden table carries the data for screen readers. Labels hide below 320px wide. Use it for 2 to 6 parts of a whole; for more categories or comparisons over time use BarChart, for a ring with a centre total use DonutChart.

props.name: data
props.doc: Slices in clockwise order, starting at the top.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading shown above the chart and used as the accessible name.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Caption under the total when no slice is active.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats values in the readout, legend and table.

props.name: showLabels
props.doc: Labels outside the slices with leader lines. Hidden automatically when the chart is narrow.

props.name: showLegend
props.doc: Legend with values under the chart.

props.name: pullOut
props.doc: Distance a hovered or focused slice pulls out, in chart units.

examples:
<PieChart
  title="Revenue by plan"
  data={[{ label: "Pro", value: 22400 }, { label: "Business", value: 31600 }]}
  format={(n) => `$${n.toLocaleString()}`}
/>

components.name: pinned-message
components.title: PinnedMessage
components.description: An accent-tinted note pinned to the top of a channel or thread, with its author.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one standing announcement above a message list; for page-wide notices use Banner, for inline warnings use Callout. Pass `onUnpin` to show an Unpin button.

props.name: author
props.doc: Who pinned or wrote it.

props.name: body
props.doc: The message text.

props.name: onUnpin
props.doc: Shows an Unpin button that calls this.

examples: <PinnedMessage author="Maya" body="Release freeze starts Friday at 18:00 UTC." onUnpin={unpin} />

components.name: plan-card
components.title: PlanCard
components.description: A pricing tier with price per period, feature list and a call to action; highlighted tiers get the accent ring.
components.whenToUse: Lay several side by side for a pricing page; mark the recommended one `highlighted` and give it a `badge`. Prices are preformatted strings. For a full feature matrix use PlanComparison, for a monthly/yearly switch use PricingToggle.

props.name: name
props.doc: Tier name.

props.name: price
props.doc: Preformatted price, e.g. "$49".

props.name: period
props.doc: Billing period after the slash, e.g. "mo" or "yr".

props.name: features
props.doc: What the tier includes, one line each.

props.name: cta
props.doc: Button label.

props.name: highlighted
props.doc: Recommended tier: accent ring and a solid button.

props.name: badge
props.doc: Small label beside the name, e.g. "Most popular".

props.name: onCta
props.doc: Called by the button.

examples: <PlanCard name="Pro" price="$49" period="mo" features={["10 seats", "Bank sync"]} highlighted badge="Most popular" onCta={() => checkout("pro")} />

components.name: plan-comparison
components.title: PlanComparison
components.description: A feature-by-plan table with check marks, dashes or short values in each cell.
components.whenToUse: A real <table> with column and row headers; icon cells carry "Included" / "Not included" for screen readers. Pass `plans` for the columns and `rows` with one value per plan: true, false, or a string such as "10 seats". Scrolls sideways on narrow screens. Pair it with PlanCard tiers above.

props.name: plans
props.doc: Column headings, one per plan.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Feature rows.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Accessible caption for the table.

examples:
<PlanComparison
  plans={["Free", "Pro", "Business"]}
  rows={[
    { feature: "Seats", values: ["1", "10", "Unlimited"] },
    { feature: "SSO", values: [false, false, true] },
  ]}
/>

components.name: popover
components.title: Popover
components.description: A floating panel anchored to its trigger, built on Base UI; without children it shows a demo trigger and panel.
components.whenToUse: Click or Enter opens it, focus moves inside, Escape or an outside click closes it and focus returns to the trigger. The panel is non-modal and labelled by PopoverTitle. Use it for small interactive content (share links, filters, quick edits); for read-only hints use Tooltip, for a list of commands use DropdownMenu, for blocking decisions use Dialog.
examples:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Share</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent align="start">
    <PopoverHeader>
      <PopoverTitle>Share report</PopoverTitle>
      <PopoverDescription>Anyone with the link can view.</PopoverDescription>
    </PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverClose render={<Button size="sm" />}>Done</PopoverClose>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>

components.name: presence-dot
components.title: PresenceDot
components.description: A small coloured dot that shows whether a person is online, away, busy or offline.
components.whenToUse: Use it on avatars, member lists and chat headers. For a labelled state chip use StatusBadge; for a pulsing "live" indicator use a badge with its own copy.

props.name: status
props.doc: Which presence to show. Colour comes from the success, warning, danger and fg-subtle tokens.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to the status, e.g. "Online".

examples:
<PresenceDot status="online" />
<PresenceDot status="busy" label="Maya is in a meeting" />

components.name: press-quote
components.title: PressQuote
components.description: A centred pull quote from a publication, with the source in small caps underneath.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one line of real press coverage on a landing page. For a customer quote with a name, role and avatar use a testimonial card. Only quote coverage you actually have.

props.name: quote
props.doc: The quoted sentence, without quotation marks; they are added for you.

props.name: source
props.doc: Publication or person the quote comes from.

props.name: cite
props.doc: URL of the original article, set as the blockquote's `cite`.

examples: <PressQuote quote="The calmest component kit we have used." source="Design Weekly" />

components.name: pricing-table
components.title: PricingTable
components.description: Three PlanCards in a responsive grid, one of them highlighted.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a pricing section with plan tiers side by side. Pair it with PricingToggle for a monthly / yearly switch. For a single plan use PlanCard directly.

props.name: plans
props.doc: One entry per tier, each taking PlanCard props. Set `highlighted: true` on the recommended one.

examples:
<PricingTable
  plans={[
    { name: "Starter", price: "$0", features: ["1 seat"], cta: "Start free" },
    { name: "Pro", price: "$49", features: ["10 seats"], highlighted: true },
  ]}
/>

components.name: pricing-toggle
components.title: PricingToggle
components.description: A Monthly / Yearly segmented switch with a savings note underneath.
components.whenToUse: Use it above a PricingTable to flip prices between billing periods. For any other two or three way choice use SegmentedControl directly.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled billing period. Leave unset to let the toggle keep its own state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting period when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the newly picked period.

props.name: note
props.doc: Line under the switch. Pass an empty string or null to hide it. Use your real discount.

examples:
const [cadence, setCadence] = React.useState<BillingCadence>("monthly")
<PricingToggle value={cadence} onChange={setCadence} note="Two months free on yearly" />

components.name: priority-picker
components.title: PriorityPicker
components.description: A row of four pill radios (Low, Medium, High, Urgent) for an issue or task priority.
components.whenToUse: Use it in issue forms and task sidebars. Arrow keys move and select, like any radio group. For an arbitrary option list use SegmentedControl or RadioGroup.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled priority: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "urgent". Leave unset for uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting priority when uncontrolled. Nothing is selected by default.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the picked priority.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the group.

examples:
const [priority, setPriority] = React.useState<Priority>("medium")
<PriorityPicker value={priority} onChange={setPriority} />

components.name: product-card
components.title: ProductCard
components.description: A square product image, title, price and an optional Add to cart button.
components.whenToUse: Use it in shop grids and recommendation rails. For a pricing tier use PlanCard; for a generic content tile use Card.

props.name: title
props.doc: Product name, rendered as an h3.

props.name: price
props.doc: Display price, already formatted, e.g. "$48" or "€42,00".

props.name: image
props.doc: Image URL, shown square and cropped to cover.

props.name: imageAlt
props.doc: Alt text for the image. Empty by default because the title sits right under it.

props.name: badge
props.doc: Short corner tag such as "New" or "-20%".

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: Shows the add button when set.

props.name: addLabel
props.doc: Text of the add button.

examples: <ProductCard title="Linen tote" price="$48" image="/tote.jpg" imageAlt="Natural linen tote bag" badge="New" onAdd={() => addToCart("tote")} />

components.name: profile-form
components.title: ProfileForm
components.description: A display name and bio form with a Save button, for account settings pages.
components.whenToUse: Use it as a starting point for profile settings; the fields are native form controls, so the values arrive in `onSubmit` as plain strings. For sign in or sign up use the auth forms.

props.name: defaultValues
props.doc: Starting values for the fields.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the trimmed values when the form is submitted.

examples: <ProfileForm defaultValues={{ name: "Maya Chen" }} onSubmit={({ name, bio }) => save(name, bio)} />

components.name: progress-circle
components.title: ProgressCircle
components.description: A small ring that fills clockwise to a percentage, with the number underneath.
components.whenToUse: Use it for compact determinate progress in cards, lists and table cells. For a full width bar use Progress; for several goals at once use RadialChart.

props.name: value
props.doc: Percent complete, clamped to 0..100.

props.name: size
props.doc: Width and height of the ring in px. Use an even number.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Show the percentage under the ring.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Progress".

examples:
<ProgressCircle value={64} label="Upload progress" />
<ProgressCircle value={30} size={56} showValue={false} />

components.name: progress
components.title: Progress
components.description: A thin determinate progress bar built on Base UI, with optional label and value text.
components.whenToUse: Use it for uploads, onboarding steps and long tasks with a known end. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar. For a compact ring use ProgressCircle; for usage against a limit use QuotaBar. Children render above the track, so put ProgressLabel and ProgressValue inside.
examples:
<Progress value={42}>
  <ProgressLabel>Uploading</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>

components.name: prompt-input-attachments
components.title: PromptInputAttachments
components.description: A PromptInput with an attach row above it for file uploads.
components.whenToUse: Use it when attachments are a first-class part of the prompt and deserve their own row. Otherwise pass `onAttach` to PromptInput and use its built-in paperclip. Takes every PromptInput prop.
examples: <PromptInputWithAttachments value={prompt} onChange={setPrompt} onSubmit={send} onAttach={() => fileInput.current?.click()} hint="PDF or CSV, up to 10 MB" />

components.name: prompt-input
components.title: PromptInput
components.description: The AI chat composer: grows with content, sends on Enter, Shift+Enter for a newline.
components.whenToUse:
The whole shell takes the focus halo.

Use it at the bottom of any AI chat. Controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`); either way `onSubmit` receives the current text. Enter while an IME is composing does not send. For a plain multi-line field use Textarea.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled text.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the new text on every keystroke.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Fires with the text on Enter or the Send button, only when it is not blank.

props.name: onAttach
props.doc: Fires when the paperclip button is pressed. Open your file picker here.

props.name: toolbar
props.doc: Optional left-side toolbar content (model picker, chips…).

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the text area.

examples:
const [prompt, setPrompt] = React.useState("")
<PromptInput value={prompt} onChange={setPrompt} onSubmit={(text) => { send(text); setPrompt("") }} />

components.name: prompt-library
components.title: PromptLibrary
components.description: A searchable list of saved prompts, each a card with a title, tag and two-line preview.
components.whenToUse: Use it in an AI app's sidebar or a "/" picker so people can reuse prompts. Search filters by title, body and tag as you type; clicking a card calls `onSelect`. For command style search across actions use a command palette instead.

props.name: prompts
props.doc: Saved prompts to list and search.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Fires with the prompt whose card was clicked.

examples: <PromptLibrary prompts={[{ id: "sum", title: "Summarize thread", body: "Summarize this thread in five bullets.", tag: "Writing" }]} onSelect={(p) => setPrompt(p.body)} />

components.name: prose
components.title: Prose
components.description: Typography for long-form HTML you do not control: docs, blog posts, markdown output, model answers.
components.whenToUse: Wrap rendered markdown or plain HTML elements in it and they get the kit's headings, spacing, links, lists, code and quotes. For single headings or paragraphs in app UI use Heading and Text.
examples:
Install

Add components with npx shadcn add.

components.name: publish-bar
components.title: PublishBar
components.description: A status badge, a save note and Preview / Publish buttons for a CMS or editor.
components.whenToUse: Use it pinned above or below an editor to show draft, scheduled or published state. For a floating unsaved-changes prompt use a toast or a save bar instead.

props.name: status
props.doc: Current state, shown as a badge.

props.name: note
props.doc: Muted line next to the badge.

props.name: onPublish
props.doc: Fires when Publish is pressed.

props.name: onPreview
props.doc: Fires when Preview is pressed.

props.name: publishing
props.doc: True while publishing: the button is disabled and reads "Publishing…".

examples: <PublishBar status="draft" onPreview={openPreview} onPublish={publish} publishing={isPending} />

components.name: qr-code
components.title: QrCode
components.description: A QR code that needs no library. The encoder is in this file: byte mode, versions 1 to 40, all four error correction levels, Reed-Solomon codewords and spec penalty masking. Modules draw as one SVG path in `currentColor`, so the code follows your tokens; a logo can sit in a cleared well at level H; and Download SVG writes a standalone file.

props.name: value
props.doc: Text to encode, as UTF-8 bytes. URLs, Wi-Fi strings, payment payloads, anything.

props.name: size
props.doc: Rendered width and height in px. The SVG scales without blur.

props.name: level
props.doc: Error correction level. L 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30% of codewords recoverable. The logo well needs H.

props.name: fg
props.doc: Module colour. Any CSS colour; defaults to the current text colour so it follows your tokens.

props.name: bg
props.doc: Background colour behind the modules and quiet zone.

props.name: margin
props.doc: Quiet zone in modules on each side. The spec asks for 4; 2 is fine on a plain surface.

props.name: logoScale
props.doc: Width of the cleared centre well as a fraction of the symbol, used when a logo is passed.

props.name: mask
props.doc: Force a mask pattern (0 to 7) instead of picking the lowest penalty one.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Caption under the code. Defaults to the host of a URL value or the value itself. Pass an empty string to hide.

props.name: download
props.doc: Show the Download SVG button.

props.name: fileName
props.doc: File name for the download.

props.name: bare
props.doc: Render the bare SVG with no card, caption or button.

props.name: title
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "QR code for <value>".

props.name: children
props.doc: Logo or icon placed in a cleared centre well. Only rendered when `level` is "H".

components.name: quantity-stepper
components.title: QuantityStepper
components.description: Minus and plus buttons around a number, clamped between `min` and `max`.
components.whenToUse: Use it for cart quantities, seat counts and guest numbers where people nudge a small integer. For free numeric entry use NumberInput; for a continuous range use Slider.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled quantity.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting quantity when uncontrolled.

props.name: min
props.doc: Lowest allowed value; the minus button disables there.

props.name: max
props.doc: Highest allowed value; the plus button disables there.

props.name: step
props.doc: Amount each press adds or removes.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the clamped new value.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Names the group and the buttons, e.g. "Tickets" gives "Decrease tickets".

examples:
const [qty, setQty] = React.useState(1)
