<QuantityStepper value={qty} onChange={setQty} min={1} max={10} aria-label="Tickets" />

components.name: query-builder
components.title: QueryBuilder
components.description: Rows of "field / operator / value" filter clauses joined by AND, with add and remove.
components.whenToUse: Use it for advanced filters on issue lists, tables and logs. Controlled with `value` + `onChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. For quick one-tap filters use FilterBar or ChipFilter.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled clauses.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting clauses when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the full clause list after every edit, add or remove.

props.name: fields
props.doc: Field names offered in the first select.

props.name: operators
props.doc: Operators offered in the second select.

examples:
const [clauses, setClauses] = React.useState<Clause[]>([{ id: "1", field: "status", op: "is", value: "open" }])
<QueryBuilder value={clauses} onChange={setClauses} fields={["status", "assignee", "label"]} />

components.name: quota-bar
components.title: QuotaBar
components.description: A labelled usage meter that reads "used / max" and fills to the percentage.
components.whenToUse: Use it on billing and usage pages for anything metered against a limit. The fill turns warning at `warnAt` percent and danger once the limit is reached. For task progress toward a finish use Progress; for many quotas at once use ResourceQuotaGrid.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being metered; also the meter's accessible name.

props.name: used
props.doc: Amount consumed.

props.name: max
props.doc: The limit.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats `used` and `max` for display. Defaults to en-US grouping, so server and client render the same text.

props.name: warnAt
props.doc: Percent at which the fill turns to the warning tone.

examples:
<QuotaBar label="Seats" used={18} max={25} />
<QuotaBar label="Storage" used={46.2} max={50} format={(n) => `${n} GB`} />

components.name: radar-chart
components.title: RadarChart
components.description: A filled polygon over concentric rings, one axis per label.
components.whenToUse: Use it to compare five to eight scores on the same 0 to 1 scale, like a vendor or skill scorecard. The shape glides to new values on the data spring. For goals against targets use RadialChart; for exact comparisons use a bar chart.

props.name: labels
props.doc: One axis per label, drawn clockwise from the top.

props.name: values
props.doc: One value per label, from 0 to 1. Missing values count as 0.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name. The spoken label also lists every axis and its score.

examples: <RadarChart labels={["Speed", "Cost", "Support", "Docs", "Uptime"]} values={[0.8, 0.6, 0.9, 0.7, 0.95]} label="Vendor scorecard" />

components.name: radial-chart
components.title: RadialChart
components.description: A radial bar chart of concentric progress rings, each labelled at its start, with a legend and a centre total. Rings sweep to new values on the data spring when the data changes and the total rolls. Pass a single item to get a full radial progress ring.

props.name: data
props.doc: Rings, outermost first. One item renders a single radial progress ring.

props.name: periods
props.doc: Datasets to switch between with a segmented control. Ignored when `data` is set.

props.name: centerLabel
props.doc: Label under the centre total.

props.name: centerValue
props.doc: Override the centre value. Defaults to the average progress of all rings.

props.name: thickness
props.doc: Ring thickness in chart units (the chart is 240 wide).

props.name: gap
props.doc: Gap between rings in chart units.

components.name: radio-group
components.title: RadioGroup
components.description: Accessible single choice radios on Base UI, with arrow-key navigation built in.
components.whenToUse: Use it for two to six mutually exclusive options shown at once, each with a Label. For a compact switcher use SegmentedControl; for long lists use Select. Base UI's `onValueChange` receives `(value, eventDetails)`.
examples: setMethod(v as string)}>

components.name: range-slider
components.title: RangeSlider
components.description: A two-thumb slider for picking a low and high value. Both value bubbles show while either thumb is dragged.
components.whenToUse: Use it for price, date or size ranges. For one value use Slider. Values are plain number arrays `[low, high]`; `onValueCommitted` fires once on release, which is the place to query.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled `[low, high]`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting `[low, high]` when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Fires on every move with `[low, high]`.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.doc: Fires once when the user releases the thumb.

props.name: step
props.doc: Snap interval.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Range" unless `aria-labelledby` is set.

examples: <RangeSlider defaultValue={[20, 80]} min={0} max={200} step={5} aria-label="Price" onValueCommitted={([lo, hi]) => setPrice({ lo, hi })} />

components.name: rating
components.title: Rating
components.description: A row of stars people click or arrow through to give a 1 to `max` score.
components.whenToUse: Use it for reviews and feedback prompts. It is a radio group: Tab lands on the current star, arrow keys move and select, hover previews. Pass `readOnly` to display an average without input. For a numeric scale with labels use SegmentedControl.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled score, 0 for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting score when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the picked score.

props.name: max
props.doc: Number of stars.

props.name: readOnly
props.doc: Show the score without letting people change it.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the group.

components.name: reaction-bar
components.title: ReactionBar
components.description: Emoji reaction pills with counts; the ones you pressed get the accent border.
components.whenToUse: Use it under comments, chat messages and changelog posts. Without `onToggle` it keeps its own counts; with it, you own the data and pass back updated `reactions`. Each pill is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`.

props.name: reactions
props.doc: Pills to show, in order.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called with the emoji that was pressed. Omit it and the bar toggles its own counts.

examples: <ReactionBar reactions={[{ emoji: "👍", count: 3, active: true }, { emoji: "🎉", count: 1 }]} onToggle={(emoji) => toggleReaction(messageId, emoji)} />

components.name: read-receipt
components.title: ReadReceipt
components.description: One tick for sent, two for delivered, two accent ticks for read.
components.whenToUse: Use it next to a message timestamp in chat bubbles. It carries a spoken label ("Read"), so it is not silent for screen readers. For a full delivery timeline use a status list.

props.name: status
props.doc: Delivery state of the message.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Sent", "Delivered" or "Read".

examples: <ReadReceipt status="delivered" />

components.name: reasoning-block
components.title: ReasoningBlock
components.description: The model's thinking, folded by default; the title shimmers while active and reports how long it took when done.
components.whenToUse: Use it above an assistant message to hold chain-of-thought or tool reasoning. Folded content is inert, so it is skipped by Tab and screen readers until opened. Controlled with `open` + `onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultOpen`. For generic disclosure use Collapsible.

props.name: children
props.doc: The reasoning text or nodes shown when expanded.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start expanded when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled expanded state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Fires with the new expanded state when the header is pressed.

props.name: active
props.doc: True while the model is still thinking.

props.name: duration
props.doc: e.g. "4s" — renders "Thought for 4s" when not active.

examples: <ReasoningBlock active={isThinking} duration="4s">{reasoningText}</ReasoningBlock>

components.name: receipt
components.title: Receipt
components.description: A monospaced receipt card with an id, itemised lines and a ruled total.
components.whenToUse: Use it in order confirmations, billing history and chat answers that show a charge. Amounts are display strings, so format money before passing it. For an editable bill use an invoice table instead.

props.name: id
props.doc: Receipt number shown in the header.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Itemised lines, in order.

props.name: total
props.doc: Formatted grand total.

examples: <Receipt id="RCP-1042" lines={[{ label: "Pro plan", amount: "$49.00" }, { label: "Tax", amount: "$3.92" }]} total="$52.92" />

components.name: regenerate-bar
components.title: RegenerateBar
components.description: A "Not quite right?" footer under an AI answer with Regenerate and an optional Edit prompt button.
components.whenToUse: Use it at the end of an assistant message. For per-message copy, like and retry icons use a message actions row instead.

props.name: onRegenerate
props.doc: Fires when Regenerate is pressed.

props.name: onEdit
props.doc: Shows an Edit prompt button when set.

props.name: label
props.doc: Muted prompt on the left.

props.name: pending
props.doc: True while a new answer streams: Regenerate is disabled and its icon spins.

examples: <RegenerateBar onRegenerate={retry} onEdit={() => setEditing(true)} pending={isStreaming} />

components.name: region-picker
components.title: RegionPicker
components.description: A grid of selectable region cards, each with a name and a latency hint.
components.whenToUse: Use it in deploy and project setup flows to choose a data region. It is a radio group: Tab lands on the selected card, arrow keys move and select. For a plain list of options use RadioGroup or Select.

props.name: regions
props.doc: Regions to offer.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled region id.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting region id when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first region.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the picked region id.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the group.

examples:
const [region, setRegion] = React.useState("eu-west")
<RegionPicker value={region} onChange={setRegion} regions={[{ id: "eu-west", label: "EU West", latency: "42ms" }, { id: "us-east", label: "US East" }]} />

components.name: relative-time
components.title: RelativeTime
components.description: A time element that reads "3h ago" and carries the exact ISO timestamp for machines.
components.whenToUse: Use it in feeds, comments, activity logs and table cells. Hover shows the full local date. Set `live` to refresh the label every minute. Server and client may disagree by a minute, so the text is hydration-safe. An invalid date renders nothing. For a fixed date use a formatted string in a time element.

props.name: date
props.doc: The instant to describe: a Date or any string `new Date()` parses (ISO 8601 is safest). Defaults to three hours ago.

props.name: live
props.doc: Re-render once a minute so the label stays current.

examples:
<RelativeTime date={comment.createdAt} />
<RelativeTime date="2026-11-14T09:30:00Z" live />

components.name: reset-password-form
components.title: ResetPasswordForm
components.description: A "set a new password" card with confirm field and a mismatch check.
components.whenToUse: Use it on the page a password reset email links to. It checks the two fields match and meet `minLength` before calling `onSubmit`; send the token and password to your server there. For the "email me a link" step use a forgot password form.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the new password once both fields match.

props.name: minLength
props.doc: Minimum password length enforced by the browser.

examples: <ResetPasswordForm onSubmit={(password) => resetPassword({ token, password })} />

components.name: resizable-panels
components.title: ResizablePanels
components.description: Split panes for editors, inspectors and dashboards. Drag a handle to resize; the hairline swells to accent under the hand. Arrow keys move it, Shift jumps, Home and End slam it, Enter collapses a collapsible pane and a double click resets the pair. Controlled or uncontrolled sizes, nothing is persisted. With no children it renders a three pane editor demo.

props.name: children
props.doc: Panels and handles: `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` children, nestable. Leave empty for the editor demo.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Direction the panels are laid out in.

props.name: sizes
props.doc: Controlled sizes in percent, one per panel.

props.name: defaultSizes
props.doc: Starting sizes in percent when uncontrolled. Overrides each panel's `defaultSize`.

props.name: onSizesChange
props.doc: Fires with the new sizes on every drag, key press or snap.

props.name: keyboardStep
props.doc: Percent moved per arrow key. Shift multiplies by five.

props.name: left
props.doc: Two panel shorthand: content of the first panel.

props.name: right
props.doc: Two panel shorthand: content of the second panel.

props.name: initial
props.doc: Two panel shorthand: starting size of the first panel in percent.

examples:
Left pane

} right={

Right pane

} />

components.name: resource-quota-grid
components.title: ResourceQuotaGrid
components.description: A responsive grid of quota cards, one bar per metered resource, for plan and usage pages.
components.whenToUse: Each card is a QuotaBar, so bars turn warning near the limit and danger at it. For a single meter use QuotaBar directly.

props.name: items
props.doc: Metered resources to show. Defaults to a Lumen workspace on the Scale plan.

examples: <ResourceQuotaGrid items={[{ label: "Seats", used: 18, max: 25 }, { label: "Storage (GB)", used: 38, max: 50 }]} />

components.name: retry-block
components.title: RetryBlock
components.description: A danger alert explaining what failed, with a Try again button under it.
components.whenToUse: Use it where a fetch, upload or AI request failed and retrying might work. The alert is a live region, so the failure is announced. For a whole empty page use an error state or EmptyState.

props.name: title
props.doc: Bold first line of the alert.

props.name: description
props.doc: What happened and what to do.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Fires when Try again is pressed.

props.name: retrying
props.doc: True while the retry runs: the button is disabled and its icon spins.

examples: <RetryBlock title="Could not load invoices" description="The server did not answer." onRetry={refetch} retrying={isFetching} />

components.name: review-request-card
components.title: ReviewRequestCard
components.description: A pull request awaiting your review: title, repo, author avatar and Review / View diff buttons.
components.whenToUse: Use it in inboxes, dashboards and notification panels for code review requests. For a full PR row with checks and labels use a list item of your own.

props.name: title
props.doc: Pull request title, rendered as an h3.

props.name: repo
props.doc: Repository the PR lives in.

props.name: author
props.doc: Author name; the avatar shows its initials.

props.name: onReview
props.doc: Fires when Review is pressed.

props.name: onViewDiff
props.doc: Fires when View diff is pressed.

examples: <ReviewRequestCard title="Add invoice export" repo="lumen/web" author="Maya Chen" onReview={() => router.push(prUrl)} onViewDiff={openDiff} />

components.name: rich-text-toolbar
components.title: RichTextToolbar
components.description: A formatting bar (bold, italic, link, bullet and numbered lists) for a text editor.
components.whenToUse: Use it above a Textarea or a contenteditable editor. It is a real ARIA toolbar on Base UI: one Tab stop, arrow keys move between buttons. Wire `onAction` to your editor's commands. For a table's search and filter row use TableToolbar.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Fires with the action and its new pressed state whenever a button toggles.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the toolbar.

examples: <RichTextToolbar onAction={(action, pressed) => editor.chain().focus().run(action, pressed)} />

components.name: role-permission-matrix
components.title: RolePermissionMatrix
components.description: A permissions table with one checkbox per role and capability, for workspace access settings.
components.whenToUse: Rows are capabilities, columns are roles; each checkbox is named "<role> <permission>" for screen readers. Seed it with `isChecked` and listen with `onCheckedChange`. For assigning one role to one person use RolePicker.

props.name: roles
props.doc: Column headers. Defaults to Lumen's three workspace roles.

props.name: permissions
props.doc: Row labels, one per capability.

props.name: isChecked
props.doc: Starting state of each checkbox. Defaults to everything on except Member, who only reads.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.type: (role: string, permission: string, checked: boolean) => void
props.doc: Fires when a checkbox changes.

examples:
<RolePermissionMatrix
  roles={["Admin", "Member"]}
  permissions={["Read", "Edit"]}
  isChecked={(role, permission) => role === "Admin" || permission === "Read"}
  onCheckedChange={(role, permission, checked) => savePermission(role, permission, checked)}
/>

components.name: role-picker
components.title: RolePicker
components.description: Labelled radios for choosing one workspace role (Owner, Admin, Member by default).
components.whenToUse: Use it in invite dialogs and member settings. Built on RadioGroup, so arrow keys move and select. For editing what each role can do use RolePermissionMatrix.

props.name: roles
props.doc: Roles to offer, in order.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled role value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting role when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Fires with the picked role value.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the group.

examples: <RolePicker value={role} onValueChange={setRole} roles={[{ value: "admin", label: "Admin" }, { value: "viewer", label: "Viewer" }]} />

components.name: row-selection
components.title: RowSelection
components.description: The select checkbox for a data table row or header, with an indeterminate state.
components.whenToUse: Put one in each row's first cell and one in the header with `indeterminate` when only some rows are selected. It is a Checkbox with a default "Select row" name; give each row a specific one.

props.name: checked
props.doc: Whether the row is selected.

props.name: indeterminate
props.doc: Shows a dash: some, not all, rows are selected. Use on the header checkbox.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: Fires with the new checked state.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name. Defaults to "Select row".

examples:
<RowSelection checked={allSelected} indeterminate={someSelected} onCheckedChange={toggleAll} aria-label="Select all rows" />
<RowSelection checked={selected.has(row.id)} onCheckedChange={(on) => toggle(row.id, on)} aria-label={`Select ${row.name}`} />

components.name: sankey-chart
components.title: SankeyChart
components.description: A sankey diagram. Columns come from the links themselves, ribbons curve between nodes with a gradient from source to target, and hovering or focusing a node lights its flows while the rest fall back. Nodes are keyboard focusable with a spoken summary; a hidden table carries the data.

props.name: links
props.doc: Flows between node ids. Columns are computed from these.

props.name: nodes
props.doc: Optional node order, labels and colours. Unknown ids found in links are added automatically.

props.name: align
props.doc: "left" puts each node one column after its furthest source; "justify" also pushes nodes with no outgoing links to the last column.

props.name: height
props.doc: Chart height in px. The width follows the container.

props.name: nodePadding
props.doc: Vertical gap between nodes in a column, in px.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats values in labels, the tooltip text and the table.

props.name: unit
props.doc: Unit word for accessible labels, e.g. "visitors".

components.name: saved-views
components.title: SavedViews
components.description: A vertical list of saved filters ("My open", "Needs review") with counts, one selected.
components.whenToUse: Use it in an issue tracker or inbox sidebar. It is a single-select listbox: Tab lands on the selected view, Up and Down arrows move and select, Home and End jump. For top-level page navigation use a sidebar nav; for switching panels in place use Tabs.

props.name: views
props.doc: Views to list, in order.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selected view id.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting view id when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first view.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the picked view id.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the list.

examples: <SavedViews views={[{ id: "mine", name: "My open", count: 12 }, { id: "all", name: "All issues" }]} value={view} onChange={setView} />

components.name: schema-field-row
components.title: SchemaFieldRow
components.description: One row of an API or data schema: field name, required badge, type and description.
components.whenToUse: Stack several to document a request body, a webhook payload or a database table. Rows are responsive: three columns from `sm`, stacked below. For an interactive table use DataTable.

props.name: name
props.doc: Field name, shown in monospace.

props.name: type
props.doc: Type signature, shown in monospace, e.g. "string" or "Invoice[]".

props.name: required
props.doc: Adds a "required" badge.

props.name: description
props.doc: What the field means.

examples:
<SchemaFieldRow name="amount" type="integer" required description="Amount in cents." />
<SchemaFieldRow name="metadata" type="Record<string, string>" description="Up to 50 keys." />

components.name: scroll-area
components.title: ScrollArea
components.description: A scroll container with thin, themed scrollbars on Base UI; native scrolling underneath.
components.whenToUse: Give it a fixed height (or max height) and put long content inside. Set `orientation` to "horizontal" or "both" for sideways overflow. The viewport is keyboard focusable so arrow keys scroll it. For a whole page let the body scroll instead.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Which scrollbars to render.

examples: {longList}

components.name: search-input
components.title: SearchInput
components.description: A search field with a magnifier icon and a clear button that appears once there is text.
components.whenToUse: Use it for list filters, table search and site search. Escape or the clear button empties it and keeps focus in the field. Controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled. Clearing calls `onClear` and an `onChange` whose `target.value` is "". For a field with a result list use SearchWithResults; for a command launcher use CommandPalette.

props.name: size
props.doc: Field height: 32, 36 or 44px.

props.name: onClear
props.doc: Fires after the clear button or Escape empties the field.

props.name: containerClassName
props.doc: Classes for the outer field box; className goes to the inner input.

examples: <SearchInput aria-label="Search invoices" placeholder="Search invoices…" value={q} onChange={(e) => setQ(e.target.value)} />

components.name: search-with-results
components.title: SearchWithResults
components.description: A search field with a result list underneath, for global search and quick lookups.
components.whenToUse: Without `onSearch` it filters `results` by title and subtitle itself; with it, you fetch and pass back `results`. Pass `onSelect` to make each result a button. The result count is announced to screen readers. For a keyboard-first launcher use CommandPalette; for a field alone use SearchInput.

props.name: results
props.doc: Results to list. Defaults to a Lumen search across invoices, customers and deploys.

props.name: onSearch
props.doc: Called on every keystroke. Without it, the list filters itself by title and subtitle.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Makes each result a button and fires with the picked result.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Placeholder and accessible name of the field.

examples: <SearchWithResults results={hits} onSearch={setQuery} onSelect={(r) => router.push(`/items/${r.id}`)} />

components.name: seat-manager
components.title: SeatManager
components.description: A card listing workspace members with their roles, a seats-used count and an Invite button.
components.whenToUse: Use it on billing and team settings pages. The "N of M used" line is computed from `seats` and `limit`. For editing a member's role use RolePicker; for permissions use RolePermissionMatrix.

props.name: seats
props.doc: Members holding a seat, keyed by email.

props.name: limit
props.doc: Seats the plan includes.

props.name: onInvite
props.doc: Fires when Invite is pressed. The button disables once every seat is used.

examples: <SeatManager seats={[{ name: "Maya Chen", email: "maya@lumen.app", role: "Owner" }]} limit={10} onInvite={openInvite} />

components.name: secret-reveal
components.title: SecretReveal
components.description: A masked API key or token with Reveal and Copy buttons.
components.whenToUse: Use it on API key and webhook secret settings. Copy always copies the real secret, even while masked. Pass only `revealedValue` and the mask is generated, keeping the prefix and the last four characters. For a plain copyable value use CodeBlock or CopyButton.

props.name: value
props.doc: The masked text shown while hidden. Generated from `revealedValue` when omitted.

props.name: revealedValue
props.doc: The real secret, shown when revealed and always used for Copy.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the buttons, e.g. "API key" gives "Reveal API key" and "Copy API key".

props.name: defaultRevealed
props.doc: Start revealed.

examples: <SecretReveal revealedValue={apiKey} label="Live API key" />

components.name: section-header
components.title: SectionHeader
components.description: A section title with an optional description on the left and actions on the right.
components.whenToUse: Use it to head a settings group, a dashboard panel or a list. It renders an h2 by default; set `level` to keep the document outline correct. For a whole page title use PageHeader.

props.name: description
props.doc: Muted line under the title.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons or links aligned to the right; they wrap under the title on narrow screens.

props.name: level
props.doc: Heading level of the title: 2 renders h2, 3 renders h3, 4 renders h4.

examples:
<SectionHeader title="Members" description="People with access to this workspace." actions={<Button size="sm">Invite</Button>} />
<SectionHeader level={3} title="Danger zone" />

components.name: segmented-control
components.title: SegmentedControl
components.description: A row of options with a raised thumb that glides to the selected one.
components.whenToUse: Use it for two to five mutually exclusive views or modes (Monthly / Yearly, List / Board). It is a radio group: Tab lands on the selected option, arrows move and select, Home and End jump. Controlled with `value` + `onChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. For form fields use RadioGroup; for switching whole panels use Tabs; for on/off toolbar buttons use ToggleGroup.

props.name: options
props.doc: Full options.

props.name: items
props.doc: Shorthand: plain labels, value = label.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selected value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Starting value when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first option.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Fires with the newly selected value.

props.name: size
props.doc: Track height: 32, 36 or 44px.

props.name: fullWidth
props.doc: Stretch to the container and split space evenly.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name of the group. Always set one that says what is being chosen.

examples:
<SegmentedControl items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} defaultValue="Week" aria-label="Range" />
<SegmentedControl
  aria-label="Layout"
  value={layout}
  onChange={setLayout}
  options={[{ value: "list", label: "List", icon: <ListIcon /> }, { value: "board", label: "Board", icon: <KanbanIcon /> }]}
/>

components.name: select
components.title: Select
components.description: A styled single or multiple choice dropdown on Base UI, with keyboard typeahead and a check on the chosen item.
components.whenToUse: Use it for picking one option from five or more in forms and toolbars. For two to four options shown at once use RadioGroup or SegmentedControl; for searchable lists use a Combobox. Pass `items` to `Select` so `SelectValue` shows the label, not the raw value. Base UI's `onValueChange` receives `(value, eventDetails)`. Label the trigger with `aria-label` or a Label whose `htmlFor` matches the trigger `id`.
examples:
const items = [{ value: "usd", label: "US dollar" }, { value: "eur", label: "Euro" }]
<Select items={items} defaultValue="usd" onValueChange={(v) => setCurrency(v as string)}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Currency" className="w-48">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a currency" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    {items.map((i) => <SelectItem key={i.value} value={i.value}>{i.label}</SelectItem>)}
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

components.name: separator
components.title: Separator
components.description: A 1px hairline that divides content, horizontally or vertically.
components.whenToUse: Base UI Separator renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`. For a purely visual rule inside a list or menu use DropdownMenuSeparator; for a labelled break ("or continue with") put text beside two Separators.
examples: DocsAPI

components.name: server-error-state
components.title: ServerErrorState
components.description: A 500 error panel: status code, a plain-language headline, a retry button and a copyable request id for support.
components.whenToUse: Use it where a server call failed and the user can retry. For a missing page use NotFoundState; for an empty list use EmptyState; for an inline field error use FormField `error`.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line on what happened and what to do next.
props.default: "The request failed on our server. Re...

props.name: code
props.doc: Status code shown above the headline.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Called by the Retry button.

props.name: requestId
props.doc: Request id shown in mono and copied by the "Copy request id" button. Leave it out to hide both.

examples: <ServerErrorState onRetry={() => refetch()} requestId={error.requestId} />

components.name: session-list
components.title: SessionList
components.description: A list of signed-in devices with a revoke action on every session except the current one.
components.whenToUse: Use it on an account security page. For API keys use ApiKeyList instead.

props.name: sessions
props.doc: Active sessions, most recent first. Defaults to Maya Chen's Lumen sessions.

props.name: onRevoke
props.doc: Called with the session id when its Revoke button is pressed.

examples: <SessionList sessions={sessions} onRevoke={(id) => revokeSession(id)} />

components.name: settings-layout
components.title: SettingsLayout
components.description: A two-column settings page: a 200px nav rail beside stacked, divided SettingsSection blocks (one column on mobile).
components.whenToUse: Use SettingsLayout for the page frame and SettingsSection for each titled group of controls. For app-wide navigation use Sidebar instead.

props.name: nav
props.doc: Navigation rail content, usually links or SidebarNavItems.

props.name: navLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the navigation rail.

props.name: children
props.doc: The SettingsSection blocks.

examples:
<SettingsLayout nav={<SidebarNavItem active>Profile</SidebarNavItem>}>
  <SettingsSection title="Profile" description="How others see you.">…</SettingsSection>
</SettingsLayout>

components.name: sheet
components.title: Sheet
components.description: A side panel that slides over the page from any edge, with a scrim, a title bar and a close button.
components.whenToUse: Built on Base UI Dialog: focus is trapped inside, the page is inert and scroll-locked, Escape and the scrim close it, and focus returns to the trigger. Use Sheet for secondary tasks beside the page (filters, edit forms, mobile nav); use Dialog for a centred decision, Drawer for a bottom sheet on mobile.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Leave it out and the sheet renders its own "Open sheet" button.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called when the sheet asks to close: Escape, the scrim or the close button. Set `open` to false here.

props.name: side
props.doc: The edge the panel slides in from.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading in the title bar; also the dialog's accessible name.

props.name: children
props.doc: Panel content. Defaults to a Lumen invoice summary.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the panel itself, e.g. `max-w-xl` for a wider sheet.

examples:
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit</Button>
<Sheet open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} side="right" title="Edit customer">
  <form>…</form>
</Sheet>

components.name: shipping-address
components.title: ShippingAddress
components.description: A shipping address fieldset: full name, street address, city and postal code, with labels wired to inputs and browser autofill tokens.
components.whenToUse: Drop it inside a checkout `<form>`; inputs carry `name` attributes so FormData picks them up. Use BillingAddress for the payment address.

props.name: legend
props.doc: Legend read before the fields by screen readers.

examples: <form action={save}><ShippingAddress /><Button type="submit">Continue</Button></form>

components.name: shortcut-cheat-sheet
components.title: ShortcutCheatSheet
components.description: A titled card listing keyboard shortcuts: action on the left, keycaps on the right.
components.whenToUse: Use it in a help panel or behind a "?" shortcut. For a single inline shortcut hint use Kbd; for a searchable list of actions use CommandPalette.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Shortcuts to list. Defaults to a short set of app shortcuts.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading above the list.

examples: <ShortcutCheatSheet rows={[{ keys: ["⌘", "K"], action: "Command palette" }, { keys: ["?"], action: "Show shortcuts" }]} />

components.name: sidebar-section
components.title: SidebarSection
components.description: A titled group inside a Sidebar: a small uppercase label above a stack of SidebarNavItems.
components.whenToUse: The title names the group for screen readers (`role="group"`). Use one per cluster of links ("Workspace", "Settings"); the Sidebar itself is the outer frame.

props.name: title
props.doc: Group label. Leave it out for an unlabelled group.

props.name: children
props.doc: The SidebarNavItems in this group.

examples:
<SidebarSection title="Workspace">
  <SidebarNavItem active>Inbox</SidebarNavItem>
  <SidebarNavItem>Projects</SidebarNavItem>
</SidebarSection>

components.name: sidebar
components.title: Sidebar
components.description: An app sidebar frame (224px, or a 56px icon rail when `collapsed`) and its nav items.
components.whenToUse: Put a `<nav aria-label="Main">` of SidebarNavItems inside, grouped with SidebarSection. When the Sidebar is collapsed, nav item labels become screen-reader only, so items stay named. For a settings page frame use SettingsLayout; for a mobile slide-over use MobileNavDrawer or Sheet.

props.name: collapsed
props.doc: Narrow icon rail; labels are hidden visually but still read by screen readers.

examples:
<Sidebar collapsed={collapsed}>
  <nav aria-label="Main">
    <SidebarNavItem icon={<InboxIcon />} active>Inbox</SidebarNavItem>
  </nav>
</Sidebar>

components.name: sign-up-form
components.title: SignUpForm
components.description: A complete sign-up card: GitHub and Google buttons, then name, email and password fields and a submit button.
components.whenToUse: Fields use browser autofill tokens (`new-password` for the password) and native required checks. Use AuthCard to build your own variant; use SocialAuthRow alone for OAuth-only sign-in.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the field values on submit; the native submit is prevented.

props.name: signInHref
props.doc: Link target for "Sign in".

props.name: onGithub
props.doc: Called by "Continue with GitHub".

props.name: onGoogle
props.doc: Called by "Continue with Google".

examples: <SignUpForm onSubmit={({ name, email, password }) => signUp(name, email, password)} signInHref="/login" />

components.name: signature-pad
components.title: SignaturePad
components.description: A signature field drawn on a canvas with smooth, pressure-aware strokes, undo and clear, a typed-name fallback for keyboard users, and PNG export.
components.whenToUse: Both modes report through one `onChange`: a drawn signature or the typed name rendered in a script face, as a transparent PNG data URL, or null when empty. Store the data URL or upload it as an image.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with a PNG data URL after each stroke or typed change, or null when empty.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label; also names the canvas and the typed input.

props.name: height
props.doc: Canvas height in px.

components.name: skeleton
components.title: Skeleton
components.description: A sunken plate with a hairline sheen that sweeps once per 1.6s, standing in for content while it loads.
components.whenToUse: Size it with className to match the content it replaces (zero layout shift when the data lands). Skeletons are aria-hidden: mark the loading region `aria-busy="true"` and give it a status label. Use Spinner for a short action in a button; use SkeletonCard for a whole card placeholder.

components.name: skip-link
components.title: SkipLink
components.description: A "Skip to content" link, visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus, then pinned top-left.
components.whenToUse: Render it as the first focusable element in the layout. Its `href` must match the id of your main landmark, e.g. `<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>`, so focus lands there after the skip.
examples: <body><SkipLink href="#main" /><Header /><main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>…</main></body>

components.name: slash-command-menu
components.title: SlashCommandMenu
components.description: A floating list of slash commands filtered by what the user has typed after the slash.
components.whenToUse: Presentational: you own the editor and pass `query` (text after "/"). The list is a listbox with roving focus: Arrow Up/Down, Home/End move, Enter or click selects, Escape calls `onClose`. For a global action search use CommandPalette; for a menu from a button use DropdownMenu.

props.name: items
props.doc: Commands to offer. Defaults to Lumen's composer commands.

props.name: query
props.doc: The text typed after the slash; filters the list (case-insensitive substring).

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the chosen command.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called on Escape so you can hide the menu and return focus to the editor.

examples: {open ? <SlashCommandMenu query={afterSlash} onSelect={(c) => run(c.id)} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} /> : null}

components.name: slider
components.title: Slider
components.description: Hairline rail, keycap thumb and a value bubble while you drag or tab to it.
components.whenToUse:
One value, or a range when `defaultValue`/`value` is an array of two. Use Slider for a continuous or stepped number; use NumberInput when the exact value matters more than the feel, and Switch for on/off. Always name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Base UI for pointer, keyboard and form behaviour. Hairline rail with an accent fill, a raised keycap thumb whose ring grows on hover, drag and focus, and an ink value bubble that settles in above the thumb while you drag or tab to it. Optional marks sit under the rail. RTL needs Base UI's <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">, not only dir="rtl", or dragging and arrow keys run backwards.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats the value in the bubble and for screen readers.

props.name: marks
props.doc: Ticks under the rail. Pass `{ value, label }` to caption them.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Show the value above the thumb while dragging or focused.

examples:
<Slider aria-label="Volume" defaultValue={40} />
<Slider aria-label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 80]} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} marks={[0, 50, 100]} />

components.name: social-auth-row
components.title: SocialAuthRow
components.description: Two outline buttons, "Continue with GitHub" and "Continue with Google", side by side for OAuth sign-in.
components.whenToUse: Put it at the top of an AuthCard, above an email form. SignUpForm already includes it.

props.name: onGithub
props.doc: Called by "Continue with GitHub".

props.name: onGoogle
props.doc: Called by "Continue with Google".

examples: <SocialAuthRow onGithub={() => signIn("github")} onGoogle={() => signIn("google")} />

components.name: social-proof
components.title: SocialProof
components.description: A stack of up to five customer avatars beside a short trust line, for hero and signup sections.
components.whenToUse: The avatars are decorative; the trust line is what screen readers hear. Only claim numbers you can back up. For quotes use Testimonial; for a row of logos use LogoCloud.

props.name: countLabel
props.doc: The trust line shown next to the avatars.

props.name: people
props.doc: People to show; only the first five are rendered.

examples: <SocialProof countLabel="Used by 40 teams in our beta" people={[{ name: "Maya Chen", src: "/maya.jpg" }]} />

components.name: sortable-header
components.title: SortableHeader
components.description: A table column header button that shows and toggles sort direction (none, ascending, descending).
components.whenToUse: Put it inside a `<TableHead>` and set `aria-sort` on that header cell to match ("ascending" | "descending" | "none"); screen readers read sort state from the cell. Use TableToolbar for filters and search above the table.

props.name: label
props.doc: Column name.

props.name: direction
props.doc: Current sort; `false` or undefined means unsorted.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called on click; cycle the direction in your state.

examples:
<TableHead aria-sort={dir === "asc" ? "ascending" : dir === "desc" ? "descending" : "none"}>
  <SortableHeader label="Amount" direction={dir} onToggle={cycle} />
</TableHead>

components.name: sortable-list
components.title: SortableList
components.description: A drag-to-reorder list: drag the grip handle, or focus it and use the arrow keys; every move is announced and the new order comes back through onReorder.
components.whenToUse:
Built on Motion's Reorder.

Keyboard: Arrow Up/Down move one place, Home/End move to the ends; focus stays on the moved handle. Pass a new `items` array (different ids or order) to reset the list from outside.

props.name: items
props.doc: Rows in their starting order. Defaults to a short sample task list.

props.name: onReorder
props.doc: Called with the full list after every drag or keyboard move.

examples: <SortableList items={tasks} onReorder={(next) => saveOrder(next.map((t) => t.id))} />

components.name: source-card
components.title: SourceCard
components.description: A citation card for AI answers and RAG results: source title, its URL or path in mono, and a quoted snippet.
components.whenToUse: Show one per retrieved source under a StreamingMessage. When `href` is set the title becomes a link.

props.name: title
props.doc: Source name, e.g. a document title.

props.name: url
props.doc: URL or path shown under the title.

props.name: href
props.doc: Opens the source; makes the title a link.

props.name: snippet
props.doc: The quoted passage the answer relied on.

props.name: badge
props.doc: Badge text in the corner.

examples: <SourceCard title="Billing API" url="docs.acme.com/billing" href="https://docs.acme.com/billing" snippet="Invoices are finalised after 1 hour." />

components.name: sparkline-set
components.title: SparklineSet
components.description: A grid of KPI cards, each with a value, a delta and a small area sparkline, for dashboard overviews.
components.whenToUse: Use it for 2 to 6 headline metrics. For one metric use StatSparkline or StatCard; for a single flat row of numbers without charts use StatsStrip.

props.name: items
props.doc: One card per metric. Defaults to Lumen's revenue, customer and churn trends.

examples: <SparklineSet items={[{ label: "Revenue", value: "$12,400", delta: 8.2, data: [4, 6, 5, 8, 9] }]} />

components.name: spinner
components.title: Spinner
components.description: A small accent ring that spins while something loads; announced once as a status with its label.
components.whenToUse: Use it inside a button or beside text for short waits. Use Skeleton when the layout of the incoming content is known, and a Progress bar when you know how far along it is.

props.name: size
props.doc: 14px, 16px or 24px.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name read by screen readers.

examples: <Button disabled><Spinner size="sm" label="Saving" /> Saving</Button>

components.name: split-button
components.title: SplitButton
components.description: A primary action with an attached chevron that opens a menu of related actions.
components.whenToUse: Use it when one action is the obvious default and two to five close variants sit behind it ("Save" / "Save draft", "Merge" / "Squash and merge"). For unrelated actions use DropdownMenu on its own; for a single action use Button.

props.name: label
props.doc: The primary action's label.

props.name: onPrimaryClick
props.doc: Called by the primary (left) button.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables both halves.

props.name: menuLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the chevron that opens the menu.

props.name: items
props.doc: Secondary actions in the menu; the menu matches the button's width.

examples:
<SplitButton
  label="Merge"
  onPrimaryClick={merge}
  items={[{ label: "Squash and merge", onSelect: squash }, { label: "Close pull request", destructive: true, onSelect: close }]}
/>

components.name: split-flap
components.title: SplitFlap
components.description: A departure-board display where each character flips through the alphabet to its target, rippling across the row like a Solari board.
components.whenToUse:
Top half falls over the bottom with a staggered start per column. Screen readers get the final text once; the flipping is decoration.

The board is always dark (it scopes the dark tokens to itself). Supported characters: A-Z, 0-9, space and : . - ' / ·; anything else shows blank. Use it for a headline status or a launch moment; for a changing number in a dashboard use NumberRoll, which is quieter.

props.name: value
props.doc: Text to flip to. Change it to flip again from the current characters.

props.name: length
props.doc: Pad or cut to this many cells.

props.name: speed
props.doc: Milliseconds per single flip.

props.name: stagger
props.doc: Extra delay per column, for the ripple.

props.name: size
props.doc: Cell size: 24px, 32px or 48px tall.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Colour of the characters.

examples: <SplitFlap value="GATE 12" length={8} tone="accent" />

components.name: split-pane
components.title: SplitPane
components.description: Two equal panes side by side in one bordered frame, stacked on mobile: for before/after, code/preview or source/result.
components.whenToUse: Static 50/50 layout; for a draggable divider use ResizablePanels. Panes clip overflow to the frame, so put scrolling content in its own `overflow-auto` box.

props.name: left
props.doc: First pane (top on mobile).

props.name: right
props.doc: Second pane (bottom on mobile).

examples: <SplitPane left={<CodeBlock code={src} />} right={<Preview />} />

components.name: sql-result-table
components.title: SqlResultTable
components.description: A compact result grid for SQL query output: uppercase column headers, mono cells, NULL shown dimmed, and a scrollable frame.
components.whenToUse: Use it under a query editor or in an AI agent's tool-call output. For an app data table with sorting, selection and pagination use Table with SortableHeader and TablePagination.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Column names in order.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Result rows; each row lines up with `columns`. `null` renders as a dimmed NULL.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Screen-reader caption, e.g. the table name and row count.

examples: <SqlResultTable columns={["id", "email"]} rows={[[1, "maya@lumen.app"], [2, null]]} caption="users, 2 rows" />

components.name: sso-provider-card
components.title: SsoProviderCard
components.description: A settings card for one SSO identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace): name, status badge, enable switch and Configure button.
components.whenToUse: Render one per provider in an organisation's security settings. The switch is controlled: pass `enabled` and update it in `onEnabledChange`.

props.name: name
props.doc: Provider name, e.g. "Okta".

props.name: description
props.doc: Protocol or a one-line note, e.g. "SAML 2.0 · 12 users".

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether sign-in through this provider is on.

props.name: configured
props.doc: Shows "Configured" (success) instead of "Not set".

props.name: onEnabledChange
props.doc: Called with the new value when the switch is toggled.

props.name: onConfigure
props.doc: Called by the Configure button.

examples: <SsoProviderCard name="Okta" description="SAML 2.0" configured enabled={on} onEnabledChange={setOn} onConfigure={openSetup} />

components.name: stack-trace
components.title: StackTrace
components.description: A scrollable, monospaced error stack in the danger tone, preserving line breaks and indentation.
components.whenToUse: Use it in error pages, logs and AI tool-call failures. For general code use CodeBlock; for an error summary with retry use ServerErrorState.

props.name: stack
props.doc: The raw stack text, e.g. `error.stack`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the scroll region.

examples: <StackTrace stack={error.stack ?? String(error)} />

components.name: stack
components.title: Stack
components.description: A vertical flex column with a fixed gap from the 4px spacing scale.
components.whenToUse: Use it to space sibling blocks evenly without margin utilities. For horizontal rows use `flex gap-*` directly; for a page grid use CSS grid.

props.name: gap
props.doc: Gap in 4px steps: 1 = 4px, 3 = 12px, 8 = 32px. A `gap-*` class in className also works.

examples: <Stack gap={4}><Heading /><Text /><Button>Continue</Button></Stack>

components.name: stacked-bar-chart
components.title: StackedBarChart
components.description: Vertical bars stacked by series, with a legend, for comparing revenue mix across periods.
components.whenToUse: Screen readers get the numbers as a hidden data table. Use it for part-to-whole over time with 2 to 4 series; use BarChart for one series and AreaChart for continuous trends.

props.name: data
props.doc: One stack per period; `values` line up with `seriesLabels`. Defaults to eight months of Lumen revenue.

props.name: seriesLabels
props.doc: Names of the stacked series, bottom to top.

props.name: label
props.doc: Chart title for screen readers.

examples:
<StackedBarChart
  label="Revenue mix by month"
  seriesLabels={["Subscriptions", "Usage"]}
  data={[{ label: "Jan", values: [48, 14] }, { label: "Feb", values: [52, 16] }]}
/>

components.name: stat-card
components.title: StatCard
components.description: Label, a big tabular value, and a delta chip that colours itself.
components.whenToUse: The delta tone comes from its leading sign: "+", "▲" read as up (success), "-", "−", "▼" as down (danger); set `invertDelta` where down is good. For a value with a trend line use StatSparkline; for several numbers in one row use StatsStrip.

props.name: label
props.doc: Metric name.

props.name: value
props.doc: Pre-formatted value, e.g. "$48,200".

props.name: delta
props.doc: Change as a signed string, e.g. "+8.2%" or "−3".

props.name: icon
props.doc: Small icon before the label.

props.name: footnote
props.doc: Muted line under the value, e.g. "vs last month".

props.name: invertDelta
props.doc: For metrics where down is good (churn, latency).

examples:
<StatCard label="MRR" value="$48,200" delta="+8.2%" footnote="vs last month" />
<StatCard label="p95 latency" value="182 ms" delta="-12%" invertDelta />

components.name: stat-sparkline
components.title: StatSparkline
components.description: A KPI card with a big number, a coloured delta and a trend sparkline bleeding off the bottom edge.
components.whenToUse: Exported as `StatWithSparkline`. Use it for one headline metric with its trend; use StatCard without a chart, and SparklineSet for a grid of several.
examples: <StatWithSparkline label="MRR" value="$48,200" delta="+8.2%" points={[31, 34, 33, 38, 41, 48]} />

components.name: stats-strip
components.title: StatsStrip
components.description: A hairline-divided row of headline numbers, for landing pages and report headers.
components.whenToUse: Marked up as a description list so each value is read with its label. Use real, sourced figures only. For dashboard metrics with deltas use StatCard; with trend lines, SparklineSet.

props.name: stats
props.doc: Headline figures, four reads best. Defaults to Lumen's company stats.

examples: <StatsStrip stats={[{ label: "Components", value: "300+" }, { label: "Dependencies", value: "2" }]} />

components.name: status-badge
components.title: StatusBadge
components.description: A status pill with a tinted fill, hairline edge and a leading dot, in six tones that share lightness.
components.whenToUse:
Tones share lightness so a row of badges reads as one set.

Use it for the state of a record ("Paid", "Failed", "Draft"); the text carries the meaning, the colour reinforces it. For counts and categories use Badge; for a bare dot use StatusDot.
examples:
<StatusBadge tone="success">Paid</StatusBadge>
<StatusBadge tone="danger">Failed</StatusBadge>

components.name: status-dot
components.title: StatusDot
components.description: An 8px coloured dot for status beside text: online, degraded, failed.
components.whenToUse: Decorative by default (the adjacent text says the status). When the dot stands alone, pass `label` so screen readers hear it. For a dot inside a pill use StatusBadge.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name when the dot is shown without text; leave out when text sits beside it.

examples: Operational

components.name: step-progress
components.title: StepProgress
components.description: A row of labelled segments that fill as a multi-step flow advances, for onboarding and checkout.
components.whenToUse: Read-only progress, not navigation. Use Stepper for the numbered variant ("1. Details"); use Progress for a single percentage.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Step labels in order. Defaults to Lumen's workspace setup.

props.name: current
props.doc: Zero-based index of the active step; earlier steps count as done.

examples: <StepProgress steps={["Account", "Company", "Review"]} current={1} />

components.name: stepper
components.title: Stepper
components.description: A numbered progress bar for multi-step forms: one segment per step, filled up to the current one, with "1. Details" style labels.
components.whenToUse: Read-only progress, not navigation. Use StepProgress for the unnumbered, smaller-label variant. Keep `current` in your form state and render the step's fields below.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Step labels in order.

props.name: current
props.doc: Zero-based index of the active step; earlier steps count as done.

examples: <Stepper steps={["Details", "Members", "Billing"]} current={step} />

components.name: sticky-bar
components.title: StickyBar
components.description: A bar pinned to the bottom of its scroll container for page-level actions: "3 selected · Delete", "Unsaved changes · Save".
components.whenToUse: Opaque surface with a hairline top edge, no blur. Put it last inside the scrolling element. Give it `role="region"` and an `aria-label` when it holds important actions. For one floating action use FloatingActionButton.
examples: Unsaved changes

components.name: sticky-column
components.title: StickyColumn
components.description: A cell wrapper that stays pinned to the left or right edge while a wide table or board scrolls horizontally.
components.whenToUse: Opaque so scrolled content passes underneath, with a hairline on the inner edge. The scroll container needs `overflow-x-auto`. For a sticky header row use `sticky top-0` on the thead.

props.name: side
props.doc: Edge to pin to.

examples:
Customer
…

components.name: stop-generating
components.title: StopGenerating
components.description: An outline button with a stop square that cancels an in-flight AI response.
components.whenToUse: Show it only while a response streams, next to the StreamingMessage or in the composer; wire `onClick` to your AbortController. AiComposer swaps its send button for a stop button itself.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Called when pressed; abort the request here.

props.name: label
props.doc: Button text.

examples: {isStreaming ? <StopGenerating onClick={() => controller.abort()} /> : null}

components.name: streak-calendar
components.title: StreakCalendar
components.description: A 7-column grid of day tiles, filled in accent on active days, for habit and contribution streaks.
components.whenToUse: Days are numbered from 1. Screen readers hear a summary ("17 of 28 days active"). For a year-long contribution graph build rows of HeatmapCell.

props.name: active
props.doc: Active day numbers, 1-based.

props.name: days
props.doc: How many days to show, in rows of seven.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading above the grid. Defaults to "{days}-day streak".

examples: <StreakCalendar active={[1, 2, 3, 5, 8]} days={28} />

components.name: streaming-cursor
components.title: StreamingCursor
components.description: A blinking 2px accent caret to append after text that is still streaming in.
components.whenToUse: Decorative (aria-hidden). Render it only while tokens arrive and remove it when the stream ends. StreamingMessage already includes it.
examples: {text}{isStreaming ? : null}

components.name: streaming-message
components.title: StreamingMessage
components.description: An assistant message bubble that shows text as it streams, with a blinking caret while `streaming` is true.
components.whenToUse: Marked `aria-busy` while streaming so screen readers wait for the finished text instead of reading every token. Pair with StopGenerating; render finished markdown in your own message view.

props.name: content
props.doc: The text received so far.

props.name: streaming
props.doc: Shows the caret and marks the message busy. Set false when the stream ends.

examples: <StreamingMessage content={partialText} streaming={!done} />

components.name: suggestion-chips
components.title: SuggestionChips
components.description: A wrap of pill buttons offering follow-up prompts in an AI chat ("Summarize", "Find bugs").
components.whenToUse: Clicking a chip calls `onSelect` with its text; send it or put it in the composer. For filters that stay on use ToggleGroup.

props.name: items
props.doc: Prompt texts, one chip each.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the chip's text.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the group.

examples: <SuggestionChips items={["Summarize", "Explain this code"]} onSelect={(text) => send(text)} />

components.name: switch
components.title: Switch
components.description: Hairline track with a raised thumb that leans on press, then springs across. While pressed the thumb stretches toward where it is about to go. The track only changes colour. 44px hit area via ::after. Pass `label` (+ `description`) for a settings row where the whole row is clickable.
components.whenToUse: Use Switch for a setting that applies immediately; use Checkbox for a choice submitted with a form, and ToggleGroup for picking one of several options. Controlled with `checked` + `onCheckedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultChecked`. Without `label`, give it an `aria-label`.

props.name: size
props.doc: Track size: 16x28 or 20x36.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows a spinner in the thumb. Stays focusable but can't be toggled.

props.name: label
props.doc: Renders a settings row: label on the left, switch on the right, whole row clickable.

props.name: description
props.doc: Muted helper line under `label`; linked with aria-describedby.

examples:
<Switch aria-label="Dark mode" checked={dark} onCheckedChange={setDark} />
<Switch label="Email alerts" description="A digest every morning." defaultChecked />

components.name: table-of-contents
components.title: TableOfContents
components.description: A table of contents for long pages. It reads h2 and h3 headings from a container, or takes explicit items, then watches the nearest scroll area and moves an accent marker to the heading you are reading. Clicking an item scrolls there smoothly and hands focus to the heading. With no props it renders a scrollable Lumen docs article next to the list so the spy can be seen working.

props.name: items
props.doc: Headings to list. When absent, h2 and h3 elements are read from `selector` after mount.

props.name: selector
props.doc: CSS selector of the container to read headings from when `items` is absent. Headings without an id get one.

props.name: title
props.doc: Small label above the list. Empty hides it.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Pixels between the top of the scroll area and a heading for it to count as reached.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.doc: Called when the active heading changes.

props.name: sticky
props.doc: Keep the list in view while the page scrolls (position sticky).

components.name: table-pagination
components.title: TablePagination
components.description: Previous/next pagination for a data table, with a "Page 2 of 9" readout.
components.whenToUse: Pages are 1-based and controlled: keep `page` in state and set it in `onPageChange`. Page changes are announced to screen readers. For numbered page links on content pages use Pagination.

props.name: page
props.doc: Current page, 1-based.

props.name: pageCount
props.doc: Total pages; 0 is shown as 1.

props.name: onPageChange
props.doc: Called with the requested page number.

examples: <TablePagination page={page} pageCount={Math.ceil(total / 20)} onPageChange={setPage} />

components.name: table-toolbar
components.title: TableToolbar
components.description: The bar above a data table: a search field on the left, your filters and actions on the right.
components.whenToUse: Search is controlled: pass `search` and update it in `onSearchChange`, then filter rows yourself. Pair with Table, SortableHeader and TablePagination.

props.name: children
props.doc: Filters and actions, right-aligned.

props.name: search
props.doc: Current search text.

props.name: onSearchChange
props.doc: Called with the new search text on every keystroke.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: Placeholder for the search field.

props.name: searchLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the search field.

examples:
<TableToolbar search={q} onSearchChange={setQ} searchPlaceholder="Search invoices…">
  <Button size="sm">New invoice</Button>
</TableToolbar>

components.name: table
components.title: Table
components.description: A semantic HTML table with hairline row dividers, a hover tint and horizontal scroll on narrow screens.
components.whenToUse: Compose Table > TableHeader/TableBody/TableFooter > TableRow > TableHead/TableCell, plus an optional TableCaption. Numbers line up (tabular-nums). Add SortableHeader inside a TableHead (set `aria-sort` on the TableHead), TableToolbar above and TablePagination below. Mark a selected row with `data-selected` or `aria-selected`. For SQL output use SqlResultTable.
examples: InvoiceAmountINV-2041$12,400.00

components.name: tabs
components.title: Tabs
components.description: A raised thumb or accent underline that glides to the active tab. Base UI for roving focus and panels. The active tab carries one indicator per list (a raised thumb, or a 2px accent underline for `line`) that glides between tabs on a spring, the way segmented-control does.
components.whenToUse: Keyboard per WAI-ARIA tabs: Arrow keys move between tabs, Home/End jump, Tab moves into the panel. Use Tabs to switch between panels of content in place; use SegmentedControl for a compact value picker without panels, and links (not tabs) when each view has its own URL. Every TabsTrigger `value` needs a TabsContent with the same `value`.
examples:
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList variant="line">
    <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="invoices" badge={12}>Invoices</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="overview">…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="invoices">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>

components.name: tags-input
components.title: TagsInput
components.description: A text field that turns typed entries into removable tag chips (Enter or comma adds, Backspace removes the last).
components.whenToUse: Use it for free-form labels, emails or keywords. Reach for `MultiSelect` when values must come from a fixed list, or `MentionInput` for @mentions inside text.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled tags. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial tags for the uncontrolled field.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the full next list whenever a tag is added or removed.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown only while there are no tags.

props.name: max
props.doc: Most tags allowed; further entries are ignored.

props.name: id
props.doc: Id for the inner text input, so a `<Label htmlFor>` can point at it.

examples: <TagsInput defaultValue={["finance", "q3"]} onChange={setTags} aria-label="Invoice labels" />

components.name: tax-fields
components.title: TaxFields
components.description: Country and tax ID fields side by side, for checkout and billing-details forms.
components.whenToUse: Uncontrolled inputs with `name`s, so they submit with a plain `<form>`. Pair it with `BillingAddress` for the full postal address.

props.name: defaultCountry
props.doc: Initial country.

props.name: defaultTaxId
props.doc: Initial VAT, GST or EIN number.

props.name: namePrefix
props.doc: Prefix for the field names: `${namePrefix}country` and `${namePrefix}taxId`.

examples: <form action={saveBilling}><TaxFields defaultCountry="Germany" /></form>

components.name: team-member-row
components.title: TeamMemberRow
components.description: One teammate in a members list: avatar, name, email and a role badge, with an optional trailing actions slot.
components.whenToUse: Stack several inside a bordered card; the last row drops its divider. Use `AdminUserRow` when you need presence and a permission chip.

props.name: role
props.doc: Free text shown in an outline badge, e.g. "Admin" or "Member".

props.name: src
props.doc: Avatar image; initials are used when absent.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Trailing controls such as a role picker or an overflow menu.

examples: <TeamMemberRow name="Priya Raman" email="priya@northwind.com" role="Owner" actions={<RowMenu />} />

components.name: terminal-window
components.title: TerminalWindow
components.description: A terminal frame with traffic-light dots and a title bar around monospace output, for install steps and CLI demos.
components.whenToUse: Children render inside a `<pre>`, so whitespace is kept. Use `CodeBlock` for highlighted source with a copy button, and `ConsoleOutput` for streaming log lines.

props.name: title
props.doc: Title bar text; also names the scrollable output for screen readers.

props.name: children
props.doc: Output text. Whitespace and line breaks are preserved.

examples: <TerminalWindow title="zsh">{"$ npx shadcn add https://ui.minidev.pro/r/button.json"}</TerminalWindow>

components.name: testimonial
components.title: Testimonial
components.description: A quote card with the customer's avatar, name and role, for landing pages and case studies.
components.whenToUse: Renders a semantic `<figure>` with `<blockquote>` and `<figcaption>`. Use `PressQuote` for a publication pull quote. Only quote real customers.

props.name: quote
props.doc: The quote, without quotation marks; curly quotes are added.

props.name: name
props.doc: Person quoted. Also drives the avatar initials.

props.name: role
props.doc: Title and company, e.g. "Head of Finance, Northwind".

props.name: src
props.doc: Avatar image; initials are used when absent.

examples: <Testimonial quote="Month-end close went from six days to two." name="Maya Chen" role="Head of Finance, Northwind" />

components.name: text
components.title: Text
components.description: Body copy: a 14px paragraph with the kit's line height, in default, muted, subtle or mono flavours.
components.whenToUse:
Renders a `

` and accepts every paragraph prop. Use `Heading` for titles and `Prose` for long-form rich text.

props.name: muted
props.doc: Secondary text colour (`text-fg-muted`, at least 7:1).

props.name: subtle
props.doc: Tertiary text colour (`text-fg-subtle`, at least 4.5:1) for hints and meta.

props.name: mono
props.doc: Geist Mono at 13px, for ids, amounts and code-like values.

examples: <Text muted>Invoices are emailed to billing@northwind.com.</Text>

components.name: textarea
components.title: Textarea
components.description: A multi-line text field styled like `Input`: hairline border, accent focus halo, invalid and read-only states.
components.whenToUse: Accepts every `<textarea>` prop. Set `autoResize` to grow with the content. Use `PromptInput` for chat composers and `MarkdownEditor` for formatted text.

props.name: autoResize
props.doc: Grow with the content (CSS `field-sizing: content`); `rows` sets the minimum height. Browsers without support keep a fixed height.

examples: <Textarea id="note" placeholder="Add a note to the customer" rows={4} autoResize aria-invalid={!!error} />

components.name: theme-picker
components.title: ThemePicker
components.description: A three-way Light / Dark / System radio group. Pass `applyToDocument` to have it toggle the `dark` class on `<html>`.
components.whenToUse: Works uncontrolled, or controlled with `value` + `onChange` when you persist the choice (cookie, localStorage). Arrow keys move and select, per the WAI-ARIA radio group pattern. Use `SegmentedControl` for any other small exclusive choice.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled mode. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial mode for the uncontrolled picker.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen mode.

props.name: applyToDocument
props.doc: Toggle the `dark` class on `<html>` when the mode changes. Off by default so demos and apps that apply the theme themselves are not affected.

examples: <ThemePicker applyToDocument value={mode} onChange={(m) => { setMode(m); localStorage.theme = m }} />

components.name: thinking-block
components.title: ThinkingBlock
components.description: A collapsible "Thinking" disclosure for a model's hidden reasoning in a chat transcript, closed by default.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one plain block of reasoning text. Use `ReasoningBlock` for streamed, step-by-step reasoning with a timer, and `ToolCallCard` for tool invocations.

props.name: children
props.doc: The reasoning text.

props.name: label
props.doc: Header text, e.g. "Thinking…" while streaming or "Thought for 4s" when done.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state for the uncontrolled block.

examples: <ThinkingBlock label="Thought for 4s">Checking which invoices are overdue before drafting the reminder…</ThinkingBlock>

components.name: time-picker
components.title: TimePicker
components.description: A native time field (`<input type="time">`) in the kit's input styling; the value is a 24-hour "HH:mm" string.
components.whenToUse: The browser supplies the locale-aware picker and keyboard support. Works controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`), and passes through `name`, `min`, `max`, `step` and `required`. Use `DatePicker` for dates.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled value, "HH:mm" (or "HH:mm:ss" with a seconds `step`). Use "" for empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial value for the uncontrolled field.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new "HH:mm" string, or "" when cleared.

props.name: size
props.doc: Field height.

examples: <TimePicker value={time} onChange={setTime} min="09:00" max="17:00" aria-label="Standup time" />

components.name: timeline
components.title: Timeline
components.description: A vertical list of dated events on a hairline, for activity feeds and audit logs.
components.whenToUse: Renders an ordered list, newest first. Use `ActivityFeed` when each event needs an avatar, and `AuditTrail` for who-did-what logs.

props.name: items
props.doc: Events, newest first. Defaults to a day of Lumen workspace activity.

examples: <Timeline items={[{ title: "Invoice INV-2041 paid", description: "$12,400 from Northwind", time: "09:41", dateTime: "2026-03-12T09:41" }]} />

components.name: toast
components.title: Toast
components.description: A single notification card: status glyph, title, optional description and action. Use `<Toaster />` + `toast()` for the stacked system.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Sets the glyph and the live role: "danger" is announced assertively (role="alert"), the rest politely.

props.name: action
props.doc: One inline action, e.g. Undo or View.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Shows a dismiss button (on hover or focus) when provided.

props.name: role
props.doc: Override the live role. The Toaster passes "none" because its list is already the live region.

examples: <Toast title="Saved" description="Changes are live." tone="success" />

components.name: toc
components.title: Toc
components.description: An indented table of contents for a docs page, with the current section highlighted.
components.whenToUse: Links jump to `#id` anchors. Pass `activeId` from your own scroll-spy (IntersectionObserver) to follow the reader; without it the last clicked entry is marked. Use `TableOfContents` for built-in scroll-spy and a sticky rail.

props.name: items
props.doc: Headings in page order. Defaults to the Lumen API guide.

props.name: activeId
props.doc: The id of the section in view. Without it, clicks track the active entry.

examples: <Toc items={[{ id: "install", title: "Install" }, { id: "usage", title: "Usage", level: 2 }]} activeId={visibleId} />

components.name: toggle-group
components.title: ToggleGroup
components.description: A row of `Toggle` buttons that share pressed state, built on Base UI: single-select by default, `multiple` for formatting bars.
components.whenToUse: `value` is always an array of the pressed toggles' `value`s. Arrow keys move focus between toggles. Use `SegmentedControl` for a view switch with a sliding thumb, and `RadioGroup` inside forms.
examples:
<ToggleGroup defaultValue={["left"]} aria-label="Text alignment">
  <Toggle value="left" aria-label="Align left"><AlignLeftIcon /></Toggle>
  <Toggle value="center" aria-label="Align center"><AlignCenterIcon /></Toggle>
</ToggleGroup>

components.name: toggle
components.title: Toggle
components.description: A two-state button (pressed or not) for toolbar actions such as bold or "show archived", built on Base UI.
components.whenToUse: Controlled with `pressed` + `onPressedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultPressed`. Icon-only toggles need an `aria-label`. Use `Switch` for settings that take effect immediately, and `ToggleGroup` for a set of related toggles.
examples: <Toggle aria-label="Bold" pressed={bold} onPressedChange={setBold}><BoldIcon /></Toggle>

components.name: token-usage-meter
components.title: TokenUsageMeter
components.description: A card showing LLM tokens used against a budget: label, "used / limit" in mono, a progress bar and a note.
components.whenToUse: Use it on AI usage and billing pages. Use `UsageMeter` for a bare labelled bar, `UsageBreakdown` for several resources, and `CreditBalance` for prepaid credits.

props.name: used
props.doc: Tokens used so far.

props.name: limit
props.doc: Token budget. The bar caps at 100%.

props.name: label
props.doc: Heading; also labels the progress bar for screen readers.

props.name: note
props.doc: Line under the bar, after the percentage.

examples: <TokenUsageMeter used={128400} limit={200000} note="Resets on the 1st" />

components.name: tool-call-card
components.title: ToolCallCard
components.description: One tool invocation inside an agent turn: tool name, argument preview, status pill, duration and a collapsible output.
components.whenToUse: Children are the output (plain text or `<pre>`); without children the header is static. Use `ToolCallCollapsed` for a minimal one-line disclosure, `ToolResultPanel` to show JSON output, and `AgentTrace` for a whole run.

props.name: name
props.doc: Tool or function name, shown in mono.

props.name: status
props.doc: "running" shows a spinner and hides the duration.

props.name: args
props.doc: Short argument preview, e.g. `path="DESIGN.md"`.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Wall time, e.g. "0.4s". Hidden while running.

props.name: children
props.doc: The output. Makes the card collapsible.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state for the uncontrolled card.

examples: <ToolCallCard name="get_invoice" args='id="INV-2041"' status="done" duration="0.3s">{JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}</ToolCallCard>

components.name: tool-call-collapsed
components.title: ToolCallCollapsed
components.description: A quiet one-line disclosure for a tool call: chevron and mono tool name, with the details hidden until opened.
components.whenToUse: Use it when tool calls should stay out of the way in a chat transcript. Use `ToolCallCard` when status and duration matter.

props.name: name
props.doc: Tool or function name, shown in mono.

props.name: children
props.doc: Details revealed when opened.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start open.

examples: <ToolCallCollapsed name="search_customers">Found 3 customers matching "northwind".</ToolCallCollapsed>

components.name: tool-result-panel
components.title: ToolResultPanel
components.description: A panel showing an AI tool call's name, a status badge and its output as highlighted JSON.
components.whenToUse: Pass `output` as a string or any JSON-serialisable value; objects are pretty-printed. Use `ToolCallCard` for a collapsible call inside a chat turn, and `JsonViewer` for large, foldable payloads.

props.name: name
props.doc: The tool that ran.

props.name: output
props.doc: Raw output: a string is shown as-is, anything else is JSON.stringified. Defaults to a Lumen invoice lookup.

examples: <ToolResultPanel name="lookup_invoice" status="success" output={{ invoice: "INV-2041", status: "paid" }} />

components.name: tooltip
components.title: Tooltip
