components.description: An ink label with an arrow that appears on hover and keyboard focus, built on Base UI.
components.whenToUse: Compose `Tooltip` > `TooltipTrigger` + `TooltipContent`; use `render` to make your own button the trigger. Wrap a toolbar in `TooltipProvider` so neighbouring tooltips open instantly. Tooltips are hints only: never put interactive content or the only copy of important text in one. Use `HoverCard` or `Popover` for rich or clickable content. `<Tooltip />` with no children renders a demo.
examples:
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Archive invoice" />}><ArchiveIcon /></TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent side="bottom">Archive <Kbd>E</Kbd></TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>

components.name: topbar
components.title: Topbar
components.description: A 56px app header bar with a title (or custom left content) and a right-hand slot for actions.
components.whenToUse: Renders a `<header>`. Use it at the top of an `AppShell` content area. Use `PageHeader` for a page title with description and actions inside the content, and `NavMarketing` for a marketing site nav.

props.name: title
props.doc: Page or section name, used when `left` is not given.

props.name: left
props.doc: Replaces the title, e.g. breadcrumbs or an org switcher.

props.name: right
props.doc: Actions on the right: search, buttons, avatar menu.

examples: <Topbar title="Invoices" right={<><SearchInput /><Button size="sm">New invoice</Button></>} />

components.name: trace-waterfall
components.title: TraceWaterfall
components.description: A distributed-trace waterfall: one row per span with its name (indented by depth), a bar placed on a shared time axis, and its duration.
components.whenToUse: Times are in milliseconds from the start of the trace. Use it for request traces and agent step timing. Use `GanttChart` for calendar schedules and `AgentTrace` for a step-by-step agent run.

props.name: spans
props.doc: Spans in display order. Defaults to a four-span API request.

examples: <TraceWaterfall spans={[{ name: "POST /invoices", start: 0, duration: 120 }, { name: "db.insert", start: 18, duration: 40, depth: 1 }]} />

components.name: tree-view
components.title: TreeView
components.description: A keyboard-navigable tree of nested nodes, all open by default, for file browsers, folders and org charts.
components.whenToUse: Follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: one tab stop, Up/Down move, Right opens or enters a branch, Left closes or goes to the parent, Home/End jump, Enter/Space selects (and toggles a branch). Use `FileTree` for files with icons and status, and `NestedNav` for sidebar navigation links.

props.name: nodes
props.doc: Root nodes. Defaults to the Lumen web app's source tree.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.doc: Branch ids open at first render. Omit to open every branch.

props.name: selectedId
props.doc: Controlled selected node id.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called when a node is clicked or chosen with Enter or Space.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the tree.

examples: <TreeView nodes={[{ id: "src", label: "src", children: [{ id: "app", label: "app.tsx" }] }]} onSelect={(node) => open(node.id)} aria-label="Project files" />

components.name: treemap-chart
components.title: TreemapChart
components.description: A squarified treemap. Groups get a header strip and their cells share one hue at falling strengths, labels appear only where they fit, and hovering or focusing a cell lifts it and shows its value and share in a tooltip. Cells are keyboard focusable with arrow keys; a hidden table carries the data.

props.name: data
props.doc: Top level items. A node with `children` renders as a group with a header strip.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading above the chart and the accessible name.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Shown next to the total.

props.name: height
props.doc: Chart height in px. The width follows the container.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats values in the tooltip, labels and table. Defaults to compact USD ("$48.2K").

props.name: valueLabel
props.doc: Name of the measure in the tooltip, e.g. "Revenue", "Storage", "Users".

props.name: minLabelSize
props.doc: Hide labels in cells narrower or shorter than this, in px.

components.name: trial-banner
components.title: TrialBanner
components.description: An accent-tinted banner counting down the days left in a free trial, with an upgrade button.
components.whenToUse: Place it above page content or in a settings sidebar. Use `UpgradePrompt` for a feature-gated card and `AnnouncementBar` for a site-wide strip.

props.name: daysLeft
props.doc: Days remaining. 0 reads "ends today".

props.name: plan
props.doc: Plan name in the heading.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting line under the heading.

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Button text.

props.name: onUpgrade
props.doc: Called when the upgrade button is pressed.

examples: <TrialBanner daysLeft={5} description="Invoice automations stay on until then." onUpgrade={() => router.push("/billing")} />

components.name: two-factor-setup
components.title: TwoFactorSetup
components.description: The enable-2FA step: a QR code slot, the manual setup key, a 6-digit code field and a verify button.
components.whenToUse: Render your QR (for example with `QrCode`) in `qr` and the base32 secret in `secret`. `onVerify` receives the code once all six digits are in. Use `TwoFactorVerify` for the sign-in challenge after 2FA is on.

props.name: qr
props.doc: The QR code for the authenticator app. Shows a placeholder when omitted.

props.name: secret
props.doc: Setup key for manual entry, shown in mono under the QR.

props.name: onVerify
props.doc: Called with the 6-digit code when the form is submitted.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Shows the field as invalid, e.g. after a wrong code.

examples: <TwoFactorSetup qr={<QrCode value={otpauthUrl} />} secret="JBSW Y3DP EHPK 3PXP" onVerify={(code) => enable2fa(code)} />

components.name: two-factor-verify
components.title: TwoFactorVerify
components.description: The sign-in 2FA challenge: a card with a 6-digit code field that submits itself when the last digit is typed.
components.whenToUse: `onVerify` receives the code. Set `invalid` after a wrong code to shake the field red. Use `TwoFactorSetup` to enrol a device, and `OtpInput` alone for other one-time codes.

props.name: onVerify
props.doc: Called with the 6-digit code on completion or submit.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Shows the field as invalid, e.g. after a wrong code.

props.name: description
props.doc: Line under the title.

examples: <TwoFactorVerify onVerify={async (code) => setInvalid(!(await verify(code)))} invalid={invalid} />

components.name: typing-indicator
components.title: TypingIndicator
components.description: Three pulsing dots in a pill that say someone (or the model) is typing; announced once to screen readers.
components.whenToUse: Render it while waiting for the first token of a reply, then swap in the message. Use `StreamingCursor` once text is arriving, and `Spinner` for non-chat loading.

props.name: label
props.doc: Screen-reader text, e.g. "Maya is typing".

examples: {isWaiting ? <TypingIndicator label="Lumen Assistant is typing" /> : null}

components.name: upgrade-prompt
components.title: UpgradePrompt
components.description: A small card that explains a locked feature and offers one upgrade button, for soft paywalls.
components.whenToUse: Show it in place of the gated feature. Use `TrialBanner` for a trial countdown, `PlanComparison` to choose between plans, and `DowngradeWarning` before a plan change.

props.name: description
props.default: "See 90 days ahead from your open inv...

props.name: actionLabel
props.doc: Button text.

props.name: onUpgrade
props.doc: Called when the upgrade button is pressed.

examples: <UpgradePrompt title="Forecasts are on Scale" description="See 90 days of cash flow from open invoices." onUpgrade={openBilling} />

components.name: uptime-bar
components.title: UptimeBar
components.description: A status-page uptime strip: one bar per day, red where there was downtime, with the uptime percentage.
components.whenToUse: `downtimes` holds zero-based day indexes counted from the oldest day. Use `HealthIndicator` for a single live status, and `IncidentBanner` to announce an ongoing outage.

props.name: label
props.doc: Service name.

props.name: days
props.doc: Number of days shown, oldest on the left.

props.name: downtimes
props.doc: Indexes (0 = oldest day) of days with downtime.

examples: <UptimeBar label="Payments API" days={90} downtimes={[12, 44]} />

components.name: usage-breakdown
components.title: UsageBreakdown
components.description: A stack of labelled usage bars, each showing used against limit, for plan and billing pages. Bars turn amber at 90% and red at the limit.
components.whenToUse: Use it to show several metered resources at once. Use `UsageMeter` for a single bar, `QuotaBar` for one quota with a legend, and `ResourceQuotaGrid` for many quotas as cards.

props.name: items
props.doc: One bar per metered resource. Defaults to a Lumen workspace's monthly usage.

examples: <UsageBreakdown items={[{ label: "Seats", used: 18, limit: 25 }, { label: "Storage (GB)", used: 38, limit: 50 }]} />

components.name: usage-meter
components.title: UsageMeter
components.description: One labelled usage bar with "used/limit" on the right, for seats, storage or API calls.
components.whenToUse: The bar caps at 100%. Use `UsageBreakdown` for several resources, `TokenUsageMeter` for an LLM token budget card, and `Meter` for a value in a known range that is not usage.

props.name: label
props.doc: Resource name; also labels the bar for screen readers.

examples: <UsageMeter label="Seats" used={18} limit={25} />

components.name: user-chip
components.title: UserChip
components.description: A pill with an avatar and a name, optionally removable, for assignee pickers and share lists.
components.whenToUse: Passing `onRemove` adds an "x" button labelled "Remove {name}". Use `AttachmentChip` for files, `ContextChip` for AI context items, and `AvatarGroup` for a compact stack of people.

props.name: name
props.doc: Display name. Also drives the initials fallback and the remove label.

props.name: src
props.doc: Avatar image; initials are used when absent.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Shows a remove button when provided.

examples: <UserChip name="Priya Raman" src="/avatars/priya.jpg" onRemove={() => unassign("priya")} />

components.name: version-badge
components.title: VersionBadge
components.description: A mono version tag ("v2.4.1") with an optional release-channel pill: stable, beta or canary.
components.whenToUse: Pass the version with or without a leading "v". Use `EnvBadge` for deploy environments and `Badge` for anything else.

props.name: version
props.doc: Semver string, e.g. "2.4.1" or "v2.4.1".

props.name: channel
props.doc: Release channel pill. Omit to hide.

examples: <VersionBadge version="2.4.1" channel="beta" />

components.name: vertical-tabs
components.title: VerticalTabs
components.description: A left-hand tab list with the active panel beside it, for settings pages; stacks above the panel on small screens.
components.whenToUse: Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: one tab stop, Up/Down (and Left/Right) move and select, Home/End jump. Use `Tabs` for horizontal tabs, `SettingsLayout` for a full settings page with routes, and `SegmentedControl` for switching a view in place.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: Tabs in order. Defaults to Lumen's workspace settings.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled selected tab id. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initially selected tab id for the uncontrolled tabs. Defaults to the first tab.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the newly selected tab.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the tab list.

examples: <VerticalTabs defaultValue="billing" tabs={[{ id: "general", label: "General", content: <GeneralForm /> }, { id: "billing", label: "Billing", content: <BillingForm /> }]} />

components.name: video-player-chrome
components.title: VideoPlayerChrome
components.description: Presentational video-player chrome: a 16:9 stage with a play/pause button and a bottom bar with progress and title.
components.whenToUse: It draws the controls only; wire `playing`, `onToggle` and `progress` to your `<video>` element, or put the video in `children`. Uncontrolled, the button just toggles its own state. Use `AudioPlayer` for audio.

props.name: title
props.doc: Shown in the bottom bar.

props.name: playing
props.doc: Controlled playing state. Pair with `onToggle`.

props.name: defaultPlaying
props.doc: Initial state for the uncontrolled player.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called with the next playing state when the button is pressed.

props.name: progress
props.doc: Playback position, 0–100.

props.name: children
props.doc: The media, e.g. a `<video>`; it fills the stage behind the button.

examples: <VideoPlayerChrome title="Q3 close walkthrough" playing={playing} onToggle={() => (playing ? ref.current.pause() : ref.current.play())} progress={pct}><video ref={ref} src="/q3.mp4" /></VideoPlayerChrome>

components.name: virtual-list
components.title: VirtualList
components.description: A windowed list. Only the rows inside the viewport (plus an overscan band) exist in the DOM, so ten thousand rows scroll like ten. Row heights are fixed or measured per row, arrow keys move an active row with Home, End and Page Up/Down, and a ref exposes scrollToIndex for deep links.

props.name: items
props.doc: Rows to render. Defaults to 10,000 Lumen invoices.

props.name: rowHeight
props.doc: Row height in px, or "auto" to measure every row (estimatedRowHeight is used until a row has been measured).

props.name: estimatedRowHeight
props.doc: Height assumed for rows that have not been measured yet, in "auto" mode.

props.name: overscan
props.doc: Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport so fast scrolling never shows a gap.

props.name: height
props.doc: Viewport height in px.

props.name: renderRow
props.type: (item: T, index: number, state: { active: boolean }) => React.ReactNode
props.doc: Renders one row. Defaults to an invoice row.

props.name: getKey
props.doc: Stable key per row. Defaults to item.id, then the index.

props.name: describeRow
props.doc: Plain text for the screen reader announcement of the active row.

props.name: activeIndex
props.doc: Controlled active row.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called on click, Enter or Space on a row.

props.name: title
props.doc: Header title. Pass an empty string to hide the header.

props.name: showJump
props.doc: Show the "Jump to row" field in the header.

props.name: showFooter
props.doc: Show the "Rows a to b of n" footer.

props.name: ref
props.doc: Imperative handle with scrollToIndex and setActiveIndex.

components.name: virtualized-list
components.title: VirtualizedList
components.description: A bare fixed-row-height windowed list that renders only the rows in view; ten thousand rows cost about twenty DOM nodes.
components.whenToUse: Pass `count`, `itemHeight` and `renderItem(index)`. Use `VirtualList` for a header, measured row heights, keyboard row navigation and scroll-to-index.

props.name: count
props.doc: Total number of rows.

props.name: itemHeight
props.doc: Height of every row, in px. Rows must not be taller.

props.name: height
props.doc: Viewport height, in px.

props.name: renderItem
props.doc: Renders the row at `index`. Defaults to a sample invoice row.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Accessible name for the scrollable list.

examples: <VirtualizedList count={rows.length} itemHeight={40} height={320} renderItem={(i) => <Row row={rows[i]} />} aria-label="Transactions" />

components.name: visually-hidden
components.title: VisuallyHidden
components.description: Text that screen readers announce but sighted users never see (Tailwind `sr-only`), e.g. a label for an icon-only control.
components.whenToUse: Accepts every `<span>` prop, so it can carry an `id` for `aria-describedby`. Prefer `aria-label` on the control when the text is short. Use `SkipLink` for a skip-to-content link that appears on focus.
examples: <button><TrashIcon aria-hidden /><VisuallyHidden>Delete invoice INV-2041</VisuallyHidden></button>

components.name: vote-control
components.title: VoteControl
components.description: A vertical up/down vote control with the score between, for feature boards and Q&A. Pressing the active arrow again clears the vote.
components.whenToUse: The arrows are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`). `score` is displayed as given, so include the viewer's vote in it. Use `FeedbackThumbs` for rating an AI answer and `ReactionBar` for emoji reactions.

props.name: score
props.doc: Net score to display, including the viewer's vote.

props.name: value
props.doc: Controlled vote. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial vote for the uncontrolled control.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new vote; null when cleared.

examples: <VoteControl score={score} value={vote} onChange={(v) => { setScore(score - delta(vote) + delta(v)); setVote(v) }} />

components.name: waffle-chart
components.title: WaffleChart
components.description: A 10-column grid of squares with the first `value` filled, for "42 of 100" style part-to-whole stats.
components.whenToUse: Keep `total` at 100 or less so each square stays countable. Use `ProgressCircle` or `GoalRing` for a single percentage and `PieChart` for several parts.

props.name: value
props.doc: Filled squares. Clamped to 0…total.

props.name: total
props.doc: Total squares, ten per row.

props.name: label
props.doc: Name of the stat; also the accessible name.

examples: <WaffleChart label="Invoices paid on time" value={42} total={100} />

components.name: webhook-list
components.title: WebhookList
components.description: A card listing webhook endpoints (URL, subscribed events, active or paused) with an "Add endpoint" button.
components.whenToUse: Use it on developer settings pages. Use `ApiKeyList` for API keys and `IntegrationCard` for third-party connections.

props.name: hooks
props.doc: Endpoints to list. Defaults to two Lumen endpoints.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: Called when "Add endpoint" is pressed.

examples: <WebhookList hooks={[{ url: "https://api.northwind.com/hooks/lumen", events: "invoice.paid, invoice.overdue", status: "active" }]} onAdd={openCreateDialog} />

components.name: welcome-screen
components.title: WelcomeScreen
components.description: A first-run welcome card: eyebrow, headline, one sentence, numbered next steps and two actions.
components.whenToUse: Show it on an empty dashboard after sign-up. Use `OnboardingChecklist` when the steps should tick off as they are done, `OnboardingWizard` for a guided multi-step flow, and `EmptyState` for an empty list.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small accent label above the headline.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Next steps, rendered as a numbered list.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons under the steps. Defaults to two sample buttons.

examples: <WelcomeScreen title="Welcome to Lumen, Maya" steps={["Connect your bank", "Invite your finance team", "Send your first invoice"]} actions={<Button>Connect bank</Button>} />

components.name: well
components.title: Well
components.description: A sunken, bordered box that sets content back from the page: notes, code samples, read-only summaries.
components.whenToUse: Accepts every `<div>` prop. Use `Card` for raised, primary content, `Callout` or `InlineAlert` for messages with a tone, and `Inset` for padding without a frame.
examples: <Well>Payouts land in your bank 2 business days after an invoice is paid.</Well>

components.name: window-chrome
components.title: WindowChrome
components.description: A neutral app-window frame (three grey dots and a title bar) for screenshots and product previews on marketing pages.
components.whenToUse: Children sit in 16px padding. Use `TerminalWindow` for CLI output and `CodeEditorFrame` for source code.

props.name: title
props.doc: Title bar text.

examples: <WindowChrome title="Lumen — Invoices"><InvoiceList /></WindowChrome>

components.name: wishlist-button
components.title: WishlistButton
components.description: A heart toggle button for saving a product to a wishlist; the heart fills when active.
components.whenToUse: It is a toggle (`aria-pressed`) with a fixed label, so screen readers hear "Save to wishlist, pressed". Works controlled (`active` + `onToggle`) or uncontrolled (`defaultActive`). Use `Toggle` for generic toolbar toggles.

props.name: active
props.doc: Controlled state. Pair with `onToggle`.

props.name: defaultActive
props.doc: Initial state for the uncontrolled button.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called with the next state when pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name. Keep it the same in both states; `aria-pressed` conveys the state.

examples: <WishlistButton active={saved} onToggle={setSaved} label="Save Aurora desk lamp" />

components.name: workspace-create
components.title: WorkspaceCreate
components.description: A create-workspace form: name (required) and URL slug, which follows the name until edited, plus a submit button.
components.whenToUse: `onCreate` gets `{ name, slug }` on submit; Enter submits. Use `JoinWorkspace` to join an existing one and `OrgSwitcher` to move between workspaces.

props.name: onCreate
props.doc: Called on submit with the trimmed name and the slug.

props.name: pending
props.doc: Disables the button and shows it busy while the workspace is created.

examples: <WorkspaceCreate onCreate={({ name, slug }) => createWorkspace(name, slug)} />

components.name: admin-console
components.title: AdminConsole
components.description: A workspace admin area: impersonation banner, org switcher, KPIs, then tabs for users, security, quotas and import.
components.whenToUse: Use as the full admin screen of a B2B app. Every panel is a registry component (AdminUserRow, AuditFilterBar, SsoProviderCard, IpAllowlist, ResourceQuotaGrid, BulkUserImport), so drop tabs you do not need. For a lighter landing page use AdminOverview; for a searchable member table use UsersTablePage.
examples: <AdminConsole />

components.name: admin-overview
components.title: AdminOverview
components.description: An admin landing page: title with "Invite admin", four org KPIs with deltas, then recent admin activity.
components.whenToUse: Use as the first screen of an admin area. For the full tabbed admin (users, SSO, quotas, import) use AdminConsole; for product metrics with charts use AnalyticsPage. Composes AdminStatStrip and ActivityFeed.

props.name: onInvite
props.doc: Called by the "Invite admin" button.

examples: <AdminOverview onInvite={() => setInviteOpen(true)} />

components.name: analytics-page
components.title: AnalyticsPage
components.description: A metrics page: four KPIs with deltas, a hoverable revenue trend and a signups bar chart.
components.whenToUse: Use for a product or revenue analytics screen with a few headline charts. For the app home with activity use DashboardHome; to let people build their own chart use ReportBuilder. Charts carry text summaries for screen readers and stack on small screens.
examples: <AnalyticsPage />

components.name: api-docs-page
components.title: ApiDocsPage
components.description: An API reference page: section nav, base URL with a copy button, the endpoint list, and a curl sample.
components.whenToUse: Use for REST reference docs. Each endpoint shows its method, path and one-line purpose. For prose guides with a table of contents use DocsPage; for an in-app API key screen use ApiKeyList. The nav collapses above the content on small screens.
examples: <ApiDocsPage />

components.name: bento-live
components.title: BentoLive
components.description: A product feature grid where every tile runs a small live piece of the product (a ticking metric, a typed answer, alerts) instead of a screenshot.
components.whenToUse: Use as the main "features" section of a landing page, with 4–6 tiles on a 6-column grid. Live tiles only tick while on screen and sit still under reduced motion. Tiles rise in once as the grid enters view and lift on hover. For a text-only grid use FeatureGrid; for a premium animated bento use FeatureBentoMotion.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Section heading (rendered as h2).

props.name: items
props.doc: Tiles in order. Defaults to five live Lumen tiles.

examples: <BentoLive items={[{ title: "Live MRR", body: "Every metric is live.", visual: <MyChart />, span: 4, tall: true }]} />

components.name: billing-page
components.title: BillingPage
components.description: A subscription page: plan cards with the current plan highlighted, seat usage, then recent invoices.
components.whenToUse: Use inside an app's settings for an existing customer. For a public pricing section with a monthly/yearly switch use PricingPlans; for paying for a cart use CommerceCheckout. Composes PlanCard, UsageMeter and InvoiceList.

props.name: onChangePlan
props.doc: Called with the plan name when a plan's button is pressed.

examples: <BillingPage onChangePlan={(plan) => openCheckout(plan)} />

components.name: changelog-page
components.title: ChangelogPage
components.description: A release-notes list: one entry per version with date, tag, title and a short body, newest first.
components.whenToUse: Use for a public /changelog or an in-app "What's new" panel. Each entry is an article with a real <time>, so feeds and search engines can read it. For a marketing changelog with motion use the premium ChangelogMarketing; for docs use DocsPage.
examples: <ChangelogPage />

components.name: chat-page
components.title: ChatPage
components.description: A full-height AI chat screen: titled header, a scrolling transcript that follows new messages, and a composer.
components.whenToUse: Use for an assistant or support chat that owns the page. Sent messages append to the thread; wire `onSend` to your model and push its reply into your own state when you copy the block. For just the transcript use ChatThread; for a composer with attachments and model picker use AiComposer. Give the block a height.

props.name: onSend
props.doc: Called with the trimmed text each time the user sends a message.

examples: <ChatPage className="h-[600px]" onSend={(text) => ask(text)} />

components.name: command-center
components.title: CommandCenter
components.description: An ops home: page title with a "Commands" button (also ⌘K / Ctrl+K), a KPI row, and a command dialog.
components.whenToUse: Use for an operator dashboard where the fastest path to any action is the keyboard. For a chart-led overview use DashboardHome; for just the palette use CommandPalette (has its own ⌘K) or CommandDialog. The shortcut listener is attached to the window while the block is mounted.
examples: <CommandCenter />

components.name: commerce-checkout
components.title: CommerceCheckout
components.description: A two-column checkout: line items and billing address on the left, a live order summary and Pay on the right.
components.whenToUse: Use for a one-page checkout of a few items or seats. Totals recompute as quantity changes. On small screens the summary stacks under the form. For plan selection before checkout use PricingPlans; for an existing subscription use BillingPage.

props.name: onPay
props.doc: Called by "Pay" with the total in cents.

examples: <CommerceCheckout onPay={(total) => createPaymentIntent(total)} />

components.name: cta-band
components.title: CtaBand
components.description: The closing call to action of a landing page: a big lit panel, a headline that catches the light, and an email field whose button morphs into a confirmation.
components.whenToUse: Use as the last section before the footer when the ask is "leave your email". For a plain row with one button use CtaBanner; for a premium glow panel use CtaGlow. `onSubmit` may return a promise: the button shows "Sending…" until it settles, "Check your inbox" on success, and an error line if it throws. Result is announced to screen readers.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline (rendered as h2). Wrap a phrase in `<span className="text-lit">` to make it catch the light.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences under the headline.
props.default: "Connect a source and get your first ...

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Email input placeholder.

props.name: button
props.doc: Submit button label at rest.

props.name: success
props.doc: Button label after a successful submit.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the email on submit. Return a promise to show the busy state; throw to show the error line.

props.name: note
props.doc: Small print under the form.

examples: <CtaBand title="Ship it this week." onSubmit={(email) => fetch("/api/waitlist", { method: "POST", body: email })} />

components.name: dashboard-home
components.title: DashboardHome
components.description: An app home: page title with a primary action, four KPIs with deltas, a revenue chart and recent activity.
components.whenToUse: Use as the first screen after sign-in. For a metrics-only page with more charts use AnalyticsPage; for an ops home driven by ⌘K use CommandCenter. Composes PageHeader, KpiRow, ChartCard, BarChart and ActivityFeed; the chart and feed stack on small screens.
examples: <DashboardHome />

components.name: device-frame
components.title: DeviceFrame
components.description: A phone or a browser window around live UI, with a lit bezel edge and a glass sheen that follow the light.
components.whenToUse: Use in heroes, feature rows and scroll stories to show real product UI instead of a screenshot. The phone is a fixed 300×630px frame (scale it with a transform class); the browser fills its container width. Children render inside the screen and stay interactive. For a static image use a plain ; for several overlapping devices use the premium DeviceStack.

props.name: device
props.doc: Which frame to draw.

props.name: url
props.doc: Address bar text (browser only). Not a link.

props.name: time
props.doc: Status bar time (phone only).

props.name: children
props.doc: The UI shown on the screen. Defaults to a placeholder.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the outer frame, e.g. a scale transform.

props.name: screenClassName
props.doc: Classes for the screen area that holds `children`.

examples:
<DeviceFrame device="browser" url="app.lumen.io/revenue"><DashboardHome /></DeviceFrame>
<DeviceFrame device="phone" time="09:41"><NotificationCenter /></DeviceFrame>

components.name: docs-page
components.title: DocsPage
components.description: A documentation article: a sticky table of contents beside prose, code samples and a callout.
components.whenToUse: Use for guides and how-tos. Every Toc entry points at a heading id in the article. For endpoint reference with methods and a curl sample use ApiDocsPage; for release notes use ChangelogPage. On small screens the Toc stacks above the article.
examples: <DocsPage />

components.name: empty-workspace
components.title: EmptyWorkspace
components.description: The first-run screen of a new workspace: page title, an empty state with one primary action, then two shortcuts.
components.whenToUse: Use when a list or workspace has no data yet and the next step is obvious. For an empty search result use EmptySearch; for a multi-step first-run setup use OnboardingFlow. Composes PageHeader and EmptyState.

props.name: onCreate
props.doc: Called by the primary "New report" button.

examples: <EmptyWorkspace onCreate={() => router.push("/projects/new")} />

components.name: engineering-console
components.title: EngineeringConsole
components.description: A dev-ops page: environment switch, the build pipeline, then tabs for commits, checks, trace and review.
components.whenToUse: Use as the engineering home of an internal tool or a developer product. Every panel is a registry component (BuildPipeline, CommitRow, CheckRunList, TraceWaterfall, ReviewRequestCard, MergeBox), so drop tabs you do not need. For workspace administration use AdminConsole; for raw log lines use LogsViewer.

props.name: defaultEnv
props.doc: Environment selected on first render.

examples: <EngineeringConsole defaultEnv="staging" />

components.name: faq-section
components.title: FaqSection
components.description: A landing-page FAQ: a heading column with a contact line beside a one-open-at-a-time accordion.
components.whenToUse: Use near the end of a marketing page, before the closing CTA. Answers open by animating grid rows (no measuring) and the plus turns into a cross. Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: Enter/Space toggles, Arrow Up/Down move between questions, Home/End jump to the first/last. Closed answers are inert. For an in-app collapsible list use Accordion.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Section heading (rendered as h2).

props.name: description
props.doc: Line under the heading, e.g. how to reach a person.
props.default: "Something else on your mind? Write t...

props.name: items
props.doc: Questions in order. Defaults to Lumen's FAQ.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Index of the question open on first render; `null` starts all closed.

examples: <FaqSection items={[{ q: "Do you store our data?", a: "Only aggregates, encrypted at rest." }]} />

components.name: feature-flags
components.title: FeatureFlags
components.description: An admin page of named flags, each a row with a description and a switch, plus a live "n of m on" count.
components.whenToUse: Use for workspace-level flags, betas and experiments. For a single flag row use FeatureFlagToggle; for per-channel notification switches use NotificationPreferences. State lives in the block; wire `onChange` to persist each flip.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the flag name and its new state after every flip.

examples: <FeatureFlags onChange={(flag, on) => api.flags.set(flag, on)} />

components.name: floating-nav
components.title: FloatingNav
components.description: A sticky marketing header that tucks into a floating raised pill once you scroll, with a hover highlight that glides between links.
components.whenToUse: Use at the top of a landing page, above HeroSpotlight. It tracks window scroll. Below md the links move into a menu sheet: the toggle has aria-expanded/aria-controls, Escape closes it and returns focus, and choosing a link closes it. For an app shell with a sidebar use Topbar or Sidebar; for in-page section tabs use Tabs.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Logo or wordmark at the left. Defaults to the Lumen wordmark.

props.name: brandHref
props.doc: Where the brand links to.

props.name: links
props.doc: Primary navigation links.

props.name: cta
props.type: { label: string; href?: string; onClick?: () => void }
props.doc: Solid button at the right. Renders as a link when `href` is set.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: Ghost link before the CTA, hidden on the smallest screens. Pass null to remove it.

examples: <FloatingNav links={[{ label: "Pricing", href: "#pricing" }]} cta={{ label: "Start free", href: "/signup" }} />

components.name: form-wizard
components.title: FormWizard
components.description: A multi-step form: a stepper, one group of fields per step, Back/Next, a review step and a done state.
components.whenToUse: Use when a form is long enough to split (connect a data source, create an account). Each step validates with the browser's own `required` checks before moving on, and focus moves to the new step's heading so screen readers hear where they are. For a first-run checklist with progress use OnboardingFlow; for one short form use FormField.

props.name: onComplete
props.doc: Called with every field's value when the review step is submitted.

examples: <FormWizard onComplete={(v) => api.sources.create(v)} />

components.name: hero-spotlight
components.title: HeroSpotlight
components.description: A launch hero: a staggered h1 that settles in with a blur, a lit second line, two actions, a proof line and a product visual that rises last.
components.whenToUse: Use as the first section of a landing page (it renders the page's h1, so use it once). Pair `visual` with a DeviceFrame wrapping real UI. Entrance motion is skipped under reduced motion. For a plain hero with no motion use Hero; for premium backgrounds use HeroAurora. Actions render as links when `href` is set, buttons otherwise.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Pill above the title with a live dot, e.g. "Now in public beta".

props.name: title
props.doc: First line of the h1.

props.name: highlight
props.doc: Second line of the title, lit by the cursor.

props.name: description
props.doc: Paragraph under the title.

props.name: primary
props.doc: Main call to action, solid with an arrow.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: Second call to action, outline.

props.name: proof
props.doc: Small proof line under the actions.
props.default: "Free for 14 days · No card · SOC 2 T...

props.name: visual
props.doc: Product visual (a DeviceFrame, a screenshot, anything).

props.name: align
props.doc: Text alignment of the copy block.

examples:
<HeroSpotlight
  title="Answers from your data,"
  highlight="before you ask."
  primary={{ label: "Start free", href: "/signup" }}
  visual={<DeviceFrame device="browser"><DashboardHome /></DeviceFrame>}
/>

components.name: inbox-page
components.title: InboxPage
components.description: A two-pane inbox: a message list with unread dots on the left, the open message on the right (stacked on mobile).
components.whenToUse: Use for in-app messages, digests or system mail. Opening a message marks it read; "Mark all read" clears the rest and the unread count is announced. For support tickets with SLA and status use SupportInbox; for short notifications use NotificationCenter.
examples: <InboxPage />

components.name: logs-viewer
components.title: LogsViewer
components.description: A log panel: text filter and level switch over a scrollable, monospaced list of timestamped lines.
components.whenToUse: Use for job, sync or request logs inside an ops screen. Filtering is client-side over the lines you pass in; for streaming or server-side search, filter upstream and keep the markup. For a structured audit trail use AuditLogEntry; for build steps use BuildPipeline.
examples: <LogsViewer className="h-96" />

components.name: marketing-landing
components.title: MarketingLanding
components.description: A plain, fast landing page from free sections: hero, logo cloud, stats, feature grid and a CTA banner.
components.whenToUse: Use for a simple product or docs home with no motion budget. For a richer launch page use HeroSpotlight, BentoLive, PricingPlans, FaqSection and CtaBand together; for premium motion use PremiumLanding or SaasMarketingPage. Logos, stats and features fall back to each section's Lumen sample data, which is fictional: replace it with your own.

props.name: onStart
props.doc: Called by the hero's primary button and the closing banner's button.

examples: <MarketingLanding onStart={() => router.push("/signup")} />

components.name: media-library
components.title: MediaLibrary
components.description: A files panel: title with an Upload button that opens the system file picker, then a responsive grid of file rows.
components.whenToUse: Use for attachments, exports or brand assets shared by a workspace. Picked files are added to the top of the list (no network); wire `onUpload` to send them. For drag-and-drop with progress use FileDropzone; for a single file use FileRow; for a folder hierarchy use FileTree.

props.name: onUpload
props.doc: Called with the files the user picked.

props.name: accept
props.doc: Same syntax as <input accept>, e.g. "image/*,.pdf".

examples: <MediaLibrary onUpload={(files) => uploadAll(files)} />

components.name: notification-center
components.title: NotificationCenter
components.description: A notifications panel: a titled header with an unread count and "Mark all read", then the latest rows.
components.whenToUse: Use as the body of a bell popover or a side panel in an app shell. For one row use NotificationItem; for a bell button that opens its own popover use NotificationInbox; for a team audit trail use ActivityFeed. Ships with Lumen sample notifications; copy the block and swap `SAMPLE` for your data.
examples: <NotificationCenter className="max-w-md" />

components.name: onboarding-flow
components.title: OnboardingFlow
components.description: A first-run setup card: progress, one short question per step (workspace, team, digest), Back/Continue, then Finish.
components.whenToUse: Use right after sign-up to collect the three things the product needs. Steps validate with `required` before moving on. For a long, multi-field form use FormWizard; for an empty screen with one action use EmptyWorkspace.

props.name: onFinish
props.doc: Called with the answers when the last step is submitted.

examples: <OnboardingFlow onFinish={(v) => api.workspace.create(v)} />

components.name: premium-landing
components.title: PremiumLanding
components.description: A short premium launch page: aurora hero, animated feature row, motion pricing and a glowing CTA.
components.whenToUse: Use for a product launch or waitlist page that should feel alive. For a full SaaS home with logos, compare and quotes use SaasMarketingPage; for the free-tier equivalent use MarketingLanding. Every section falls back to its own Lumen sample copy; pass props to the sections to change it.
examples: <PremiumLanding />

components.name: pricing-plans
components.title: PricingPlans
components.description: A public pricing section: a monthly/yearly switch whose prices roll digit by digit, a featured plan in ink, and plain yes/no feature rows.
components.whenToUse: Use on a marketing or /pricing page with two to four plans. Prices are numbers per month; the yearly figure is the monthly-equivalent price and the "Billed $X yearly" line is derived. A price of 0 reads "Free". For an existing customer's plan and invoices use BillingPage; for a premium animated variant use PricingMotion. Period is uncontrolled by default; pass `period` + `onPeriodChange` to control it.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Section heading (rendered as h2).
props.default: "Priced like a tool, not a hire."

props.name: description
props.default: "Per seat, per month. Change plans an...

props.name: plans
props.doc: Plans in display order. Defaults to Lumen's Starter, Team and Scale.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code used to format prices, e.g. "USD", "EUR".

props.name: yearlyBadge
props.doc: Discount badge on the yearly option.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the plan name and the selected period when a plan's button is pressed.

props.name: period
props.doc: Controlled billing period.

props.name: defaultPeriod
props.doc: Initial billing period when uncontrolled.

props.name: onPeriodChange
props.doc: Called when the period switch changes.

props.name: unit
props.doc: Price suffix, e.g. "/ seat / mo" or "/ mo".

props.name: per
props.doc: Used in "Billed $X per seat yearly". Empty string drops it.

examples:
<PricingPlans
  plans={[{ name: "Team", blurb: "For finance teams", monthly: 49, yearly: 39, cta: "Start trial", featured: true, features: ["Unlimited workspaces"] }]}
  onSelect={(plan, period) => router.push(`/signup?plan=${plan}&period=${period}`)}
/>

components.name: project-detail
components.title: ProjectDetail
components.description: A record page: back link, title with status and actions, a facts list, then recent activity.
components.whenToUse: Use for any "one item" screen (a project, customer, invoice) reached from a list. For the list itself use ProjectList; for a person use UserDetail. Composes PageHeader, DescriptionList and ActivityFeed; swap the sample Lumen board-pack data for your record.
examples: <ProjectDetail />

components.name: project-list
components.title: ProjectList
components.description: An index page: title with "New project", then one linked row per project with owner, freshness and status.
components.whenToUse: Use for short lists (under ~30 items) where each row opens a detail page (see ProjectDetail). For sortable, selectable or long lists use UsersTablePage / DataTable. Rows are real links, so they work with the keyboard, middle-click and screen readers.
examples: <ProjectList />

components.name: report-builder
components.title: ReportBuilder
components.description: A report editor page: title with Export, a date range, a metric switch and a live chart preview.
components.whenToUse: Use when people assemble a saved report from a metric and a period. For a read-only dashboard use DashboardHome or AnalyticsPage. Composes DateRangePicker, SegmentedControl, ChartCard and BarChart.

props.name: onExport
props.type: (report: { metric: ReportMetric; range: { from?: string; to?: string } }) => void
props.doc: Called by "Export CSV" with the selected metric and date range (ISO yyyy-mm-dd strings).

examples: <ReportBuilder onExport={({ metric, range }) => downloadCsv(metric, range)} />

components.name: saas-marketing-page
components.title: SaasMarketingPage
components.description: A premium SaaS home page stacked from motion sections: pitch hero, logo wall, bento, compare, quotes, CTA.
components.whenToUse: Use as a starting point for a pitch or launch page built from premium sections. For the free-tier equivalent use MarketingLanding; for a lighter premium page use PremiumLanding. Each section is its own registry component, so remove or reorder lines freely. The sample logos and quotes are fictional; replace them with your own.
examples: <SaasMarketingPage />

components.name: scroll-story
components.title: ScrollStory
components.description: A "how it works" section: numbered steps on one side, a pinned visual on the other that swaps as each step reaches mid-screen, with a filling progress rail.
components.whenToUse: Use for a 3–5 step explanation on a landing page. On large screens the visual is sticky; below lg each step shows its own visual inline, so nothing is lost on mobile. Each `visual` should be a compact panel (a DeviceFrame scaled down, a card). Swaps are instant under reduced motion. For a static grid of features use BentoLive.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Section heading (rendered as h2).

props.name: steps
props.doc: Steps in order. Defaults to Lumen's connect, learn, tell story.

examples: <ScrollStory steps={[{ kicker: "01 · Connect", title: "Point it at your tools.", body: "Read-only keys.", visual: <MyPanel /> }]} />

components.name: search-results-page
components.title: SearchResultsPage
components.description: A search screen: a search field, a live result count, and linked results grouped by type with the match highlighted.
components.whenToUse: Use for an in-app search across records (customers, invoices, reports). Results filter as you type and the count is announced to screen readers. For a dropdown of results under a field use SearchWithResults; for a ⌘K launcher use CommandPalette; for "nothing found" art use EmptySearch.

props.name: defaultQuery
props.doc: Starting query.

examples: <SearchResultsPage defaultQuery="northwind" />

components.name: settings-page
components.title: SettingsPage
components.description: An account settings page: profile form, theme picker, notification channels and a danger zone, in that order.
components.whenToUse: Use for a single-column personal or workspace settings screen. For admin-only controls (users, SSO, quotas) use AdminConsole; for billing use BillingPage. Each section is a registry component, so drop the ones you do not need. The theme picker applies to the whole document by default.
examples: <SettingsPage className="max-w-2xl" />

components.name: sign-in-page
components.title: SignInPage
components.description: A centred sign-in screen: GitHub and Google buttons, an "or" divider, then email and password in a real form.
components.whenToUse: Use as the whole /sign-in route. Fields carry `autoComplete` so password managers fill them, and Enter submits. For just the card use AuthCard; for one-time codes use OtpInput. Wire `onSubmit` to your auth call.

props.name: onSubmit
props.type: (values: { email: string; password: string }) => void | Promise<void>
props.doc: Called with the entered credentials when the form is submitted.

examples: <SignInPage onSubmit={({ email, password }) => signIn(email, password)} />

components.name: social-proof-wall
components.title: SocialProofWall
components.description: A customer section: a logo marquee that fades at the edges, then a wall of quotes in up to three columns drifting at different speeds.
components.whenToUse: Use once on a landing page, after the product sections. Motion pauses on hover and with the "Pause motion" button (WCAG 2.2.2), and stops entirely under reduced motion; duplicated copies used for the loop are hidden from screen readers. The default logos and quotes are fictional samples: always pass your own real customers. For a single featured quote use a Testimonial; for a static logo row use LogoCloud.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small mono label above the title. Empty string hides it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Section heading (rendered as h2).

props.name: logos
props.doc: Company names for the marquee, rendered as text wordmarks.

props.name: quotes
props.doc: Quotes, distributed round-robin into three columns.

examples: <SocialProofWall logos={["Acme", "Globex"]} quotes={[{ quote: "Closed the books in two days.", name: "Jane Doe", role: "CFO, Acme" }]} />

components.name: status-page
components.title: StatusPage
components.description: A public status page: an overall verdict derived from every service, then each service with its health and 90-day uptime.
components.whenToUse: Use for status.yourapp.com or an in-app "System status" panel. The headline badge is computed from the worst service, so it never disagrees with the list. For a single live dot use HealthIndicator; for an outage notice across the app use IncidentBanner.
examples: <StatusPage />

components.name: support-inbox
components.title: SupportInbox
components.description: A ticket queue: open count and SLA risk in the header, search, then linked tickets with status and time left.
components.whenToUse: Use for a helpdesk or customer-success queue. Tickets under two hours to SLA are flagged. Search matches subject, id or sender. For personal messages use InboxPage; for in-app notifications use NotificationCenter.

props.name: onCompose
props.doc: Called by the Compose button.

examples: <SupportInbox onCompose={() => setComposeOpen(true)} />

components.name: user-detail
components.title: UserDetail
components.description: One person's admin page: back link, avatar and name as the title, account facts, then their recent activity.
components.whenToUse: Use as the target of a row in UsersTablePage or AdminConsole. For a non-person record use ProjectDetail; for a single member row inside a list use TeamMemberRow. Swap the sample Lumen user for your data.
examples: <UserDetail />

components.name: users-table-page
components.title: UsersTablePage
components.description: A members page: title with Invite, a search toolbar, and a sortable table of people with role and status.

Use it for integration and pipeline diagrams; for a lit box outline use BorderBeam instead. Reduced motion keeps the static path and drops the light.

components.name: animated-list
components.title: AnimatedList
components.description: A live activity feed where new items drop in at the top on a spring and older ones slide down and fall off the end.
components.whenToUse: Use it for "happening now" sections, notification previews and activity streams on marketing pages. Items cycle through `items` on a timer while the list is on screen, and pause while the pointer or keyboard focus is on it. Reduced motion shows the first `max` items, still. For a static list of notifications use a plain list; for a one-off reveal use BlurFade.

props.name: items
props.doc: Items to cycle through, newest first.

props.name: interval
props.doc: Milliseconds between arrivals.

props.name: max
props.doc: How many items to keep on screen.

components.name: animated-tabs
components.title: AnimatedTabs
components.description: Tabs with a pill that slides between triggers and panels that cross-fade in the direction of travel.
components.whenToUse: Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: roving focus, Arrow keys, Home and End, automatic activation. Pass `tabs` as data (id, label, content). Works uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`). Use it for a marketing or overview panel with a few views; for app navigation tabs built from parts use Tabs, and for a compact toggle between options use SegmentedControl.

components.name: animated-tooltip
components.title: AnimatedTooltip
components.description: A row of overlapping avatars where hovering or focusing one pops up a name and role card that leans and slides with the pointer.
components.whenToUse: The card rises on a spring, tilts a few degrees toward the pointer as it crosses the face, and settles back when it leaves. Keyboard focus opens the same card centred; Escape closes it; a tap toggles it on touch. Reduced motion shows and hides the card instantly with no tilt. Use it for team, contributor or "who's online" rows; for a tooltip on any trigger use Tooltip, and for a plain stacked row use AvatarGroup.

props.name: people
props.doc: People to show, left to right. Defaults to a five-person sample team.

props.name: size

components.name: aurora-background
components.title: AuroraBackground
components.description: Soft northern-lights curtains that drift and sway across the panel behind your content. Three blurred bands of accent colour move at different periods, so the motion never reads as a loop. The light sits behind the content, ignores the pointer, pauses off screen and holds still for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it as a hero or CTA backdrop; children render on top. For a static glow use HeroGradientMesh, for a pointer-reactive grid use BackgroundBoxes.

props.name: intensity
props.doc: Strength of the light, 0 to 1.

props.name: speed
props.doc: Speed multiplier. 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast.

props.name: blur
props.doc: Softness of the bands in pixels.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colours of the bands. Any CSS colour, including var(--token).

examples: See your runway in a new light

components.name: background-boxes
components.title: BackgroundBoxes
components.description: A skewed grid of hairline boxes behind your content where the box under the pointer lights up in colour and fades out behind it. One pointer handler maps the cursor into the skewed grid with a little matrix maths and writes the colour straight to the box, so React never re-renders a box. Neighbours catch a softer glow. It works through the content on top and with touch. Left alone, a box lights now and then so the panel looks alive; that idle flicker pauses off screen and stops for reduced motion, and the fade is instant for reduced motion too.
components.whenToUse: Use it as an interactive hero backdrop; children render on top. For quiet ambient motion use FlickeringGrid or AuroraBackground instead.

props.name: density
props.doc: Box density. 1 draws 64px boxes, 2 draws them half the size.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colours the boxes light up in. Any CSS colour, including var(--token).

props.name: fade
props.doc: Seconds a lit box takes to fade back.

props.name: idle
props.doc: Boxes that light on their own each second while nobody hovers. 0 turns the idle flicker off.

props.name: skew
props.doc: Tilt of the grid in degrees: skew along x, then along y.

examples: Built on a grid you can feel

components.name: before-after-wipe
components.title: BeforeAfterWipe
components.description: A before and after comparison: drag the divider (or use the arrow keys) to wipe between two layers.
components.whenToUse: The divider is a real range input under the hood, so it is keyboard and screen reader operable (Arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up/Down). Pass any content as `before` and `after` (screenshots, mockups, two renders of a component); with neither it shows a sample dashboard. Works uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`). Use it for redesigns, filters and "with vs without" proof; for flipping between more than two states use AnimatedTabs.

props.name: before
props.doc: Content of the left (before) layer.

props.name: after
props.doc: Content of the right (after) layer, revealed as the divider moves left.

props.name: beforeLabel
props.doc: Name of the before layer, shown on the sample and read to screen readers.

props.name: afterLabel
props.doc: Name of the after layer.

props.name: value
props.doc: Divider position in percent (0 shows only after, 100 only before) when controlled.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial divider position in percent when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new divider position in percent.

examples: } after={} />

props.name: title
props.doc: Page heading (the only h1).

components.name: blur-fade
components.title: BlurFade
components.description: Reveals its children as they scroll into view, rising out of a soft blur and settling into focus on a spring. Wrap each item of a list and grow the `delay` to stagger them. Reduced motion shows everything in place at once.
components.whenToUse: Use it for scroll reveals of cards, sections and images on marketing pages. Product UI should not animate on load (law 5), so keep it out of app chrome. With no children it renders a sample grid of six feature cards.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Seconds to wait before the reveal starts; grow it per item to stagger a list.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds the reveal takes.

props.name: direction
props.doc: Which way the content travels as it settles.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Pixels of travel.

props.name: blur
props.doc: Blur in pixels the content starts from.

props.name: once
props.doc: Reveal once, or again every time it enters the viewport.

props.name: amount
props.doc: How much of the element has to be visible before it reveals, 0 to 1.

components.name: border-beam
components.title: BorderBeam
components.description: A short beam of light that travels around the border of any box to mark the one thing that matters.
components.whenToUse: Wrap a card, input or pricing tier with it. The beam is a rotating conic gradient masked to the border ring, so the content inside is untouched; it animates transform only and holds still for reduced motion. Set `radius` to match the child's corner radius. For light flowing between elements use AnimatedBeam; for a static highlight use a `border-accent` ring.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds per lap.

props.name: width
props.doc: Border width in pixels.

props.name: length
props.doc: Beam length, as a fraction of the lap, 0 to 1.

props.name: radius
props.doc: Corner radius in pixels; match the wrapped element.

examples:
<BorderBeam radius={12} duration={8}>
  <Card className="w-80">…</Card>
</BorderBeam>

components.name: brand-kit-page
components.title: BrandKitPage

components.name: browser-mockup
components.title: BrowserMockup
components.description: A browser window frame with traffic lights, back and forward buttons, an address bar and optional tabs, wrapping your screenshot or any children. PhoneMockup, exported from the same file, is the matching handset with a dynamic island and rounded screen. Both are built from tokens, so they follow light, dark and every material. With no content, the browser shows a Lumen dashboard made of plain divs, with a phone over its corner on wide screens and below it on narrow ones.
components.whenToUse: Use it to frame product screenshots on landing pages, docs and changelogs. For several tilted frames at once use DeviceFrameStack.

props.name: url

props.name: tabs

props.name: activeTab

props.name: src

props.name: appearance
props.doc: Stay dark in both themes, or follow the page theme.

props.name: phone
props.doc: Render a PhoneMockup beside the window. Defaults to on for the built-in sample only.

<PhoneMockup width={260}><MyMobileScreen /></PhoneMockup>

components.name: card-tilt
components.title: CardTilt
components.description: A card that tilts in 3D toward a mouse pointer, with an accent glare that follows it.
components.whenToUse: Tilt and glare run on motion values, so moving the pointer never re-renders React. Mouse only: touch and keyboard see a flat card, and reduced motion keeps it flat too. Pass `children` for your own content, or `title` and `body` for the built-in layout. Use it for a featured card or showcase tile on marketing pages; for a flat spotlight panel use CursorSpotlightPanel, and keep it out of product UI.

props.name: body

components.title: CommandWaitlist
components.description: A terminal-styled waitlist card with a monospace email field and a Join button that springs into view as it scrolls on screen.
components.whenToUse: Handles its own pending, success and error states and announces them to screen readers. Use it for a launch or beta waitlist; for a newsletter row in a footer use a plain Input and Button.

props.name: onSubmit

components.name: confetti-button
components.title: ConfettiButton
components.description: A button that bursts confetti from itself on click, for celebrating a finished action.
components.whenToUse: A few dozen paper pieces with gravity, drag and spin are drawn on a throwaway canvas and cleaned up when they land; physics are time based, so 60 and 120Hz screens fall at the same speed. No library. Reduced motion skips the burst and keeps the click. It takes every native button prop. Use it for "you did it" moments (first invoice sent, plan upgraded), not for routine saves; for a normal action use Button.

props.name: count
props.doc: Number of pieces per burst.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Piece colours, any CSS colour. Defaults to the accent, accent-2, success, warning and info tokens.

components.name: light-field
components.title: LightField
components.description: A living WebGL background of slow colour silk with a soft light that follows the cursor and fine film grain. Warped noise drifts slowly, the cursor carries a soft light through it, and fine grain keeps it from looking digital. It starts when the browser is idle, compiles its shader off the main thread where the GPU allows, renders at half resolution and 30 fps, fades in on its first frame, sleeps when off screen or in a background tab, stays empty without a real GPU (put a still behind it), and draws a single still frame for reduced motion. Glass surfaces placed over it frost it beautifully.
components.whenToUse: It fills its parent: put it in a sized, `relative` box with your content layered above. Reach for AuroraBackground or HeroGradientMesh for a CSS-only backdrop, and WavyBackground or Particles for a lighter canvas effect.

props.doc: Frames per second. The silk drifts slowly, so 30 looks the same as 60 for half the GPU work.

props.name: resolution
props.doc: Render scale in CSS pixels. The field is soft, so 0.5 (scaled up by the browser) is indistinguishable from full size.
