components.title: OnboardingMotion
components.description: A short onboarding card that slides between steps, with a segmented progress bar you can click, Back and Continue, and a magnetic finish button. Each step slides in on the morph spring and leaves faster than it came. The progress segments are real buttons with `aria-current="step"`, and the step text is announced politely as it changes. Reduced motion swaps steps instantly.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a three-to-five step welcome on a marketing or signup page. Reach for the free OnboardingWizard for multi-step forms inside a product, OnboardingChecklist for a task list, and ProductTour to walk through features beside a preview.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Steps in order.

props.name: finishLabel
props.doc: Label of the button on the last step.

props.name: onFinish
props.doc: Called when the finish button is pressed.

examples:
<OnboardingMotion
  steps={[{ title: "Connect your bank", body: "Transactions sync every hour." }, { title: "Send an invoice", body: "Numbering and reminders are handled." }]}
  finishLabel="Open Lumen"
  onFinish={() => router.push("/app")}
/>

components.name: orbit-logo-cluster
components.title: OrbitLogoCluster
components.description: A ring of logo or name pills slowly orbiting a centre badge, each pill staying upright as it travels. The orbit is a pair of CSS transform loops (the ring turns, each pill turns back), so it runs on the compositor and costs nothing on the main thread. It pauses while the pointer is over it and holds still for reduced motion. Screen readers get the names as a plain list.
components.whenToUse: Use it for "connects with" or partner sections with text names. Reach for OrbitingCircles for icons on several rings, and LogoWallMotion for a scrolling strip. Pass real partners: never invent logos.

props.name: center
props.doc: Content of the centre badge: your mark or a short name.

props.name: logos
props.doc: Names or logo elements on the ring. Elements need their own accessible name.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds for one full orbit.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name for the list of logos.

examples: <OrbitLogoCluster center="Lumen" logos={["Stripe", "Plaid", "Xero", "QuickBooks"]} duration={48} />

components.name: orbiting-circles
components.title: OrbitingCircles
components.description: Icons orbiting a centre on hairline rings, each ring at its own speed and direction, for integration sections. Icons orbiting a centre on hairline rings, for "works with everything" integration sections. Each ring sets its own radius, speed and direction; icons stay upright as they travel. Static for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it for an integrations or "works with your stack" section. Reach for OrbitLogoCluster for text logos on one ring, IconCloud for a 3D sphere of icons, and AnimatedBeam to show data flowing between named tools.

props.name: size
props.doc: Box size in pixels.

examples: <OrbitingCircles size={320} rings={[{ radius: 80, duration: 20, icons: [MailIcon, DatabaseIcon] }]} center={<Logo />} />

components.name: parallax-panel
components.title: ParallaxPanel
components.description: A sunken panel whose text and soft accent glow drift at different speeds as the page scrolls, giving the section depth. Both layers move with transforms tied straight to scroll position, so nothing lays out again and nothing lags. Reduced motion holds both still.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a quiet feature or manifesto section between busier ones. Reach for ScrollReveal to bring any block in once, StickyFeatureStory for a pinned multi-step story, and TiltCard for depth under the pointer instead.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small label above the title.

props.name: depth
props.doc: Pixels the text travels across the full scroll through the panel.

examples: <ParallaxPanel eyebrow="Reconciliation" title="Every payment, matched" body="Lumen pairs deposits with invoices as they land." />

components.name: particles
components.title: Particles
components.description: A canvas particle field that drifts behind your content and parts around the pointer, or gathers toward it. Colour comes from the accent token and follows theme and material changes. The canvas is sharp on high density screens, resizes with its box, sleeps off screen and in background tabs, and draws one still frame for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it behind a hero or CTA panel that should feel alive under the pointer. Reach for Meteors for streaks, LightField for a soft WebGL glow, and DotPattern or FlickeringGrid for a static or barely moving texture.

props.name: quantity
props.doc: Number of particles.

props.name: size
props.doc: Radius of the nearest particles in pixels. Farther ones are smaller.

props.name: color
props.doc: Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the accent.

props.name: mode
props.doc: Push particles away from the pointer, or pull them toward it.

props.name: radius
props.doc: Reach of the pointer in pixels.

props.name: drift
props.doc: Drift speed multiplier. 0 holds the field still apart from the pointer.

examples: Every invoice, accounted for

components.name: pin-scroll-gallery
components.title: PinScrollGallery
components.description: A gallery that pins to the viewport and slides its frames sideways as you scroll down, then releases. The section is as tall as the frames need; vertical scroll drives a horizontal transform, so nothing lays out again while it moves. Reduced motion shows the frames as a plain grid instead of hijacking the scroll.
components.whenToUse: Use it for three to five big product moments on a launch page. Reach for HorizontalProductRail for a rail the visitor scrolls themselves, StickyFeatureStory for pinned steps beside one preview, and ScrollChapterStory for stacked chapters.

props.name: frames
props.doc: Frames in order. Each takes the full width of the pinned stage.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small label above every frame title.

examples: <PinScrollGallery frames={[{ title: "Send", body: "Invoices go out on schedule." }, { title: "Match", body: "Payments pair with invoices." }]} />

components.name: pricing-kinetic
components.title: PricingKinetic
components.description: A complete kinetic pricing section: headline, typographic marquee, a price that rolls between monthly and yearly, a comparison table and a magnetic upgrade button. It composes MorphPrice, TypographicMarquee, FeatureComparison and MagneticCta, so each piece keeps its own accessibility and reduced-motion behaviour. Copy the file and edit the content in place; it is a page section, not a configurable widget.
components.whenToUse: Use it as the pricing section of a launch page. Reach for PricingPage for a whole page with nav and footer, PricingMotion for plan cards alone, and the free PricingTable inside product billing.
examples: <PricingKinetic className="py-16" />

components.name: pricing-motion
components.title: PricingMotion
components.description: Pricing tiers that rise into view one after another as they scroll in. Each card rises on the morph spring with a short stagger, once. The featured plan gets the accent border, a "Most popular" badge and the solid button. Reduced motion shows every card in place.
components.whenToUse: Use it for two to four plans on a marketing page. Reach for MorphPrice for one plan with a Monthly / Yearly roll, PricingKinetic or PricingPage for a full section, and the free PricingTable or PlanCard inside billing screens.

props.name: plans
props.doc: Plans in display order.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the plan whose button was pressed.

examples:
<PricingMotion
  plans={[{ name: "Pro", price: "$49", period: "/ month", blurb: "For finance teams", featured: true, features: ["Unlimited invoices"] }]}
  onSelect={(plan) => router.push(`/signup?plan=${plan.name}`)}
/>

components.name: pricing-page
components.title: PricingPage
components.description: A full pricing page kit: marketing nav, Monthly / Yearly toggle, three plan cards, a feature comparison, FAQ, a closing CTA and a mega footer. The toggle drives the featured plan's price. Every section is a kit component with its own keyboard and reduced-motion behaviour. Copy the file and replace the sample plans, rows and questions with yours.
components.whenToUse: Use it as a starting point for /pricing. Reach for PricingKinetic for just the pricing section, PricingMotion for the plan cards, and the free PricingTable or PlanComparison inside a product.
examples: <PricingPage />

components.name: product-launch
components.title: ProductLaunch
components.description: A full product launch page kit: scroll progress rail, kinetic hero with device frames, product rail, sticky feature story, before/after wipe, stats, quotes, spotlight panel, countdown and waitlist. Every section is a separate Premium component, so you can delete or reorder sections freely. Copy the file and swap the sample copy and figures for your own; never ship invented stats or quotes.
components.whenToUse: Use it as the skeleton of a launch or "coming soon" page. Reach for SaasLanding for an evergreen home page, PricingPage for /pricing, and the individual sections when you only need one.
examples: <ProductLaunch />

components.name: product-os-mock
components.title: ProductOsMock
components.description: A mock product window with a sidebar of workspaces that cycles on its own, each view rising in with its rows and KPI bars. It auto-advances every few seconds to show the product breathing, pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside, and stops for good once the visitor picks a view. Reduced motion never auto-advances and shows every view in place.
components.whenToUse: Use it as a hero visual for a product or platform page. Reach for BrowserMockup or DeviceFrameStack to frame your own screenshot, and ProductTour for a guided, visitor-driven walkthrough.

props.name: interval
props.doc: Milliseconds each view stays before the next.

examples: <ProductOsMock interval={3200} />

components.name: product-tour
components.title: ProductTour
components.description: A step list beside a stage that fades to the selected step, with Back and Next. The list items are buttons marked `aria-current="step"`; the stage rises in on the morph spring and is announced politely as it changes. Optional `media` per step fills the stage. Reduced motion swaps steps instantly.
components.whenToUse: Use it to walk visitors through four or five features in order. Reach for OnboardingMotion for a compact welcome card, StickyFeatureStory when scroll should drive the steps, and the free OnboardingWizard for real forms.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Steps in order.

props.name: onStepChange
props.doc: Called with the index of the step the visitor moves to.

examples: }]} />

components.name: retro-grid
components.title: RetroGrid
components.description: A retro perspective grid floor that recedes to a glowing horizon and scrolls slowly toward you. Lines are tinted with the accent and fade out before they reach the horizon, so they never shimmer. The floor sits behind the content, ignores the pointer, pauses off screen and holds still for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it behind a launch, deploy or developer-tool hero. Reach for DotPattern or BackgroundBoxes for a flat grid, and LampEffect when the headline should be lit rather than grounded.

props.name: angle
props.doc: Tilt of the floor in degrees. Higher is flatter and longer.

props.name: cellSize
props.doc: Size of one grid cell in pixels, at the front of the floor.

props.name: speed
props.doc: Cells per second travelled toward the viewer.

props.name: horizon
props.doc: Where the floor meets the sky, as a percent of the height from the top.

examples: Every release, right on schedule

components.name: ripple
components.title: Ripple
components.description: Concentric rings behind your content with a soft pulse that travels outward ring by ring, like a sonar ping. Clicking or tapping the panel sends an extra ripple out from the pointer. The rings sit behind the content, pause off screen and hold still for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it behind a "live", "listening" or "connected" message. Reach for OrbitingCircles to show integrations around a centre, and Meteors or Particles for a looser, less centred backdrop.

props.name: count
props.doc: Number of rings.

props.name: spacing
props.doc: Gap between neighbouring rings in pixels.

props.name: size
props.doc: Diameter of the innermost ring in pixels.

props.name: origin
props.doc: Centre of the rings, in percent of the panel width and height.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds for one pulse to travel out and settle.

props.name: interactive
props.doc: Send a ripple out from the pointer on click or tap.

examples: Lumen hears every payment

components.name: saas-landing
components.title: SaasLanding
components.description: A complete SaaS landing page kit: aurora hero, moving logo wall, stats, feature row, pricing cards, testimonial carousel, FAQ and a glowing CTA. Every section is a separate kit component with its own accessibility and reduced-motion handling, so you can delete or reorder sections freely. Copy the file and replace the sample copy, logos and figures with your own; never ship invented customers, stats or testimonials.
components.whenToUse: Use it as the home page of a SaaS product. Reach for ProductLaunch for a launch or waitlist page, and PricingPage for /pricing.
examples: <SaasLanding />

components.name: scratch-to-reveal
components.title: ScratchToReveal
components.description: A scratch card: a foil you rub away with the pointer or a finger to reveal what is underneath, which clears itself once enough is gone. The foil is a canvas painted with a gradient from your tokens. Progress is tracked on a coarse grid, so there is no pixel reading on every move. Past the threshold the rest lifts away on its own and onComplete fires. A Reveal button serves keyboard users, and reduced motion skips the fade.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a playful reward, promo code or launch teaser. Reach for SecretReveal to show a sensitive value behind a click, and BeforeAfterWipe to compare two images.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: Percent of the foil that must be scratched before the rest clears itself.

props.name: brush
props.doc: Brush radius in pixels.

props.name: gradient
props.doc: Colours of the foil gradient. CSS colours and var(--token) both work.

props.name: label
props.doc: Hint printed on the foil.

props.name: onComplete
props.doc: Called once the card is fully revealed.

props.name: onProgress
props.doc: Called with the scratched percentage as it changes.

examples:
track("reward_revealed")}>

20% off Lumen Pro

components.name: scroll-chapter-story
components.title: ScrollChapterStory
components.description: A long-form story told in numbered chapters that rise in as you reach them, under a sticky progress bar that fills with your reading. The progress bar is a scaleX transform tied straight to scroll, so it never lays out again. Each chapter rises once on the morph spring. Reduced motion shows chapters in place and the bar still tracks progress, without motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a narrative "how it works" or manifesto section. Reach for StickyFeatureStory for steps beside one pinned preview, TracingBeam for a changelog-style timeline, and ScrollProgress for a page-wide reading bar.

props.name: chapters
props.doc: Chapters in order.

examples: <ScrollChapterStory chapters={[{ kicker: "01 · Send", title: "Invoices go out on time.", body: "Schedules and reminders are automatic." }]} />

components.name: scroll-progress-rail
components.title: ScrollProgressRail
components.description: A sticky top rail with a thin bar that fills as the page scrolls and a row of section labels underneath. The bar is a scaleX transform smoothed by the release spring, so it glides with the scroll; reduced motion tracks the scroll exactly. Labels are plain text by default, or pass `href`s to make them in-page links.
components.whenToUse: Use it at the top of a long launch or story page. Reach for ScrollProgress for a bare bar or a percent ring, and the free TableOfContents for a full side navigation that highlights the current section.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Section labels, left to right. Strings render as text; `{ label, href }` renders a link.

examples: <ScrollProgressRail labels={[{ label: "Intro", href: "#intro" }, { label: "Pricing", href: "#pricing" }]} />

components.name: scroll-progress
components.title: ScrollProgress
components.description: Reading progress as a thin bar that fills along the top edge and a ring with the percent inside, for the page or any scrollable element. Pin it to the viewport with `fixed`, point it at a scroller with `container`, or give it children and it becomes its own scrolling panel. The spring gives the bar a little weight as you scroll; reduced motion tracks the scroll position exactly.
components.whenToUse: Use it on long articles, docs and changelogs. Reach for ScrollProgressRail for a sticky rail with section labels, and the free Progress for task progress that is not tied to scrolling.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Which indicators to show.

props.name: container
props.doc: A scrollable element to track instead of the window. The indicators render where you put them, inside a `relative` wrapper.

props.name: fixed
props.doc: Pin the indicators to the viewport and track the page (or `container`). Nothing else renders.

props.name: height
props.doc: Bar thickness in pixels.

props.name: size
props.doc: Ring diameter in pixels.

props.name: children
props.doc: Without `fixed` or `container`, the component scrolls this content in its own panel.

props.name: title
props.doc: Panel header title.

props.name: subtitle
props.doc: Panel header line under the title.

examples:
<ScrollProgress fixed variant="bar" />
<ScrollProgress variant="both" title="Release notes">{longContent}</ScrollProgress>

components.name: scroll-reveal
components.title: ScrollReveal
components.description: A wrapper that lifts any block into place on a spring the first time it scrolls into view. Only transform moves, so the content is visible and readable from the first paint (no hidden text for search engines or screen readers) and nothing lays out again. It plays once; reduced motion shows the block in place.
components.whenToUse: Use it on marketing sections that should arrive as you reach them; stagger siblings with `delay`. Reach for BlurFade for a blur-and-fade entrance, TextReveal for word-by-word paragraphs, and nothing at all inside product UI, where content should simply be there.

props.name: y
props.doc: Pixels the block rises from.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Seconds to wait after it enters view. Use small steps (0.06 to 0.1) to stagger siblings.

examples:
<ScrollReveal delay={0.08}>
  <FeatureCard />
</ScrollReveal>

components.name: shimmer-button
components.title: ShimmerButton
components.description: A call-to-action button with a slow band of light sweeping across its face, a lit top edge and a soft bloom. A call to action with a slow band of light that sweeps across the face, a lit top edge and a soft bloom underneath. The sweep pauses for reduced motion. Renders a button, or pass `render` to make it a link.
components.whenToUse: Use it for the single most important action on a marketing page. Reach for Button in product UI, MagneticCta when the action should move toward the pointer, and BorderBeam or ShineBorder to light a whole card.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds for one sweep.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Ink is the kit's primary action; accent spends the brand violet.

props.name: size
props.doc: 40px (default) or 48px (lg) tall.

props.name: render
props.doc: Render as another element, e.g. <a href="/signup" /> or a router Link. Props and handlers are passed through.

examples:
<ShimmerButton tone="accent" onClick={startTrial}>Start free trial</ShimmerButton>
<ShimmerButton render={<a href="/signup" />}>Get started</ShimmerButton>

components.name: shine-border
components.title: ShineBorder
components.description: A card whose border is a band of coloured light sweeping around it, masked to the border ring so the content is untouched. A conic gradient of your colours turns on a registered CSS angle behind a mask that keeps only the ring, so it stays crisp at any radius. It holds still for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it to single out one card: a featured plan, a new release, an invite. Reach for BorderBeam for a short travelling beam instead of a band, and CtaGlow for a whole glowing call-to-action section.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colours in the band, in order. Any CSS colour; tokens like var(--accent) work.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds per lap.

props.name: borderWidth
props.doc: Border width in pixels.

props.name: radius
props.doc: Corner radius in pixels.

examples: Lumen Pro

components.name: soft-stack
components.title: SoftStack
components.description: A small stack of cards that fan up into a tidy, receding pile on a spring when it scrolls into view. Each card sits a little lower and smaller than the one in front, so the pile reads as depth without blurred shadows. It plays once; reduced motion shows the settled pile.
components.whenToUse: Use it as a light visual beside feature copy ("your workspaces", "every account"). Reach for StackRevealStory for readable stacked cards with body text, and DeviceFrameStack for stacked screenshots.

props.name: items
props.doc: Card titles, front to back. Three or four read best.

examples: <SoftStack items={["Payroll", "Invoices", "Expenses"]} />

components.name: sparkles-text
components.title: SparklesText
components.description: Text with small four-point stars that twinkle in and out around it at random. Text with small four point stars that twinkle around it, placed at random and replaced as they fade. The stars are decorative and hidden from assistive tech; the text stays a normal text node.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one short celebratory word or phrase. Reach for GradientText for a still accent and ConfettiButton for a one-off burst on success.

props.name: children
props.doc: The text that sparkles. Stays a plain text node for search and screen readers.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many stars are alive at once.

examples: <SparklesText count={10}>Paid in full</SparklesText>

components.name: split-proof-panel
components.title: SplitProofPanel
components.description: A two-column proof section: a pitch with a checklist and a call to action on one side, a stack of short proof cards rising in on the other. The proof column rises once on the morph spring; reduced motion shows it in place. Copy the file and replace the sample pitch and proof points with real, checkable ones.
components.whenToUse: Use it to back a claim right after a hero ("built to survive a client tab share"). Reach for FreePremiumCompare for a side-by-side tier comparison, and MetricTickerBoard when the proof is numbers.
examples: <SplitProofPanel />

components.name: stack-reveal-story
components.title: StackRevealStory
components.description: Numbered cards that rise on a spring and overlap into a stack on wider screens, telling a short three-step story. From md up each card tucks under the one before it; on phones they sit as a plain list so nothing overlaps text. Each card plays once; reduced motion shows the stack in place.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a compact "how it works" in three beats. Reach for SoftStack for a purely visual pile, ScrollChapterStory for full-width chapters, and StickyFeatureStory for pinned steps beside a preview.

props.name: cards
props.doc: Cards in order; each is numbered 01, 02, 03…

examples: <StackRevealStory cards={[{ title: "Connect", body: "Link your bank once." }, { title: "Send", body: "Invoices go out on time." }]} />

components.name: stats-counter
components.title: StatsCounter
components.description: A single stat whose digits roll up from zero, odometer style, when it scrolls into view, for stats sections. The digits spring into place with the roll preset rather than counting through every value. Screen readers and search engines get the final value as plain text from the first paint; reduced motion shows it straight away.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one figure in a row of stats. Reach for MetricTickerBoard for a ready-made board of several, and NumberRoll for a live value that changes.

props.name: value
props.doc: The final value. Use a real figure: never invent stats.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the number counts, shown under it.

props.name: suffix
props.doc: Text after the number, like "%" or "+".

props.name: format
props.doc: Intl.NumberFormat options, e.g. { style: "currency", currency: "USD" }.

components.name: status-marketing
components.title: StatusMarketing
components.description: A status page section: incident banner, operational badge, a gradient headline that wipes in, and a grid of uptime bars per service. It composes the free IncidentBanner, StatusBadge and UptimeBar with MaskedGradientHeadline, so the data components stay accessible and the motion stays to one headline wipe and one rise. Copy the file and feed it your real services and downtime days.
components.whenToUse: Use it on a public status or reliability page. Reach for UptimeBar alone inside product UI, and HealthIndicator for one service's state.
examples: <StatusMarketing />

components.name: sticky-cta-bar
components.title: StickyCtaBar
components.description: A floating call-to-action bar that springs up from the bottom of the screen once the visitor has scrolled past the hero, and tucks away again at the top. While hidden it is inert, so keyboard and screen-reader users never land on buttons they cannot see. It moves on the snappy spring; reduced motion shows and hides it instantly.
components.whenToUse: Use it on long marketing pages where the hero CTA scrolls away. Reach for the free StickyBar or PublishBar for in-product action bars, and AnnouncementBar for a message pinned to the top.

props.name: title
props.doc: Message on the left of the bar.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: Pixels scrolled from the top before the bar appears.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Your buttons or links. Defaults to a sample Docs + Get started pair.

examples: <StickyCtaBar title="Close your books in a day" threshold={480} actions={<Button render={<a href="/signup" />}>Start free</Button>} />

components.name: sticky-feature-story
components.title: StickyFeatureStory
components.description: A pinned two-column story: as you scroll, each step on the left lights up in turn while a mock preview on the right follows along. The section is as tall as its steps need and works for any number of them. The active step nudges into place on the snappy spring and is marked `aria-current="step"`. Reduced motion drops the pinning and shows every step as a plain list.
components.whenToUse: Use it to explain three to five features in order on a launch page. Reach for ScrollChapterStory for full-width chapters, PinScrollGallery for big sideways frames, and ProductTour when the visitor should click through.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Steps in order.

examples: <StickyFeatureStory steps={[{ label: "01", title: "Connect", body: "Link your bank once." }, { label: "02", title: "Reconcile", body: "Payments match themselves." }]} />

components.name: terminal
components.title: Terminal
components.description: An animated terminal window that types each command and prints its output line by line, with a blinking cursor and a replay button. Five line kinds (command, output, success, error, info) each get their own token colour and glyph. Typing pauses while the window is off screen and picks up where it left off; reduced motion prints the whole transcript at once. The box reserves its full height, so nothing below it shifts.
components.whenToUse: Use it to show an install command or CLI flow on a docs or launch page. Reach for the free TerminalWindow for a static transcript, CodeBlock for copyable code, and ConsoleOutput for streaming logs inside product UI.

props.name: prompt
props.doc: Prompt printed before each command.

props.name: typingSpeed
props.doc: Milliseconds per typed character.

props.name: lineDelay
props.doc: Milliseconds before each output line prints.

props.name: commandDelay
props.doc: Milliseconds before a command starts typing.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Start over after the last line, with a pause.

props.name: replay
props.doc: Show the replay button in the title bar.

props.name: appearance
props.doc: Stay dark in both themes, or follow the page theme.

props.name: onComplete
props.doc: Called once the last line has printed.

examples: <Terminal title="zsh" lines={[{ kind: "command", text: "npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.minidev.pro/r/button.json" }, { kind: "success", text: "Created 1 file" }]} />

components.name: testimonial-carousel
components.title: TestimonialCarousel
components.description: One large customer quote at a time that rotates on its own, with dot and Previous / Next controls. It follows the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern: a labelled region, slide buttons with `aria-current`, rotation that pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside and stops once the visitor takes control, and a polite announcement only when the visitor changes the slide. Quotes rise on the morph spring and leave faster; reduced motion never auto-rotates.
components.whenToUse: Use it for three to six longer testimonials. Reach for MarqueeQuotes for many short quotes at once, and the free Testimonial or PressQuote for a single static quote. Use real customer words: never invent testimonials.

props.name: interval
props.doc: Milliseconds each quote stays while auto-rotating. 0 turns rotation off.

props.name: label
props.doc: Accessible name of the carousel region.

examples: <TestimonialCarousel interval={6000} items={[{ quote: "Month-end close went from four days to one.", name: "Maya Patel", role: "Controller, Northwind" }]} />

components.name: text-reveal
components.title: TextReveal
components.description: A paragraph that lights up word by word, from muted to full ink, as it scrolls through the viewport. A paragraph that lights up word by word as it scrolls through the viewport, from muted to full ink. The words are real text in order, so search engines and screen readers read it normally.
components.whenToUse: Use it for one manifesto or mission paragraph on a long page. Reach for MaskedGradientHeadline for a headline wipe, and BlurFade or ScrollReveal to bring whole blocks in.
examples: <TextReveal text="Lumen closes the books so your team can open the next quarter." />

components.name: text-scramble
components.title: TextScramble
components.description: A short monospace line that decodes from random glyphs into the real text, left to right, the first time it scrolls into view. The real text is in the page from the first paint and is what screen readers and search engines read; the scrambled glyphs are hidden from them. Monospace keeps the width steady while it decodes. It plays once; reduced motion shows the text straight away.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a short label, eyebrow or code-flavoured headline (two or three words). Reach for HyperText for a scramble on hover, TypingText for a typewriter, and WordRotate or MorphingText for cycling phrases.

props.name: text
props.doc: The final text. Short, uppercase lines decode best.

props.name: glyphs
props.doc: Characters drawn while decoding.

examples: <TextScramble text="RECONCILED" />

components.name: tilt-card
components.title: TiltCard
components.description: A card that tilts toward the pointer in 3D, with a sliding glare and parallax children, and springs flat when the pointer leaves. The glare moves across the face like light on a foil print. Children marked `data-depth` float at their own parallax rate. Touch scrolls straight through it; reduced motion keeps it flat.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a showcase card, a pricing hero or a product shot. Reach for CardTilt for a simpler tilt without glare or depth, and ShineBorder to draw the eye without motion.

props.name: maxTilt
props.doc: Maximum rotation in degrees on either axis.

props.name: glare
props.doc: Glare strength from 0 (off) to 1.

props.name: perspective
props.doc: Perspective distance in pixels; smaller is more dramatic.

props.name: parallax
props.doc: Pixels of travel for a child with `data-depth="1"`; scale the number for more or less.

examples: Lumen Pro

components.name: tracing-beam
components.title: TracingBeam
components.description: A vertical beam beside long content that grows as you scroll, with a glowing tip and a node that lights for each entry. The beam is an SVG path driven by scroll progress through the section and smoothed with a spring, so it glides rather than jumps. Each direct child of the content gets a node on the track that fills the moment the beam passes it. Reduced motion drops the spring and follows the scroll exactly.
components.whenToUse: Use it for changelogs, timelines and long step-by-step stories. Reach for the free Timeline for a static list, and StickyFeatureStory or ScrollChapterStory for full-screen scroll chapters.

props.name: items
props.doc: Entries to trace. Each one gets a node on the beam.

props.name: children
props.doc: Your own content in place of the entries. Each direct child gets a node.

props.name: color
props.doc: Beam colour. Any CSS colour, including var(--token). Defaults to the accent.

props.name: rail
props.doc: Width of the rail the beam runs in, in pixels.

examples: <TracingBeam items={[{ version: "v3.2", date: "14 Oct 2026", title: "Auto-reconcile", body: "…" }]} />

components.name: typing-text
components.title: TypingText
components.description: A typewriter line that types a phrase, holds, deletes it and moves to the next, with a blinking caret. A typewriter that types a phrase, holds, deletes and moves to the next, with a blinking caret. Starts when it scrolls into view, and screen readers get the phrases as plain text instead of the keystrokes.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a short hero line that types a few phrases. Reach for WordRotate to swap one word in a sentence, MorphingText for a softer melt, and HeroTypedHeadline for a complete typed hero.

props.name: speed
props.doc: Milliseconds per typed character.

props.name: hold
props.doc: Milliseconds to hold a finished phrase.

examples: <TypingText phrases={["Send the invoice.", "Get paid on time."]} speed={50} />

components.name: typographic-marquee
components.title: TypographicMarquee
components.description: Big display phrases separated by accent dots, scrolling endlessly across a band, for a bold typographic break between sections. The band loops on the compositor (a CSS transform), pauses while the pointer is over it, and holds still for reduced motion. Screen readers read the phrases once; the looping copy is hidden from them.
components.whenToUse: Use it as a loud divider or a list of selling points. Reach for LogoWallMotion for logos, MarqueeQuotes for testimonials, and the free Marquee for a small, quiet ticker.

props.name: phrases
props.doc: Phrases in order. Keep them short: two or three words each.

props.name: text
props.doc: Deprecated.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds for one full loop. Higher is calmer.

examples: <TypographicMarquee phrases={["Bank sync", "Auto reminders", "One-click close"]} duration={24} />

components.name: waitlist-hero
components.title: WaitlistHero
components.description: A "coming soon" hero with a breathing accent glow, a one-field email form that handles loading, success and error, and a social-proof row. `onSubmit` may return a promise: the button shows progress, success replaces the form with a confirmation, and a thrown error keeps the typed email and shows the message. Results are announced to screen readers. The glow holds still for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a pre-launch page or a gated beta. Reach for CommandWaitlist for a command-palette styled signup, the free NewsletterSignup for a small inline form, and LaunchCountdown to add a clock.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the email. Return a promise to show progress; throw to show an error.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Small label above the title.

props.name: description
props.default: "Be first to the motion pack, landing...

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: Submit button label.

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: Shown in place of the form after a successful submit.
props.default: "You are on the list. We will email y...

props.name: proof
props.doc: Social proof under the form. Defaults to a sample avatar row; pass null to hide it. Never invent numbers.

examples:
<WaitlistHero
  title="Lumen 3.0 is almost here"
  onSubmit={async (email) => { await fetch("/api/waitlist", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ email }) }) }}
  proof={null}
/>

components.name: waveform-hero
components.title: WaveformHero
components.description: A hero with a headline over a row of thin accent bars that rise and fall like a live audio waveform, and a magnetic call to action. The bars breathe with compositor-only CSS transforms, each at its own pace, pause while off screen, and hold still for reduced motion. The waveform is decorative and hidden from screen readers.
components.whenToUse: Use it for audio, voice, AI-call or "live" products. Reach for WavyBackground for soft rolling waves behind any hero, and the free AudioPlayer when the waveform must reflect real audio.

props.name: cta
props.doc: Label of the call to action. Pass null to hide it.

props.name: bars
props.doc: Number of bars.

examples: <WaveformHero title="Every call, transcribed" description="Lumen listens to supplier calls and logs every promise to pay." cta="Try it free" />

components.name: wavy-background
components.title: WavyBackground
components.description: Layered canvas waves that roll across the bottom of the panel behind your content, each at its own pace. Every wave is two sine harmonics with its own phase, so the layers breathe against each other instead of marching in step. Colours resolve through the cascade, so var(--accent) follows theme and material changes. The canvas is sharp on high density screens, resizes with its box, sleeps off screen and in background tabs, and draws one still frame for reduced motion.
components.whenToUse: Use it behind a hero, footer or sign-up panel. Reach for AuroraBackground for a CSS-only gradient, LightField for a WebGL glow, and Meteors or Particles for small moving points.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colours of the waves, back to front. Any CSS colour, including var(--token).

props.name: speed
props.doc: Speed multiplier. 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast.

props.name: amplitude
props.doc: Height of the swell in pixels.

props.name: blur
props.doc: Softness in pixels. 0 draws crisp edges.

props.name: coverage
props.doc: Share of the panel the waves rise to, from the bottom, 0 to 1.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: Opacity of each wave, 0 to 1.

examples: Cash flow, smoothed out

components.name: word-rotate
components.title: WordRotate
components.description: A sentence with one word that rotates through a list in place, lifting and blurring out as the next rises in. The slot holds every word invisibly, so it is always as wide as the widest one and the sentence around it never jumps. The new word arrives on the morph spring and the old one leaves faster than it came. It pauses off screen, shows the first word for reduced motion, and screen readers hear the full list once.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a hero line like "Interfaces for <rotating word>". Reach for MorphingText to cycle whole phrases, TypingText for a typewriter, and HyperText or TextScramble for a one-off decode.

props.name: words
props.doc: Words to cycle through, in order.

props.name: interval
props.doc: Milliseconds each word stays.

props.name: prefix
props.doc: Text before the rotating word.

examples: <WordRotate prefix="Invoicing for" words={["agencies", "studios", "consultants"]} interval={2400} />
